A congruence identity relates this complement to the extended state-space description, which allows us to extend the AG formulas to general bianisotropic media and to establish the conditions of their validity in the presence of dissipation. The AG dispersive corrections are thus the imprints of the eliminated degrees of freedom rather than independent constitutive postulates. They hold for fields driven at arbitrary real frequency and wave vector, and not only for eigenmodes, provided that the sources act on the fields alone and that any dissipation is carried by the electromagnetic subsystem. We verify the construction on the Lorentz, Drude, magnetized-plasma, and hydrodynamic models, the last of which describes a nonlocal metal. Additionally, a bianisotropic omega-medium and a capacitively loaded wire medium are treated in the Supplemental Material.

items.title: Ultralow-Energy Measurements using the Startpoint of $β$ Decays
items.summary: We propose a novel measurement of $β$ decays using low-temperature solid-state detector technologies. The $β$ startpoint, where the $β$ kinetic energy is zero, offers a unique probe of weak nuclear physics that has not yet been exploited experimentally. We describe how this technique enables searches for heavy sterile neutrinos in the keV--MeV energy range and show that, with current technologies, sensitivities to sterile neutrino coupling to electrons can be achieved that exceed the current best constraints. The spectrum produced by the recoiling daughter ion also offers a calibration of the nuclear recoil response, critical for both sub-GeV dark matter searches and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) measurements. We outline a potential experimental scheme using neutron activation to produce $^{32}$P in situ in a silicon substrate, discuss projected sensitivities to sterile neutrinos, and evaluate the prospects for nuclear recoil calibrations.

items.title: Population structure of the velocity distribution in normal shock waves: Gaussian representations, Mach-number similarity, and prediction
items.summary: Normal shock waves are commonly described as mixtures of upstream and downstream Maxwellians. Discrete-velocity solutions of three relaxation models up to Mach 12 and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) of hard-sphere and variable-hard-sphere gases up to Mach 25 are used to examine the population structure, Mach-number similarity and upstream precursor of their velocity distributions. Three anisotropic Gaussian populations reproduce the streamwise reduced distributions of the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model and of DSMC to within 4\% up to Mach 12, and of DSMC to within 6\% at Mach 25, whereas two Maxwellians incur errors up to 50\% (BGK) and 37\% (DSMC). Collision histories identify the hard-sphere beam with unscattered stream molecules, which carry half of the peak viscous stress; the other populations are effective descriptions, not collision classes. Above Mach 5, Rankine--Hugoniot-scaled distributions are nearly Mach-independent, with corrections linear in $1/M^2$, consistent with the scaled kinetic equation. At equal normalised density, Mach 8 and 12 give the heat flux and stress at Mach 25 within 1\%, comparable to the accuracy of the reference; with one moment equation for position, physical-space profiles follow within 5\%. Comparing three prediction methods shows that the accuracy comes from the scaling; the Gaussian form adds compactness. Ahead of the shock, the mass of upstream-moving molecules decays as a stretched exponential with effective exponent 0.68--0.87. Collisions regenerate upstream-moving molecules, which explains a decay slower than free-flight survival; a linear cascade model with a downstream-Maxwellian source and no input from the shock interior reproduces the decay rates within 1.2\%.

items.title: Multi-output neural network surrogate for double-pulse femtosecond optothermal control of thin silicon films on fused silica
items.summary: We introduce a multi-output feedforward neural network surrogate trained on a coupled multiple-reflection and two-temperature model to map double-pulse femtosecond laser excitation (1030 nm) of crystalline silicon films on fused silica across film thicknesses (50-500 nm) and inter-pulse delays (0-10ps). Trained via Levenberg-Marquardt optimization on 2000 physical simulations, the dual-hidden-layer network ([40,30] neurons) simultaneously predicts six strongly coupled optothermal observables, peak electron temperature, peak lattice temperature, peak carrier density, minimum and maximum absorptivity and minimum refractive index achieving coefficients of determination R2 larger than 0.9998 across all targets. Evaluating a dense 200 by 200 design grid in milliseconds resolves pronounced thin-film interference fringes and carrier-induced index modulation, identifying an optimal optothermal coupling regime at d=156 nm and Dt=4.572 ps. This unified machine-learning workflow eliminates computationally expensive multi-physics runtime bottlenecks for real-time laser processing control and inverse photonic thin-film design.

items.title: Geometric tracking of a halo CME using full-circle wide-field views from PUNCH
items.summary: We tracked the large, geoeffective halo coronal mass ejection (CME) of 2025-May-31 across the very wide field of view of the Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission, as a proof of concept for data-informed forecasting of CME arrival times at Earth. using simple point-and-click measurement of the front location as far as 47 degrees away from the Sun itself, we constrained an analytic "ludicrous ice-cream cone" geometric model with just three parameters: position angle, off-Earth-Sun angle, and propagation speed. We show that the model is sufficient to capture the bulk envelope of the CME, and also insufficient to capture the complexity of the CME's evolution. We generated simulated arrival-time forecasts for the CME by extrapolating the constant-velocity propagation to determine the time of impact with Earth. These "retro-forecasts" converged to within 30 +/- 15 minutes of the actual arrival time, 8 hours prior to arrival. The convergence was marked by a clear inflection point in the curve of predicted-arrival-time vs time-of-forecast. We conclude that continuous wide-field tracking is sufficiently powerful to enable even crude models to substantially improve arrival-time forecasting precision, and discuss future work required both to validate this single-event result and to extend it to more sophisticated analyses.

items.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
items.summary: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data remain distributed, moved between slab layouts using collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a p-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-pMG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for the generalised Poisson problem on octree meshes across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. These results provide practical guidelines for solver selection based on mesh structure and coefficient characteristics.

items.title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
items.summary: Compliant coatings offer a passive approach to modifying near-wall turbulence and potentially reducing skin-friction drag, but high-fidelity exploration of the coupled parameter space is costly. We develop a two-way coupled resolvent-Galerkin framework for turbulent channel flow over finite-thickness, layered viscoelastic coatings. The fluid is modeled using the Navier-Stokes equations linearized about a turbulent mean state, while the solid is represented by a through-thickness Galerkin discretization of the elastodynamic equations. The solid response is condensed into a spectral surface-impedance operator at the fluid-solid interface. At $Re_τ= 180$, stiff panels approach the rigid-wall response, whereas more compliant panels modify the low-rank response associated with the near-wall cycle. A Reynolds-number study shows that panels with fixed nondimensional material stiffness can produce different responses depending on whether their thickness scales with inner or outer flow length scales. The influence of viscoelastic damping is examined across low- and high-frequency regimes, where stiffness-proportional damping alters the high-frequency fractional-energy distribution, while the low-frequency distribution remains relatively insensitive to damping. For multilayer panels, the fluid-facing material determines the interfacial wave speed, while the subsurface stiffness distribution modifies the panel's effective thickness. Temporal stability analysis identifies regions of parameter space where a steady harmonic response is relevant and regions where instabilities grow. Finally, a leading-order, covariance-based drag-estimation framework relates the coupled response to changes in the mean flow and to the estimated skin-friction drag. Together, these tools provide a basis for screening coating designs and selecting candidates for high-fidelity simulations and experiments.

items.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
items.summary: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

items.title: Geometry-Derived Capacitance Dyadics with Floquet Sideband Correction for Anisotropic Periodic Patch Metasurfaces
items.summary: Homogenised sheet models describe periodic metallic patch layers using a scalar sheet capacitance, which is only valid when the effective response is isotropic. An isotropic response exists for unit cells with patch geometries that have rotational symmetry of order three or higher. Lower-symmetry unit cells with irregular or random geometries generically require a full 2 x 2 surface-capacitance dyadic. We present a framework that computes this dyadic directly from the arbitrary gap-connected patch geometry on a unit cell of a hexagonal lattice. The two-dimensional Bravais periodicity fixes the two independent macroscopic loading directions, the connectivity of the gap ensures a full-rank response for the geometries considered here, and the point-group symmetry of the patch constrains the form of the dyadic. A quasi-static boundary value problem on a single periodic cell then determines its independent entries. We use the surface-capacitance dyadic in the anisotropic surface- wave dispersion relation, which includes the leading spatially-dispersive first shell Floquet-sideband correction. For each new patch geometry, the dyadic and the first-shell correction are obtained from a single quasi-static cell problem and from the reconstructed boundary. So anisotropic surface- wave dispersion follows without a per-geometry full-wave eigenmode band sweep or sheet-tensor retrieval. We validate this geometry-to-dispersion chain against full-wave eigenmode simulations across six representative symmetry classes, showing that the correction captures band flattening near the Brillouin-zone boundary and improves agreement relative to the local dyadic model.

items.title: New rules, old habits: across seven team sports, each league keeps its own way of using the rules
items.summary: Studies of a rule change usually report one average effect, for one league or several combined. We asked whether a rule change reorders leagues, in 101 leagues of seven sports. When the substitution limit rose from three to five, the leagues already ranked from most substitutions to fewest, as known for the biggest leagues. In their first season under five, the fourteen top leagues kept that order (rank correlation 0.89; one means the same order, zero unrelated orders). That is about as firmly as from one ordinary season to the next. A prediction for twelve second tiers, written before their records were read, held (0.73). They ranked like their country's top league. Across rule changes in other sports, leagues kept their order in four of eight tests. In every sport measured, a league stayed near its place among its sport's leagues from season to season. Under five, clubs inside a league differed more within a season than the leagues did, but their differences lasted less. Rule-makers should judge a change league by league, against each league's own seasons.

items.title: Improving Tropical Cyclone Forecasts through Objective Ensemble Track-Error Reduction
items.summary: Accurate tropical cyclone (TC) track guidance is essential for warnings, evacuation planning, and risk communication, but outlying members and distinct track scenarios can degrade raw ensemble forecasts. Statistical and machine-learning (ML) methods proposed to improve ensemble guidance are difficult to compare because previous studies often use different forecast systems, basins, periods, and verification methods. Using a common verification framework, this study compares six objective methods (four statistical trimming and two ML methods) with the full ensemble mean for 138 TCs forecast by GEFS, MOGREPS-G, and IFS during 2016-2024. Dynamic trimming (DT) is the most consistent statistical method, reducing mean total track error by 8.0%, 13.4%, and 16.1% at short, medium, and long ranges. Its largest benefits occur in high-spread cases, where it can reach 70% of the low-error bound. Short-lead-error trimming (SLET) provides useful delayed guidance after early observations become available, but its improvement decreases with lead time. Regression-mixture clustering (RC) shows potential in low-spread cases and provides the largest improvement over the control run. The gradient boosted tree (GBT) produces the largest medium-range improvement and exceeds the theoretical trimming bound, suggesting strong potential, particularly when the observed track is poorly represented by the ensemble family. However, its 12.8% short-range degradation and gains concentrated in a small subset of cases indicate overcorrection when the ensemble mean is already accurate, highlighting the need for additional constraints. These results provide a consistent basis for using objective error-reduction methods to strengthen TC track guidance for operational decision-making.

items.title: Machine Learning the $GW$ Self-Energy Operator for Real Materials
items.summary: Machine learning of $GW$ in solids has largely focused on prediction of scalar quasiparticle energy corrections. Here, we introduce a phase-aware many-body transformer that predicts the full $\mathbf{k}$-resolved complex self-energy matrix. As a proof of principle, we apply the model to predict quasiparticle energies before and after diagonalization of the quasiparticle Hamiltonian, obtaining a test set mean absolute error (MAE) of 29 meV for a dataset of 1745 2D materials in the static COHSEX approximation and 60 meV for a more limited dataset of 433 materials calculated within a plasmon-pole model. COHSEX pretraining followed by finetuning reduces this MAE to 42 meV. The predicted matrices also accurately reproduce QP wavefunctions.

items.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
items.summary: Symmetry is a foundational principle of physics: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the coordinate frame, unit system, or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet today's leading neural surrogates lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation), rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs. Because the boundary determines the interior solution, ISLA encodes the posed boundary once into learned slices and evaluates arbitrary interior points independently through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel. Inputs are nondimensionalized in scales computed from the boundary, sums over boundary cells are area-weighted quadratures that converge under mesh refinement, and geometry enters only as distances and relative angles to equivariant slice anchors, making the model equivariant to rigid motions and reflections up to optional token subsampling and tree clustering. On AeroZoo, 2,816 3D flows spanning diverse geometries, poses, physical scales, and boundary conditions, ISLA's mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 1.9 and 2.2 times lower than any baseline's. On full AirfRANS, ISLA is second only to an explicit boundary-integral network (GLOBE), with errors at least 1.6 times lower than Transolver's and GeoTransolver's in every field.

items.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moiré Flat-Band Superlattices
items.summary: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moiré superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moiré modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moiré superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moiré superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

items.title: On the relation of secondary motions to large- and very-large-scale motions
items.summary: The coexistence of secondary motions with large-scale and very-large-scale motions (LSMs/VLSMs) is investigated by direct numerical simulations of turbulent open-channel flow over streamwise-aligned Gaussian ridges, varying the ridge spacing $S$ and height $h$. First, the ridge height controls the secondary-motion strength and thereby the coexistence with VLSMs. VLSMs are suppressed for $h \geqslant 0.05δ$, with $δ$ the open-channel height, and re-emerge at $h = 0.025δ$, where the mean secondary motions are comparable in strength to those over strip-type surfaces. Previously reported differences between strip- and ridge-type surfaces thus reflect secondary-motion strength rather than surface type. Second, proper orthogonal decomposition and conditional averaging reveal instantaneous secondary motions that span approximately $2δ$, fill the channel height irrespective of $S$ and $h$, and are stronger than their mean. These are identified as LSMs spatially locked and amplified by the ridges. Over dense ridges, their alternation between neighbouring ridges yields weak, near-wall confined mean secondary motions, although VLSMs are suppressed over the full channel height. The ridge height thus sets the strength of the locked LSMs, whereas the ridge spacing sets where and for how long they persist. For weak locked LSMs, ridges spaced at their natural spanwise extent increase the VLSM energy, indicating that persistent locked LSMs concatenate into VLSMs. Third, large-scale instantaneous secondary motions persist over dense ridges in the absence of long streaks. This suggests that secondary motions are driven by intermittent cross-sectional motions rather than by long streaks, similar to the streak-less bursts in near-wall turbulence.

items.title: Recursive regularisation in lattice Boltzmann magnetohydrodynamics
items.summary: Recursive regularisation (RR) improves the stability of lattice Boltzmann schemes, but its structure and limitations in magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) remain insufficiently understood. This work connects RR to central-Hermite-moment (CHM) collisions on D2Q9 and D3Q27 through a closed-form reconstruction valid for arbitrary second-order relaxation rates. The central moments of the Maxwell stress coincide, up to sign, with the recursion coefficients, providing a systematic basis for MHD collision operators. Common two-dimensional raw- and central-moment schemes thus correspond to regularisation with a unit bulk relaxation rate. In three dimensions, a CHM implementation reproduces RR to round-off, while a monomial central-moment collision differs at fourth order and produces a four- to twelve-fold larger kinetic-energy error in the tested flow. Chapman--Enskog analysis shows that, with a magnetic field, the hydrodynamic recursion reconstructs the third-order non-equilibrium with a relative error of $78$--$96\%$ ($4\%$ without a field). A local correction largely removes it, yet changes the solutions by less than their discretisation error, consistent with its Burnett-order character. Three-dimensional vortex simulations show approximately second-order convergence at $\mathrm{Re}=100$ and agree with pseudo-spectral solutions through the peak current at $\mathrm{Re}=1000$ and, with a unit bulk rate, at $\mathrm{Re}=3000$. There, single-rate RR develops a compressive instability whose onset depends on the grid, lattice Mach number and initial magnetic configuration. For the standard initial field, a unit bulk rate suppresses it at $\mathrm{Ma}=0.034$ for $N\ge128$. This improvement does not extend to BGK collisions or prevent failure at $\mathrm{Re}=10,000$. These results show that robust three-dimensional MHD simulations require regularisation and bulk dissipation to be considered together.

items.title: Threshold Properties in Degenerate Distributed Feedback Lasing
items.summary: We investigate threshold properties in degenerate distributed feedback (DDFB) lasing in a double-grating photonic structure that operates near a degenerate band edge (DBE) with the potential to support robust single-frequency lasing. The DBE is an exceptional point degeneracy (EPD) of fourth order involving four coalescing Bloch eigenmodes. We also provide an analytical demonstration that, for a four-mode system, a quartic flat Bloch dispersion implies the coalescence of the four eigenvectors into a single eigendirection, without explicitly calculating them. Unlike previous studies based on coupled-mode theory, here the realistic double grating is studied using a full-wave method. A DDFB photonic cavity operating close to the DBE frequency is shown to display a large quality factor that scales with the fifth power of the cavity length. Upon the inclusion of gain, the DDFB cavity displays a low lasing threshold with the exceptional scaling as the inverse of the fifth power of the double-grating length, i.e., $α_{D,th} \propto 1/N^5$, where $N$ is the number of waveguide unit cells making the mirrorless cavity. These results suggest the potential for compact, single-frequency lasing using a mirrorless cavity with minimal device footprint. The DDFB laser is very attractive for various applications including communications, sensing, and spectroscopy.

items.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
items.summary: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

items.title: Detection of minimum ionising particles with internal gain in the first Silicon Electron Multiplier demonstrators
items.summary: The Silicon Electron Multiplier (SiEM) is a novel sensor concept for minimum ionising particle (MIP) detection that uses internal gain achieved through a composite electrode structure embedded within the silicon bulk. Unlike conventional gain sensors (LGADs, APDs), the SiEM achieves amplification through applied electric potentials rather than doped gain layers, potentially offering superior radiation hardness above $10^{16}\,n_{\mathrm{eq}}/\mathrm{cm}^2$. Following initial conceptual studies and simulation work, several fabrication approaches were explored, including Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) at Centro Nacional de Microelectrónica (CNM) and Metal Assisted Chemical Etching (MACEtch) at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI). This paper reports the first experimental results from functional SiEM demonstrators produced by Hamamatsu Photonics K. K. (HPK) using a single-electrode configuration with modified geometry. Electrical characterisation through I-V measurements and test beam studies with minimum ionising particles demonstrate clear evidence of charge multiplication, with gains comparable to simulation predictions.

items.title: A Gravitomagnetic Bootstrap: from Newtonian gravity to general relativity via localizing rotational and conformal symmetries
items.summary: Newtonian gravity, in the light of the Equivalence Principle, is best understood as a localization of Galilean inertial structure --- or at least, of the part of Galilean inertial structure that defines rectilinear acceleration. I consider what kind of theory can be constructed if we also localize rotational inertia and spatial and temporal scales. The resultant theory, given weak assumptions, is unique up to a constant with the dimensions of velocity and an overall sign. For an appropriate choice of these, it coincides with the first post-Newtonian approximation to general relativity, so that this construction gives a method to bootstrap from Newtonian gravity to general relativity without explicitly presupposing special relativity.

items.title: An Analytical Model for Fast Design Optimization and Performance Studies of nuSTORM
items.summary: The concept of generating neutrino beams from stored muons (nuSTORM) has been explored for several decades. A few nuSTORM facilities have been designed for GeV muons, and a design of a sub-GeV nuSTORM, proposed for the European Spallation Source, is now underway. At low energy, the much larger beam divergence can significantly reduce the neutrino flux reaching the detector. Therefore, optimization of facility parameters is essential to avoid additional flux losses. This optimization, however, is not trivial due to the interdependency of the parameters. In this paper, we derive an analytical expression for the absolute neutrino flux incident on the detector front face and show how it can guide the optimization of a nuSTORM facility. The analytical expression is furthermore validated with published data and Monte Carlo simulations from five separate cases. In addition, we show how it can be extended to also predict the neutrino energy distribution at the detector, thus offering a convenient method to estimate the facility performance without time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations of particle transport and decay.
authors: J. P. A. M. de André

items.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
items.summary: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(ρ)=1+a^2/(4ρ^2)$. Through the Plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=μ_r=n(ρ)\mathbf{I}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(ωa/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $πa^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

items.title: Quantum-Enhanced Passive and Active Radio-Frequency Photonic Imaging
items.summary: Radio-frequency (RF) photonics enables broadband, phase-coherent sensing beyond the reach of purely electronic architectures, yet at a given optical carrier power its sensitivity is bounded by the standard quantum limit of the optical readout. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that this limit can be surpassed in both passive and active RF imaging modalities by encoding RF signals onto a bright phase-squeezed optical carrier and recovering them via balanced homodyne detection, while the RF front end, illumination, and image reconstruction remain classical. A unified measurement model shows that phase squeezing reduces the variance of the additive readout noise by a single factor $g$, yielding peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) gains of up to $2G$, where $G\equiv10\log_{10}(1/g)$: between $G$ and $2G$ for deterministic targets in active imaging when the classical noise of the echoes is negligible against the readout noise, and set by the ratio of scene noise to readout noise in passive imaging. We validate the model in an experiment in the 5--20 MHz band, in which synthesized RF scenes are replayed through a physical squeezed-light receiver. With 3 dB of squeezing, the PSNR improves by about 6 dB, close to $2G$, in the readout-noise-dominated regime of both modalities, and the model predicts the measured gains without free parameters. These results identify where squeezed-light readout benefits RF-photonic imaging: wherever the optical readout noise, rather than the scene or the RF front end, dominates the image error.

items.title: Exact Scaling Theory of Social Tipping Phenomena in Finite Populations
items.summary: Granovetter's threshold model provides a classical framework for social mobilization, in which collective action spreads through self-reinforcing cascades as individuals join once the movement size reaches their personal threshold. Here, we investigate social tipping points by treating the initial fraction of instigators, $ρ_0$, as a control parameter in a finite population of $N$ agents with activation thresholds drawn from a Beta distribution with shape parameters $α$ and $β$. We characterize the thermodynamic phase diagram, which exhibits both continuous and discontinuous cascade transitions, and develop an exact combinatorial formulation for finite populations. The discontinuous transitions are hybrid, combining a jump in the final active fraction with a square-root critical singularity associated with an interior saddle-node bifurcation. Using the empirical cumulative distribution of quenched thresholds, we develop an asymptotic finite-size scaling theory that identifies the stochastic mechanisms responsible for rounding these transitions. For power-law thresholds ($α>1$, $β=1$), the critical window and the mean inactive fraction at criticality both scale as $N^{-1/3}$. For hybrid transitions governed by an interior saddle-node, the critical window scales as $N^{-1/2}$, while the conditional displacement of stalled cascades from the marginal state scales as $N^{-1/4}$. We further derive an explicit Gaussian scaling function for the probability of complete activation and show that convergence to this limiting function is exceptionally slow, with corrections of order $N^{-1/6}$. These results establish the extensively seeded Granovetter model as a tractable framework for investigating finite-population fluctuations and hybrid criticality in irreversible threshold-driven cascades.

items.title: Solver-consistent learned curvature for algebraic volume-of-fluid simulations of rising bubbles: symmetry-preserving networks, closed-loop data aggregation and a posteriori benchmarks
items.summary: Curvature reconstructed from compressed volume fractions exhibits a persistent force-weighted bias in the tested algebraic volume-of-fluid formulation. In OpenFOAM interFoam, face curvature is underestimated by 11-22% for radii of 2.5-40 cells, explaining the 14-17% static Laplace-pressure deficit. This bias is consistent with approximately 2% rise-velocity underprediction in the first Hysing benchmark. We estimate curvature from 5 x 5 volume-fraction stencils using a two-hidden-layer perceptron with exact phase-exchange antisymmetry and invariance under all eight square-grid symmetries. Training uses solver-generated profiles of periodic translating bubbles, droplets, and flat films with exact analytical curvature labels. Iterative data aggregation incorporates model-solver feedback and resolves deployment instabilities found in 15 of 76 periodic cases with the initial model. Band-weighted face interpolation supplies the same capillary force to momentum prediction and pressure correction. Independent tests show static pressure-jump errors of 2-6% and reductions in time-averaged maximum capillary numbers by factors of 2.8-16. Across three grids, time-integrated rise-velocity errors decrease from 2.06-2.76% to 0.65-1.04% in the first Hysing benchmark and from 5.64-8.72% to 4.72-7.61% in the second. Tuned curvature smoothing gives smaller static pressure-jump errors, but its first-benchmark accuracy deteriorates with refinement and second-benchmark gains remain marginal. A separate interface-gated dissipative momentum closure achieves a held-out coefficient of determination of 0.47 on Favre-filtered targets but changes rise velocity by less than 0.03% of its peak. Capillary-force discretisation is therefore the more influential correction target for the tested laminar bubbles.

items.title: Analytic Model for Transient Plateau Filling in Vibrational Distributions of Periodically Driven Plasmas
items.summary: In periodically driven molecular plasmas, the vibrational distribution function is governed by the competition between vibration--vibration (V-V) up-pumping along the anharmonic ladder and vibration--translation (V-T) relaxation, producing the Treanor--Gordiets distribution. When vibrational energy accumulates across cycles faster than V-V exchange can populate the upper levels, the Gordiets plateau remains transiently depleted. Existing algebraic models assume a quasi-steady plateau, whereas exact transient solutions of the nonlinear V-V diffusion equation require the elapsed time since excitation and the source strength, which are unavailable in multidimensional simulations that track only local macroscopic variables. Here, elapsed time is replaced by a local vibrational energy timescale formed from the vibrational energy per molecule and its period-averaged rate of change. This reduces the diffusion equation in level space to an ordinary differential equation solved in closed form without linearization, yielding a level-dependent correction to the steady plateau governed by a single dimensionless group: the number of V-V collisions per energy timescale weighted by the plateau amplitude at the Treanor minimum. The distribution front advances as the square root of this group, and the steady distribution is recovered as the group grows large. Compared with state-to-state master-equation calculations for N$_2$ under nanosecond pulse trains spanning 300-1500 K, 0.041-1 atm, and 1-100 kHz (1440 sampled states), the model reduces the 90th-percentile error in level populations from 1.88 decades for the steady model and 1.32 decades for an adapted self-similar solution to 0.53 decades, at essentially the evaluation cost of the steady model.

items.title: Rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculation and master equation analysis of the CNO system in high-energy collisions
items.summary: The CNO system governs the formation and depletion of the CN, CO and NO radiative species relevant to combustion, astrophysical and hypersonic applications. The NO($X^2Π$) + C($^3P$), CN($X^2Σ^+$) + O($^3P$) and CO($X^1Σ^+$) + N($^4S$, $^2D$) collisional systems are investigated using rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculations and master equation analysis under hypersonic thermal conditions. Inelastic processes proceed primarily through rotational excitation of low-lying states and rovibrational excitation of high-lying states. For most systems, rotational and vibrational relaxation times exhibit comparable scales and unconventional temperature dependences, invalidating the assumption of decoupled energy modes. Dissociation is governed by high-lying rovibrational states and correlates strongly with the state-specific energy deficit rather than vibrational-specific dynamics. At $T$ = 10,000 K, 72 to 93% of the depletion of the diatomic species occurs within a quasi-steady-state (QSS) regime for all systems. At lower temperatures, a large portion of the depletion occurs outside the QSS regime, indicating that the QSS assumption holds only for moderate to high temperatures. No such regime is established for exchange reactions, demonstrating that the QSS assumption is invalid for modelling them. The NO + C system proceeds predominantly towards CN + O at low temperatures and towards the CO + N channels at high temperatures, preferentially forming N($^4S$). The fraction proceeding towards the CO + N channels remains lower than in available shock-tube measurements, while the thermal exchange rate coefficients reproduce shock-tube measurements and high-fidelity calculations. Finally, consistent similarities across inelastic, exchange and dissociation processes offer promising physical foundations for reduced-order model development.

items.title: A Differentiable Surrogate for Loss-Dominated Ion Beam Transport
items.summary: Radioactive nuclei with extreme proton-to-neutron ratios provide unique probes of nuclear structure, fundamental symmetries, astrophysical processes, and applications such as medicine. However, their short half-lives and low production rates mean that experiments must work with few desired ions, often amid contaminant backgrounds exceeding the signal by six orders of magnitude. Efficiently isolating, transporting, and delivering these ions through multi-stage apparatus is therefore a central challenge. We introduce a differentiable probabilistic surrogate for ion-beam transport in regimes dominated by particle loss. The model jointly captures the survival probability of ions along the beamline and the evolving phase-space distribution of the surviving particles by combining discrete-time survival analysis with conditional normalizing flows. Applied to a high-dimensional electrostatic beamline, the resulting likelihood enables gradient-based optimization of operating voltages and inference of beam properties from sparse detector observations. Once trained, the surrogate provides millisecond-scale differentiable predictions, transforming particle-tracking simulations with hard losses into an inference-ready model for experimental design, beamline optimization, and future digital twins of experiments with rare nuclei.

items.title: A plug-in energy-balance freezing module for transformer frost nowcasting without leaf-sensor inputs
items.summary: Frost protection requires local warnings where leaf-sensor inputs are unavailable. In the frost literature we surveyed, physics entered machine-learning models through inputs, numerical-model coupling, or losses, rather than model structure. We develop a transformer-compatible module that embeds leaf energy-balance physics in freezing-probability forecasts: an energy-balance temperature reference and a learned residual predict leaf temperature, which drives a multiplicative gate imposing a temperature-dependent probability cap. We mathematically prove conditional monotonicity and an alarm boundary, and test whether placing the same information in the output pathway or in attention yields different benefits. We evaluated 12 hourly leads at 19 Korean stations over five frost seasons, with and without leaf-sensor inputs. In the 2025-2026 hold-out season without these inputs, our time-token transformer (PET-E) achieved a lead-mean critical success index (CSI) of 0.516 versus 0.478 for fixed-configuration, joint-lead LightGBM, with significant gains at all 12 leads, and the fraction of alarms at observed leaf temperatures of at least 2 degrees C fell from 0.087 to 0.051 relative to the unmodified backbone. Across the hold-out and a retrospective 2024-2025 evaluation, the module reduced Brier scores and warm-surface alarm fractions in both the time-token transformer and iTransformer, with no significant CSI decrease at any lead. At held-out stations without static or leaf-sensor inputs, both module-equipped backbones exceeded LightGBM at all 12 leads (CSI 0.468 and 0.467 versus 0.437). In the time-token backbone, the temperature pathway reduced this alarm fraction in all four settings, whereas the attention prior increased CSI in three. These findings link an explicit temperature-dependent probability cap to improved forecasts and distinguish output-side from attention-based embedding.

items.title: Gas expansion in global models of nanosecond pulsed discharges: a reduced gas-dynamic model coupled to plasma kinetics
items.summary: Global (zero-dimensional) kinetic models of nanosecond pulsed discharges describe the expansion of the heated gas channel (kernel) with simplified gas-dynamic closures. We show that these closures can lead to errors of tens of percent in the calculated gas density, temperature and species densities, especially in the first microseconds after every pulse. Here, we propose a fast, reduced gas-dynamic model of Lagrangian shells, closed by an approximate cylindrical acoustic radiation condition, with no fitted physical coefficient. The reduced model reproduces the axis density obtained by verified one- dimensional compressible computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations within 2.4% for smooth deposition profiles and axis pressures up to six times ambient, typically a thousand times faster than CFD. We couple it with our in-house global plasma-kinetics solver (SoPlasma-0D), whose energy partition after the pulse agrees well with that derived from measurements and with an independent calculation. Two microseconds after a single pulse in air, and compared with the proposed coupled model, the existing closures overestimate the axis density by up to a factor of 2.8, the atomic oxygen density by up to 2.7 and the temperature by up to 680 K. For repetitive pulses 200 or 430 ns apart, of equal energy per unit volume, no existing closure follows the coupled model at both intervals, in the gas density met by each later pulse and in the energy per molecule deposited by late pulses, which sets how strongly they dissociate and heat the gas. The proposed reduced model should therefore be used to describe the gas evolution during the expansion phase after every nanosecond pulse, and for repetitive pulses above about 100 kHz in kernels of radius up to about a millimetre.

items.title: Stability of Plasma Echo Growth and the Sharp Sobolev Stability Threshold for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau Equation
items.summary: We establish stability of growing plasma echo cascades for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau equation with Coulomb collisions near a global Maxwellian. The occurrence of plasma echoes, or even a growing cascade in a reduced model, does not by itself establish this stability. We prove that the amplification persists under changes in the linearized operator, including collisions and the exact evolving background coefficients, and under nonlinear perturbations. This yields optimality of the exponent $1/3$ obtained by Chaturvedi, Luk, and Nguyen in the Sobolev stability threshold. Specifically, we construct solutions with initial Sobolev perturbations of size $ν^{1/3}[\log(1/ν)]^p$ whose transport profiles exhibit norm inflation before the enhanced-dissipation time scale $ν^{-1/3}$. Since collisions preclude the backward Sobolev construction used in collisionless echo arguments, we prepare the initial data at physical time zero and control the entire forward evolution.

items.title: The role of turbulent jet dynamics on contrail formation from conventional and sustainable aviation fuels
items.summary: Large-eddy simulations (LES) coupled with a discretised population balance equation (PBE) are used to quantify the effect of turbulence on the early stages of contrail formation (jet regime) for both conventional (soot-rich) and sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs). SAFs typically have low aromatic content which causes a shift in the dominant nucleation pathway. The contribution from soot (non-volatile particulate matter, nvPM) is reduced, while the contribution from volatile particulate matter (vPM) is increased. The computational domain reproduces an experimental jet configuration that replicates the thermodynamic conditions encountered in the upper troposphere. The LES-PBE simulations capture well the jet-core cooling and bracket the experimental values of ice-crystal characteristics (number concentration, mean diameter and mass density) if a range of judicious values for parameters not specified in the experiments are employed. With the aid of one-dimensional, one-way coupled PBE approach, it is shown that soot particle activation can be reliably captured using steady aerosol-jet models. On the other hand, volatile particle activation is significantly affected by large fluctuations in temperature and humidity (and thereby supersaturation). Further downstream, non-linear dynamic coupling between the gas and aerosol phases becomes increasingly important for ice-crystal growth as well. Overall, the results demonstrate that for SAFs, turbulence is an important driver of particle activation and subsequent ice crystal growth and cannot be neglected. This finding motivates more fundamental studies to assess how turbulent jet dynamics modulates contrail formation in realistic engine configurations.

items.title: Physics-Spawned Neural Integration of Rotating Shallow-Water Dynamics
items.summary: Equation-derived neural integration can execute prescribed dynamics without training, while informative ensemble learning can estimate uncertain parameters and identify governing interactions without requiring differentiability. Together, these approaches motivate Physics-Spawned Informative Networks ($Φ$SpIN), a framework for prescribed and adaptive hybrid dynamical systems. As a first step toward flood modeling applications, we present $Φ$SpIN-SW, its prescribed-physics realization for the rotating shallow-water equations. Compatible C-grid operators on spherical Voronoi meshes define a computational graph that retains non-polynomial operations and advances the state through recurrent neural integration compiled with JAX. Analytical benchmarks characterize numerical errors, and global and coastal experiments closely reproduce reference solutions generated using the Model Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) model. At approximately 14~km global resolution, A100, H200 and B200 GPUs attain 9-, 19- and 34-fold higher timestep throughput than a 96-core MPAS-SW CPU reference under matched workloads. These results extend training-free neural integration beyond polynomial dynamics to complex geophysical simulation, establishing a computational foundation for subsequent adjoint-free ensemble estimation of physical and neural parameters and informative adaptation of operator structure.

items.title: Dynamics and stability of volatile thin liquid films on a heated vertical cylinder
items.summary: Volatile thin liquid films flowing down heated vertical cylinders are central to many heat transfer applications, including evaporative condensers, cooling of electronics, and solar thermal systems. Despite their importance, the coupled dynamics of evaporation, thermocapillarity, and interfacial instabilities on cylindrical geometries remain poorly understood. In this work, a lubrication-based model is developed to capture the nonlinear evolution of a volatile thin film under gravity, surface tension, van der Waals forces, and non-conservative evaporative flux. The model incorporates hydrodynamic pressure contributions to evaporation, enabling a unified description of phase-change effects on curved substrates. A linear stability analysis of the model equation is performed with a non-constant base film thickness. The linear growth rate is first obtained for a spatially uniform film. Then, for a spatially nonuniform film, a coupled system of linearized equations is solved using the finite element method. Further, the full liquid-vapor interface is numerically simulated to demonstrate liquid evaporation. Results reveal that evaporation accelerates film thinning, condensation promotes thickening, and van der Waals forces stabilize ultra-thin films by preventing rupture. The influence of Bond number, wavenumber, and pressure-dependent flux laws on droplet formation and collision dynamics is quantified. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into phase-change driven instabilities in cylindrical thin films and have direct implications for the design of efficient thermal management systems, evaporative cooling devices, and surface-engineered heat exchangers.

items.title: Fluid drags on a sphere at finite Reynolds number--a classical problem examined afresh
items.summary: Evaluating the drag coefficient Cd for a sphere moving in a fluid at finite Reynolds number Re has become a classical research subject in fluid dynamics, with publications appearing continuously by numerous authors over the years due to the unavailability of closed-form mathematical solutions. To date, mathematical formulas for calculating Cd as a function of Re can only be obtained by correlation curve fitting to experimental data. The consequence is the coexistence of various formulas with different mathematical fitting functions and an increasing number of fitting parameters. The present study focuses on examining the accuracy of Klyachko's 1934 formula for Cd with two common fractions as fitting parameters, which could enable closed form integration of a simplified equation governing rectilinear motion of aerosol spheres. The computed values of root-mean-square relative error from recently developed formulas show reasonable accuracy of the Klyachko formula for Re less than 1000 and its extension to Re less than 2e5 as a piecewise continuous function, with the possibility of significant improvement through a slight modification. Hence, a few demonstrative examples are presented using the extended Klyachko formula in the study of rectilinear acceleration, the calculation of the terminal velocity of aerosol spheres, and so forth, to shed fresh light on how this classical problem can be studied.

items.title: U-HamGNN: a universal model for magnetic Hamiltonians conditioned on spin and Hubbard U
items.summary: The electronic structure of a magnetic crystal depends jointly on its spin configuration and the on-site Hubbard correction U, requiring a separate DFT+U calculation for each combination. We introduce U-HamGNN, an equivariant network that takes these two inputs directly and predicts spin-resolved Hamiltonians across diverse crystal chemistries. A spectral-hybrid optimizer that weights each update direction by how consistently the gradient points along it reaches 8% lower Hamiltonian error than Muon and 26% lower than AdamW in a ten-epoch benchmark. The predicted bands reproduce U-dependent gap opening and altermagnetic spin splitting within the trained window and beyond it; exchange couplings and magnetic-order calls derived from the Hamiltonian agree with DFT+U on a calibration set. This universal model provides a new tool for magnetic research.

items.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
items.summary: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.

items.title: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the MoS$_2$/Sapphire System
items.summary: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the MoS$_2$/ $α$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) system. The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from ~1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On 2,820 held-out test structures from the DFT pool, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/angstrom. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5 %, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of point defects (Spearman $ρ$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($ρ$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($ρ$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %.

items.title: Self-assembly of dipolar nanoclusters on an attractive substrate: A coarse-grained simulation approach
items.summary: Recently, Thomas et al. [Nanoscale 17, 18291 (2025)] showed that bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of the type [Bi$_{38}$ O$_{45}$ (Boc-L-Phe-O)$_{24}$] form chains when deposited onto gold or pyrolitic graphite substrates. This chain formation is significantly enhanced when the bismuth in the BiO-NCs is partially replaced by cerium through doping. In this work, we study a simplified, coarse-grained model of this process, namely (magnetic) Stockmayer particles in the presence of an attractive substrate. The model is investigated by means of molecular dynamics simulations. The deposition experiment is mimicked by a rapid quench from high temperature to a low temperature below the bulk coexistence curve. The results are found to be qualitatively similar to the experimental observations reported earlier. In our simulations, we find significant chain formation in the bulk even at rather low concentrations, which is in contrast to the BiO-NCs in ethanol for which dynamic light scattering reveals negligible aggregation in the absence of the substrate. This lends support to a scenario, conjectured in the work of Thomas at al., where the dipole moments are induced by the particle-substrate interaction and hence there is little dipole moment in the bulk. In a second part, we study the system in equilibrium. We consider the scaling of chains, the number of layers populated as a function of two-dimensional density, and we draw analogies to polymers on interfaces, which have been extensively studied over the past decades. Most notably, it is found that the chains behave as self-avoiding walks at low densities, which gives way to rod-like scaling at higher densities.

items.title: Motion of a cylinder between parallel plates: complete Stokes resistance and pressure response
items.summary: A circular cylinder moving between two parallel plates is the canonical confined problem of two-dimensional Stokes flow. Rotation and translation of the cylinder along the channel become coupled and generate a pressure difference along the channel under zero-net-flux conditions. Existing results use different methods. We develop a completed double-layer boundary integral formulation based on the channel Green function to resolve narrow gaps at arbitrary transverse positions. The channel Green kernels are derived from a Fourier-transformed biharmonic problem, permitting explicit treatment of the free-space singularity, the slowly decaying nearest-wall contribution, and the small-wavenumber limit for accurate kernel evaluation under strong confinement. The boundary integral equation is discretised by a spectrally accurate Nyström scheme on a graded parametrisation, and the pressure jump follows from the zero-wavenumber limit of the streamwise momentum balance. A single linear system yields the full resistance matrix and pressure-jump coefficients for an eccentric cylinder; an additional right-hand side treats imposed net flux. For nonzero coefficients, comparisons with independent COMSOL finite-element simulations show relative differences below \(0.1\%\) for the resistance coefficients and at most \(0.0122\%\) for the pressure-response coefficients and excess hydraulic resistance. Reciprocity, symmetry constraints, and lubrication asymptotics provide additional checks on the numerical results. We track the coupling between rotation and translation and the pressure generated by the cylinder from the channel scale into the lubrication regime, and determine the pressure--flow relation, driving torque and efficiency of the rotating-cylinder pump for asymmetric clearances.

items.title: Quantum modeling of radical pair magnetic sensor based on electric dipole moment
items.summary: Photoreduction of cryptochrome protein in the retina is a well-known mechanism of navigation of birds through the geomagnetic field, yet the biosignal nature of the mechanism remains unclear. The absorption of blue light by the flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) chromophore can alter the distribution of electrons in cryptochrome and create radical pairs with separated charges. In this study, the spin dynamics of electrons in the radical pair including its spin-orbit coupling were investigated by quantum mechanical modeling. Spin-orbit coupling is negligible relative to other terms and has no significant role in the dynamics. However, it engages the spatial states of the radical pair and make possible to study spatial related observables. Several interactions were considered in the presence of an external magnetic field, and the resulting electric dipole moment in cryptochrome was computed as the quantity emerging from this coupling. The computations show the induced electric dipole moment clearly depend on the characteristics of the applied magnetic field even after considering dissipative effects. In fact, our findings indicate that the radical pair in cryptochrome protein is a magnetic biosensor, in the sense that in the presence of the geomagnetic field, variations in spin states can influence its electric dipole moment, which may be interpreted via the bird as an orientation signal. The results can be used in the advancement of bio-inspired technologies which replicate animal magnetic sensitivity.

items.title: Twister After Dark: Diagnosing a Damaging Nocturnal Tornado in Iloilo, Philippines (08 August 2026)
items.summary: (Abridge) At ~1430 UTC (2230 LST) on 08 August 2026, a significant tornado struck the Mandurriao and Jaro districts of Iloilo City, Philippines. Its parent supercell developed within the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Dolphin, under weak synoptic forcing, as a nocturnal low-level jet of ~40 kt near 1.5-3 km advected warm, moist marine air onshore. ERA5 depicted MUCAPE of ~2000 J/kg, negligible inhibition, an LCL below 300 m, and nearly purely streamwise low-level vorticity, but deep-layer shear (DLS, 0-6 km bulk wind difference) below 3 m/s. Hodographs from the newly operational Iloilo S-band dual-polarization radar (S-ILO), ~5-7 km from the storm, revealed low-level shear (LLS, 0-1 km bulk wind difference) of ~16 m/s and 0-1 km storm-relative helicity of 124-211 m^2/s^2. The storm exhibited a hook echo with a weak echo hole, a $Z_{DR}$ arc and ring, an elevated 55-60 dBZ rear-flank core consistent with a descending reflectivity core, and a ~50 dBZ ring interpreted as a debris ball. A survey of 31 damage indicators documented a ~2.9 km long and up to ~340 m wide path rated IF2 on the International Fujita Scale. Processor smoothing of the radial velocity and a $ρ_{HV}$ threshold for rainfall estimation masked any tornadic vortex or debris signature, although a radial velocity simulation shows that a narrow vortex (core radius ~50-100 m) with a rotational velocity of ~35-45 m/s could have been concealed. This case shows that significant tornadoes can develop at night during the Philippine monsoon season and that operational radar quality control should be revised to retain severe-storm signatures.

items.title: GPROF V08: Improving Satellite Precipitation Estimates Across a Heterogeneous Constellation of Passive-Microwave Sensors
items.summary: Precipitation estimates from the passive microwave observations (PMW) of the Global Precipitation Measurements (GPM) mission serve a wide range of scientific, societal, and economic applications. The Goddard Profiling Algorithm (GPROF) is the operational retrieval used to produce the precipitation estimates for all GPM PMW sensors. This study presents the implementation GPROF V08 -- the most recent version of GPROF and a major update aimed at improving the accuracy of precipitation estimates from the GPM constellation. GPROF V08 replaces the conventional Bayesian scheme used by earlier GPROF versions by a convolutional neural network (CNN). The first part of this two-part study described a novel ML framework for generating synthetic observations required for training CNN retrievals for all GPM sensors. This second part describes the final, operational implementation, which adds a second finetuning stage to the training.Retrievals from the new GPROF V08 algorithm for all principal GPM sensors are validated against reference precipitation estimates from various sources. Our results show that, while the magnitude of improvements vary by sensor and surface type, they are robust across sensors and metrics and can be as high as 40 \% for the linear correlation coefficient for precipitation estimates from SSMIS and ATMS over ocean compared to combined radar and radiometer retrievals from GPM. While some challenges remain -- such as an increased sensitivity to sensor degradation and the persistence of climatological biases, which remain of the same order as for GPROF V07 -- GPROF V08 constitutes a substantial advancement in spaceborne precipitation monitoring. Since the improvements are robust across all sensor of the constellation, the update is expected to improve the full record of GPM precipitation estimates and thus benefit a wide range of downstream datasets and applications.

items.title: Towards GPROF V08: A Machine-Learning Framework for Simulating Passive Microwave Observations of Precipitation
items.summary: Spatially resolved precipitation retrievals based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can improve precipitation estimates from passive microwave (PMW) observations and will be used to implement the next operational PMW retrieval algorithm for the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission. However, the conventional radiative transfer simulations used to extend the retrieval algorithm to the various sensors of the GPM constellation do not provide the spatial coverage required to train CNN-based retrievals. To address this, we introduce a machine-learning-based simulation framework that enables the training of the CNN-based GPROF-NN 3D retrieval algorithm for the full GPM constellation. At the core of this framework is Satformer, a new neural-network architecture that can translate PMW observations between any pair of GPM sensors. The resulting synthetic observations exhibit lower errors than conventional radiative transfer simulations and lead to more accurate precipitation retrievals when used to train GPROF-NN precipitation retrievals. We further demonstrate the applicability of the framework to new instruments by developing GPROF-NN retrievals for the Microwave Imager aboard the Weather System Follow-on Microwave satellite. While GPROF-NN retrievals based on the new simulation framework achieve lower instantaneous retrieval errors and higher correlations compared to independent reference data than conventional retrievals, residual simulation errors can introduce systematic biases in the resulting retrievals. The proposed simulation framework provides a key component for extending GPROF-NN to the full GPM constellation as part of the upcoming operational GPROF V08 retrieval algorithm. The results demonstrate the potential of machine-learning-based simulations to support spatially resolved precipitation retrievals across heterogeneous satellite constellations.

items.title: Darcy plume oscillations at low injection velocities
items.summary: We numerically investigate miscible buoyancy-driven Darcy plumes at low injection velocities. Below a critical injection velocity, the steady plume becomes unstable and develops periodic oscillations. Approaching the critical velocity, the oscillation amplitude vanishes while the frequency remains finite at the critical point, consistent with a supercritical Hopf bifurcation, whereas at lower injection velocities increasingly complex dynamics emerge. Unsteadiness also strongly enhances lateral mixing, increasing the mixing-layer thickness by a factor of approximately 2-3 compared with a steady plume. These findings reveal a previously unexplored dynamical regime of Darcy plumes with important consequences for subsurface transport and leakage.

items.title: Adaptive dynamics of eco-evolutionary repeated games: Effect of reward and punishment
items.summary: Long-term evolutionary processes can strongly influence common-pool resource conservation by generating new traits or behaviours that modify the feedback between population strategies and the resource state. Here we develop an eco-evolutionary framework in which individuals repeatedly interact with the same opponent and follow direct reciprocity through reactive strategies. The strategic dynamics is coupled to a renewable common resource and analyzed using adaptive dynamics. After our exhaustive non-linear dynamical analysis of $2\times2$ strategic games, we focus on comparative and combined usefulness of institutional incentives in the form of rewards and punishments in preventing the Tragedy of the Commons even when defection dominates in the replete resource state. We also report possibility of robust stable oscillations -- emerging via Hopf bifurcation -- in resource state and population strategies.

items.title: Magnetic control of hydrodynamic spin coupling between rotors: Ferrohydrodynamic effects in the two-rotor problem
items.summary: The hydrodynamic spin coupling between two rotors ("fluid gears") is investigated numerically for a magnetic fluid in non-uniform magnetic fields. An active cylinder drives a torque-free passive one inside a circular corral, with one rotor heated. The model combines magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and ferrohydrodynamics (FHD), with the full Kelvin force and temperature-dependent Langevin magnetisation. For the oil-based ferrofluid EFH1 the Lorentz force is negligible, and the Kelvin force drives thermomagnetic convection from the heated rotor. Steady torque-free states are computed with Taylor-Hood finite elements, the gear ratio $Γ$ being an additional unknown. Without a field the results agree within 1-8% with published planar simulations up to $\mathrm{Re}\approx 50$. About 17,000 steady states cover 34 arrangements of wires, NdFeB rods and magnet cores, gaps $G=0.1$-$0.7$, $\mathrm{Re}=10$-$40$ and heating of 5-20 K. Because the coupling is weak, fields of 1-2 mT change $Γ$ by an amount comparable to $Γ$ itself. At 2 mT it is reversed, strengthened or weakened in nine cases out of ten. The outcome is set by the source position: at the experimental gap and $\mathrm{Re}=20$ a source below the corral or behind the active rotor strengthens the gear-like counter-rotation up to 2.7-fold, and a source above the corral reverses it into belt-like corotation. Several sources do not act additively, and a magnet core inside the active rotor raises $|Γ|$ at small gaps to seven times the largest hydrodynamic value. At fixed geometry and Reynolds number, field strength and heating act approximately through a single thermomagnetic source parameter.

items.title: Geomagnetic Q-Response Inversion as a Calderón-Type Inverse Boundary Value Problem
items.summary: Whether electrical conductivity can be uniquely determined from magnetic measurements alone is a fundamental question in geomagnetic induction sounding. For a spherical conductor in the magnetoquasistatic model, we establish an equivalence between the complete Q-response and a restricted magnetic boundary operator, connecting geomagnetic induction to Calderon-type inverse boundary value theory. For axisymmetric conductivities, we derive exact representations of the zero-frequency zonal response derivatives as conductivity-weighted spatial moments. These formulas give an explicit interpretation of individual response derivatives, and completeness of the moment family yields conductivity uniqueness. For layered axisymmetric models with known shell interfaces and piecewise-constant radial dependence, we further establish uniqueness at a single nonzero frequency. Finite-dimensional subclasses also admit uniqueness and stability estimates from finitely many response coefficients at sufficiently low nonzero frequencies. These results identify complementary mechanisms for conductivity recovery from magnetic-only observations, while uniqueness for general three-dimensional scalar conductivities from ideal magnetic-only Q-response data remains unresolved.

items.title: Bowed-String-Mechanism-Inspired Quantum Dissociation Control of Molecules
items.summary: Inspired by Guettler's mechanics of accelerating Helmholtz motion, we present a predictive laser pulse-shaping strategy to rapidly initiate the multiphoton dissociation of vibrationally excited diatomic molecules. In intense infrared fields, NO molecules often exhibit unpredictable control windows due to the chaotic fragmentation of intensity thresholds. By incorporating a bowing-analogue transient shaper enforced by a boundary-matching constraint with symmetric derivative slope transitions and vanishing initial boundary conditions ($T(0) = 0, T'(0) = 0$), we demonstrate that a pulse engineered with non-linear front-flank acceleration reduces the multi-valued threshold topology into a single, predictable linear dissociation corridor. Wigner quasiprobability distributions confirm that this temporal acceleration trajectory opens cantori bottlenecks and suppresses wave-packet fragmentation, restricting the quantum non-classicality index to $M_{\text{nc}} \le 0.15$. Our simulations verify that this trajectory engineering preserves wave-packet localization and maintains high dissociation yields ($P_{\text{diss}} > 0.95$) even under Markovian thermal dephasing ($δ/ω_0 = 10^{-4}$) and frozen rotational variations up to $J = 5$. Comparison with contemporary ultrafast spectral phase modulation protocols demonstrates that conventional smooth pulse envelopes, despite advanced phase-chirping, exhibit limitations in restricting non-hyperbolic cantori stickiness due to insufficient sub-picosecond acceleration. In contrast, our boundary-constrained shaper enforces a deterministic, single-valued dissociation corridor under equivalent few-picosecond control windows.

items.title: Gradient-Based Inverse Design of Free-Energy Landscapes with Diffusion Models
items.summary: Free-energy surfaces govern the populations of metastable states and the barriers that control transitions between them, making their direct optimization a central challenge in molecular and materials design. In this work, we introduce Gradient-Based Free Energy Surface Optimization (GB-FESO), an inverse design framework that uses a trained conditional diffusion model as a differentiable surrogate for the ensemble distribution. After training, the diffusion model is frozen, and the conditioning variables defining the system are optimized so that the generated ensemble reproduces a prescribed target free-energy surface. The optimization is carried out by backpropagating a distribution-level loss, based on kernel density estimates of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, through a deterministic diffusion sampling trajectory. We first validate GB-FESO on one-dimensional Gaussian ensembles, demonstrating that both continuous and relaxed discrete conditioning variables can be optimized to recover target distributions, including those outside the training domain. We then apply the method to a four-particle Lennard-Jones toy peptide exhibiting multiple metastable conformational states. In this more physically motivated setting, GB-FESO successfully optimizes the interaction parameters to reproduce target free-energy landscapes in the majority of test cases, with optimization performed either in the full internal-coordinate space or in a reduced collective-variable representation. These results establish GB-FESO as a promising first step toward an ensemble-level inverse design framework for molecular systems with prescribed thermodynamic and kinetic behavior.

items.title: Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
items.summary: Magnetic d-electron oxides usually have a long-range-ordered ground state and an above-ground-state disordered para phase. The historical Slater-Mott controversy still reverberating to date pertains to understanding the origin of the insulating vs metallic nature of these two phases. Slater suggested that the insulating character evolved from the long-range order (LRO) antiferromagnetic (AFM) cell-doubling, leading to energy band repulsion and thus to forming a band gap. The reliance on LRO to explain gapping suggests that the absence of LRO in the spin-disordered para-phase would deprive the system from band repulsion, thus predicting a metallic paramagnetic (PM) phase.
