We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exact Rajchman realization. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. This gives a negative answer to an open-range absolute-continuity question of Ohrysko and Wojciechowski.

items.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic not 3
items.summary: This article takes place in the extension and generalization proposed by Corredor, Deloro and Wiscons of the works of Dickson and Wagner regarding the Classification of minimal $\text{Sym}(n)$- and $\text{Alt}(n)$-modules. In particular, we classify the minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(6)$-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(n)$- and $\text{Sym}(n)$-modules with an additive dimension.

items.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
items.summary: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

items.title: Convex polynomial approximation on the unit ball
items.summary: Let $\mathbb{B}^d$ be the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge1$. We prove that, for every convex $f\in C(\mathbb{B}^d)$ and every integer $n\ge1$, there exists a polynomial $P_n$ of total degree at most $n$, convex on all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that $\|f-P_n\|_{C(\mathbb{B}^d)}\le c\,ω_2(f,n^{-1};\mathbb{B}^d)$. Here $ω_2$ is the ordinary second modulus of smoothness and $c=c_d$ depends only on $d$. In particular, we obtain the rate $O(n^{-2})$ for convex functions with uniformly bounded second derivatives.

items.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

items.title: A scaling approach to double phase equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
items.summary: We study radial solutions of the double phase equation $-Δ_p u - \operatorname{div}(|x|^{-b}\,|\nabla u|^{q-2}\nabla u) = f(|x|,u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, whose operator admits a scaling that acts on both phases simultaneously. Our first main result is a sharp description of the continuous and compact embeddings of the radial energy space into weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^s(\mathbb{R}^N;|x|^{-c})$ with an explicit characterization of their admissible regions in the $(s,c)$-plane. The two critical edges reflect the two phases: on the edge attached to the $p$-phase compactness is lost by spreading to infinity, while on the edge attached to the weighted $q$-phase it is lost by concentration at the origin. Our second main result concerns equations with one critical term on each edge. We show that bounded Palais-Smale sequences either converge or lose at least the energy $β^\ast = \min\{β_1,β_2\}$, where $β_1$ and $β_2$ are the explicit single-phase thresholds, and that this level is optimal when the critical terms are unweighted. Thus, the two mechanisms cannot combine to lower the compactness threshold. Combining these results with a Pohožaev identity, variational methods for scaled functionals and the Fadell-Rabinowitz cohomological index, we prove nonexistence results, obtain an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues on the scaling line and infinitely many solutions for pure power equations, and show that large superscaled and small subscaled perturbations of the doubly critical equation yield multiple solutions.

items.title: The pinched Veronese has no Koszul filtration
items.summary: In this paper we prove that the pinched Veronese subalgebra $k [x^3,x^2y,xy^2,x^2z,xz^2,y^3,y^2z,yz^2,z^3] \subset k[x,y,z]$ has no Koszul filtration regardless of the field $k$, despite it being a Koszul algebra. We do this by showing that no ideal $(f,g)$ minimally generated by two linear forms can belong to a Koszul filtration. By the definition of a Koszul filtration this, in turn, implies that no Koszul filtration can exist.

items.title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
items.summary: This paper presents a computational model integrating transmural drug transport, smooth muscle cell contraction, nonlinear anisotropic material behavior, and residual stresses to investigate the effects of calcium channel blockers~(CCBs) on local stress distributions in atherosclerotic arteries. The balance of linear momentum is coupled with a three-dimensional reaction-diffusion equation for the drug transport. Smooth muscle contraction is modeled phenomenologically based on a chemo-mechanical model that incorporates the effects of stretch on intracellular calcium dynamics and calcium sensitization. A novel drug-tissue interaction model is proposed to capture the effects of CCBs on intracellular calcium and thus on smooth muscle contraction. Material parameters are identified by fitting to experimental data from the literature and finite element simulations are conducted on five exemplary atherosclerotic arterial geometries reconstructed from histological cross-sections. Simulation results show that although CCBs reduce the stresses in the media through reduced smooth muscle contraction, they shift load to the fibrous cap, whose stress increases in all five geometries (median of up to 28.9~kPa). This increase varies strongly between plaque morphologies and becomes smaller with lower smooth muscle tone before treatment, lower drug concentrations in the arterial wall and increasing axial pre-stretch. A blood pressure reduction of 10~mmHg already lowers it to a median of at most 3.8~kPa in four of the five geometries. Our findings suggest that CCBs may increase the rupture risk of vulnerable plaques with highly loaded fibrous caps under insufficient blood pressure reduction, which remains to be confirmed experimentally and clinically.

items.title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
items.summary: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other, while staying in a set of arbitrarily small Lebesgue measure. We give a full characterization of those subsets of a great circle that have this property on the sphere. We also show how the first mentioned result can be applied to obtain discontinuity results about the area swept by continuously moving objects.

items.title: On the role of dense ideals on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and associated $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets
items.summary: This article is a continuation of the work done in [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289] on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and concerns in addition the generalized version of Arbault sets, namely, $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets that is generated from this collection. A special class of ideals, namely, non-$snt$ ideals was introduced in 2023 ($snt$ stands for ``strongly non translation invariant") which was found to be effective in understanding ``Eggleston's dichotomy". Here we introduce another new class of ideals $\mathcal{H}$, a subclass of non-$snt$ ideals. We are able to establish a (new) necessary and sufficient condition for a $P$-ideal to be dense in Theorem 2.8 using the condition used to define the class $\mathcal{H}$ from which it follows that $\mathcal{H}$ coincides with dense $P$-ideals. Furthermore the important fact is established that the class of non-$snt$ ideals strictly contains the class of dense $P$-ideals. Subsequent investigation leads us to Theorem 2.14 which establishes the novelty of $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups for ideals coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$ and arbitrary arithmetic sequences showing that these are not even Arbault sets. Before all these, we also present a correct and revised proof of the main result of [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289], namely Theorem 3.8 (which had a gap in the proof). Finally we extend the results of [Das et al., Bul. Sci. Math. 179 (2022), 103157] for generalized version of Arbault sets and primarily show that for each ideal coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$, the class of $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets not only properly contains the class of classical Arbault sets but also a large subfamily of sets of absolute convergence while being contained in the class of weak Dirichlet sets.

items.title: Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
items.summary: Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. To improve the reliability of CL, this work establishes a mechanism allowing FE-occurrence to be verified a priori: We propose replaying a given training segment in the reference until data with finite excitation is collected online. Provided the training segment fulfills a certain off-line excitation test, FE then occurs in unknown, but finite time. Moreover, we provide an upper bound on the time-to-FE. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. The theoretical findings are verified on an academic simulation example.

items.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
items.summary: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $μ(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((κ^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixing. Specifically, via a weak-$(1,1)$ maximal inequality that follows from Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem, we uncover a stability mechanism in high-probability domains with respect to equilibrium. This enables straightforward localization to naturally arising domains of fast local mixing, and seamlessly fits broad local frameworks via Dobrushin contraction, Wasserstein contraction and local Harris' theorems. We develop the Dobrushin formulation.

items.title: On the enumeration of signatures of XOR-CNF's
items.summary: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$ with clauses $C_1, \dots, C_m$ over a set of variables $V$, a truth assignment $\mathbf{a} : V \to \{0, 1\}$ generates a binary sequence $σ_\varphi(\mathbf{a})=(C_1(\mathbf{a}), \ldots, C_m(\mathbf{a}))$, called a signature of $\varphi$, where $C_i(\mathbf{a})=1$ if clause $C_i$ evaluates to 1 under assignment $\mathbf{a}$, and $C_i(\mathbf{a})=0$ otherwise. Signatures and their associated generation problems have given rise to new yet promising research questions in algorithmic enumeration. In a recent paper, Bérczi et al. interestingly proved that generating signatures of a CNF is tractable despite the fact that verifying a solution is hard. They also showed the hardness of finding maximal signatures of an arbitrary CNF due to the intractability of satisfiability in general. Their contribution leaves open the problem of efficiently generating maximal signatures for tractable classes of CNFs, i.e., those for which satisfiability can be solved in polynomial time. Stepping into that direction, we completely characterize the complexity of generating all, minimal, and maximal signatures for XOR-CNFs.

items.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
items.summary: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

items.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
items.summary: It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-δ,δ]$ ($0<δ<π$) from its finite oversampling data $f(j),-n+1\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formulas have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. A recent sinh regularized formula achieved so far the best rate $$ O(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(π-δ)n)). $$ We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $ρ_{n,δ}$ satisfying $$ \frac{c_*}{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}\le ρ_{n,δ}\le \frac{C_*}{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}, 0<δ\leqπ, n\geq1, $$ where $c_*,C_*$ are explicit positive constants independent of $n$ and $δ$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words, $$ ρ_{n,δ} \asymp \frac{\sqrt{\tan\fracδ4}}{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-c_δ(π-δ)n), $$ where $c_δ$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,π]$ and $$ \lim_{δ\toπ^-}c_δ=1,\ \lim_{δ\to 0^+}c_δ=+\infty. $$ For one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $-n+1\le j\le 0$, we also obtain the sharp approximation order of optimally recovering function values on $[0,1]$: $$ ρ_{n,δ}^-\asymp \sqrt{δ/π}\sin^n(δ/2),\ 0<δ<π,\ n\ge1, $$ which improves the celebrated result of H. J. Landau on extrapolation of bandlimited functions.

items.title: Stability manifolds and resolutions of singularities
items.summary: In this article, we study descent and lifting of Bridgeland stability conditions along Verdier quotients. We give a torsion-pair criterion for lifting every stability condition on the quotient to a weak stability condition with a prescribed heart on the null category. When this criterion holds for every heart on the null category, the space of weak stability conditions with this massless subcategory is homeomorphic to the product of the stability space of the quotient and the discrete set of hearts of bounded $t$-structures on the null category. We apply these results to contractions of relative dimension one, resolutions of nodal varieties, and blowups of smooth projective varieties along smooth centers. For projective surfaces with ADE singularities, we identify the discrete factor through a simply transitive braid group action. When the minimal resolution is a K3 surface, every weak stability condition obtained by lifting a numerical stability condition from the singular surface is the limit of a continuous, quasi-convergent family of numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the resolution with the same heart.

items.title: Layer-wise Geometric Approximation Rates for Deep Networks
items.summary: Depth is widely viewed as a central contributor to the success of deep neural networks, yet standard approximation results typically give error bounds only for the final output of a network. Inspired by classical multiscale expansions and multigrade deep learning, we give depth a scale-dependent interpretation by constructing a single network whose intermediate readouts approximate the target at successively finer scales. For any $f\in L^p([0,1]^d)$ with $1\le p <\infty$ and any integer $N\ge2$, we construct a single network of width $3dN+2d+4$ with the same activation pattern in every hidden layer, using sine in the first two neurons and $\mathtt{ReLU}$ in the rest. For every $\ell\ge0$, the $L^p$ approximation error of the readout $Φ_\ell$ at layer $\ell+4$ is bounded by $(2d+1)ω_{f,p}(N^{-\ell})$, where $ω_{f,p}$ denotes the $L^p$ translation modulus of $f$. Under the Hölder condition $ω_{f,p}(t)\le Ct^α$ with $C>0$ and $0< α\le 1$, this estimate yields the geometric bound $(2d+1)C N^{-α\ell}$. More generally, if $ω_{f,p}(t)$ has a known upper bound that tends to zero as $t\downarrow0$, we obtain a stopping rule for adaptive depth selection. We can stop at the first depth where the error bound meets the desired tolerance and later append layers to meet a tighter tolerance while keeping all earlier maps and readouts fixed.

items.title: Triangle Tiling: The case $3α+ 2β= π$
items.summary: An $N$-tiling of triangle $ABC$ by triangle $T$ (the ``tile'') is a way of writing $ABC$ as a union of $N$ copies of $T$ overlapping only at their boundaries. Let the tile $T$ have angles $(α,β,γ)$, and sides $(a,b,c)$. This paper takes up the case when $3α+ 2β= π$. Then there are (as was already known) exactly five possible shapes of $ABC$ not similar to $T$: either $ABC$ is isosceles with base angles $α$, $β$, or $α+β$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2α,β,α+β)$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2α, α, 2β)$. We prove that the tile is rational (the ratios of its sides are rational). We then exhibit several families of previously unknown tilings. We also exhibit, for each shape, a Diophantine equation in $N$ and the parameters of the tile that must have a solution whenever there is a tiling of some triangle of that shape. By means of these Diophantine equations, some conclusions about the possible values of $N$ are drawn. We prove, for example, that there is no $N$-tiling with $N$ prime when $3α+ 2β= π$, for three of the five shapes; that question remains open for the shape $(2α,β,α+β)$ and for isosceles triangles with base angles $β$. These equations also imply that for each $N$, there is a finite set of possibilities for the tile $(a,b,c)$ and the triangle $ABC$. (Usually, but not always, there is just one possible tile.) For each of the five shapes, we give a construction method that works under certain sufficient conditions, but there remain values of $N$ that satisfy our necessary conditions and for which we do not know whether a tiling exists. All results have been formalized in Lean.

items.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
items.summary: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $Ψ_F$, the Boij-Söderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leqΨ_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $Ψ$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.

items.title: Numerical range of finite perturbations of a 2-periodic weighted shift
items.summary: In this note, we consider a weighted shift operator of weight sequence which is a finite perturbation of a 2-periodic weighted shift. We characterise the equality of the closure of its numerical range and its essential numerical range. We end up with some applications and comments.

items.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
items.summary: Let $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be induced by a normal $τ$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},τ)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.

items.title: Certified Nash Equilibrium Learning for Nonzero-Sum Jump-Diffusion Games: Policy Iteration and Off-Policy Q-Learning
items.summary: This paper establishes two model-free reinforcement learning methods for infinite-horizon N-player linear-quadratic nonzero-sum stochastic differential games whose drift, Brownian diffusion, and Poisson jump amplitudes depend on all players' controls. Control dependence in the diffusion and jump terms couples the players' simultaneous feedback updates. A verifiable certificate ensures that the partially model-free policy iteration map is contractive on an invariant closed ball centered at an admissible initial feedback profile. All feedback iterates are mean-square stabilizing, and the algorithm achieves local geometric convergence of feedback gains and value matrices to those associated with a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. The term certified refers to a verifiable convergence certificate that guarantees mean-square stability of all policy iterates and local geometric convergence to a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. To implement the policy updates from data, the off-policy Q-learning algorithm reuses the same behavior-policy data across iterations without requiring the system coefficients or jump intensity. Under quantitative persistence of excitation and a common initialization, exact population regression reproduces the policy-iteration sequence. The same local convergence guarantee therefore applies to off-policy Q-learning at the population level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the two proposed algorithms.

items.title: Central Limit Theorems and Network-Free Inference for Heterogeneous Spatial Autoregressions on Sparse Graphons
items.summary: Network dependence is widely regarded as a fundamental obstacle to inference: outcomes linked through a graph are not independent, the graph is rarely observed in full, and models for how dependence propagates are easily misspecified. We show that for a broad class of responses generated through a random network, the obstacle is smaller than it appears. We study a heterogeneous spatial autoregression on a sparse graphon, in which each node's response is a weighted average of its neighbors' responses with a node-specific, nonparametric coefficient plus a node-specific input, and we prove that sample means and smooth functions of vector means are asymptotically Gaussian down to average degree nearly logarithmic in the population size, allowing unbounded graphons with hubs and heavy-tailed inputs. The limiting variance interpolates exactly between two regimes according to the sampling fraction. When the observed nodes are a vanishing fraction of the population, the variance is the marginal variance of the response, the ordinary sample variance is consistent, and the usual $t$-interval is valid with no knowledge of the network. The proof averages over the graph rather than conditioning on it, isolating the behavior of the response through an exact identity for resolvents of Markov kernels and controlling the network noise by an Efron-Stein inequality; neither step requires the walk-by-walk covariance bounds of fixed-network analyses. Consequences for regression with node-level and network-derived covariates are derived.

items.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
items.summary: We reconstruct smooth cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution through classical interpolation of smooth plane conics from five distinct points, or four with their cross-ratio. If the quadratic coefficient map has rank three and the fixed cubic surface has trivial automorphism group, five polarized anti-invariant Jacobian factors of smooth Eckardt sections suffice, or four with their parameters. Both bounds are optimal. By contrast, in rank two we construct two-dimensional families of equivariantly nonisomorphic fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. The factor family also has an integral projective Lagrangian closure in an associated OG10 compactification.

items.title: Singular Global Compactness for Logarithmically Coupled \(p\)-Laplacian Systems
items.summary: We establish global compactness for logarithmically coupled p-Laplacian systems on RN, where p=N>4 and bounded positive potentials converge to positive constants at infinity. The finite-energy domain need not be closed under subtraction, obstructing direct profile subtraction. We develop a scalar localisation method using slowly expanding cutoffs and residual commutator estimates uniform in the regularisation parameter. As the regularisation vanishes, residual Palais-Smale sequences split into a solution of the original system and finitely many separating autonomous profiles, with a strongly vanishing remainder and splitting of the logarithmic densities. A converse construction characterises all levels of compactness failure. Applications include convergence of ground-state levels, a compactness-escape alternative for minimising sequences, and a directional response formula for the ground-state energy.

items.title: In-Context Estimation and Prediction for Parametric ODEs
items.summary: Transformers have demonstrated the ability to perform in-context learning, that is, to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without updating their parameters. Existing theory has largely focused on emulating gradient-based algorithms for convex statistical problems or establishing general function approximation guarantees without exploiting the underlying statistical structure. We study in-context parameter estimation and trajectory prediction for parametric ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where estimation is generally nonconvex. Under suitable identifiability and regularity conditions, we construct a transformer that estimates unknown system parameters from noisy trajectory observations through a two-stage approximate maximum likelihood procedure: a coarse search provides an initialization within a locally strongly convex region, followed by gradient descent with local linear contraction. For prediction, we compose this estimator with a neural approximation of the ODE solution map. We further show that, through parameter sharing, a single transformer can perform both parameter estimation and trajectory prediction simultaneously. For these constructions, we establish nonasymptotic guarantees and finite-pretraining oracle inequalities that separate errors due to finite pretraining data, finite context length, and finite-sized transformer approximation. Numerical experiments on linear and nonlinear ODEs further show that pretrained transformers can benefit from longer inference contexts without updating their weights.

items.title: Belavin--Drinfeld bivectors and Poisson deformations
items.summary: We study Belavin--Drinfeld Poisson bivectors $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ on $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(\mathbb{C})$ from the perspective of Poisson deformation theory. We prove that the log-canonical part $π_0$ of $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ is $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-log-symplectic if and only if the pair $(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)$ of Belavin--Drinfeld triples is aperiodic. In this case, we show that $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ is a maximal $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-invariant Poisson deformation of $π_0$, and we construct a $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-equivariant Poisson birational map between $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},π_0)$ and $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)})$.

items.title: Analytic Tools and Weighted Composition Operators on Paley--Wiener Spaces
items.summary: We develop a scale-explicit analytic framework for operator-theoretic problems on the Paley--Wiener spaces $B_σ^p$, $σ>0$, throughout the full range $0<p\leq\infty$. Using localized Paley--Wiener packets, we obtain sharp-order point-evaluation estimates, quantitative separation of distinct point-evaluation functionals, sampling estimates, and Carleson measure characterizations. As a principal application, we develop a comprehensive theory of weighted composition operators $W_{ψ,\varphi}:B_σ^p\to B_τ^q$, $0<p,q\leq\infty$, $σ,τ>0$. Boundedness forces every nonconstant symbol to be affine with real slope. A sharp dichotomy appears: when $p\leq q$, the weight is governed by the residual bandwidth $τ-σ|a|$; when $q<p$, the weight must also supply the missing integrability, with exponent $pq/(p-q)$, and boundedness coincides with compactness. We also obtain compactness criteria and essential-norm estimates, characterize differences of weighted composition operators via a no-cancellation principle for distinct symbols, and determine the connected and path-connected components of the corresponding operator spaces.

items.title: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in short intervals
items.summary: For any real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $α$ be any irrational number. We prove that there exist infinitely many $X$ such that for $Y=X^γ/2$ with $7/12<γ\le 1$ and $0<θ<\min \{(12γ-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there is a prime $p$ satisfying $$ \|αp\|<X^{-θ},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. In particular, if $α$ has a continued fraction expansion with bounded partial quotients, then this asymptotic holds for all sufficiently large $X$. Our result extends the admissible range of short intervals in the corresponding theorem of Baier and Roy from $2/3<γ\le 1$ to $7/12<γ\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals, and also improves the exponent $θ$ for $2/3\le γ\le 3/4$. The improvement is obtained by adapting a recent result of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwiłł on exponential sums over primes.

items.title: Odd faces as a parameter for maximum independent set in embedded graphs
items.summary: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for finding a maximum weight independent set in a graph embedded in a surface of bounded genus and with a bounded number of vertex-disjoint odd faces. In particular, we obtain an algorithm for graphs with an even-faced embedding in a torus and for planar graphs with a bounded number of odd faces, answering a question of Thomassé (2018) and a question of Choi, Gorsky, Kim, McFarland, and Wiederrecht (2025) respectively. We reduce the original problem to finding a minimum cost non-negative integer circulation with homology constraints in the dual of a certain double cover of the original graph.

items.title: Quasi-locality and weak containment for Roe algebras
items.summary: We establish two characterisations of Property A for discrete metric spaces of bounded geometry. Such a space has Property A if and only if its Roe algebra coincides with its quasi-local algebra, and if and only if the canonical map from its maximal Roe algebra to its reduced Roe algebra is injective. Both characterisations hold in the uniform and ordinary Roe settings. We also prove, without assuming Property A, that strong quasi-locality is equivalent to norm approximability by finite-propagation operators. In particular, the strongly quasi-local algebra always coincides with the Roe algebra. As applications, we show that a discrete group is exact whenever its full group $C^*$-algebra has the local lifting property, and that the maximal injective crossed-product functor agrees with the reduced crossed-product functor precisely for exact discrete groups.

items.title: Dimension-free spectral laws and the risk of spectral filters
items.summary: Spectral properties of the sample covariance are key to modern machine learning with high-dimensional data. Random matrix theory (RMT) supplies powerful tools; however, most classical results assume proportional asymptotics, where $d/n$ tends to a finite limit. In functional data analysis and kernel methods, a fixed infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is often the more natural setting for the observations, beyond the scope of proportional asymptotics. This calls for a dimension-free spectral theory for i.i.d. observations $\boldsymbol{x}_1, \dots, \boldsymbol{x}_n$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with trace-class population covariance $Σ$. Building on the dimension-free ridge regression analysis of Cheng and Montanari (2024), we establish two deterministic equivalents with explicit nonasymptotic error bounds. The first approximates the empirical spectral law $\widehatμ_n$ of the sample Gram matrix by a deterministic law $μ_n$. The second characterizes the conditional prediction risk of analytic spectral filters in linear regression. Previous sharp approximations to prediction risk in this setting have focused on ridge regression and closely-related problems. Our analysis covers a broader class of filters at the bulk scale, with an explicit user-friendly spectral stability condition to check. We apply our theory to power and critical spectral laws, and we recover the proportional regime. For prediction, we study (negative) ridge estimators, iterated ridge, and gradient flow. Mathematically, building on the idea of stochastic interpolation, we construct a deterministic backward path to interpolate the spectral parameter. The resulting bounds on resolvent and mixed-resolvent traces give mesoscopic approximations to the spectral law within the bulk and, by Cauchy's formula, deterministic equivalents for the prediction variance and squared bias of analytic spectral filters.

items.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
items.summary: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

items.title: A Fully Discrete Nonnegativity-Preserving FEM for a Stochastic Heat Equation
items.summary: We consider a stochastic heat equation with nonlinear finite-rank space-coloured multiplicative noise that admits a unique nonnegative solution when given nonnegative initial data. Inspired by existing results for fully discrete finite difference schemes and building on the convergence analysis of semi-discrete mass-lumped finite element approximations, a fully discrete numerical method is introduced that combines mass-lumped finite elements with a Lie-Trotter splitting strategy. This discretization preserves nonnegativity at the discrete level and is shown to be convergent under suitable regularity conditions. A rigorous convergence analysis is provided, highlighting the role of mass lumping in ensuring nonnegativity and of operator splitting in decoupling the deterministic and stochastic dynamics. Numerical experiments are presented to confirm the convergence rates and the preservation of nonnegativity. In addition, we examine several numerical examples outside the scope of the established theory, aiming to explore the range of applicability and potential limitations of the proposed method.

items.title: Topological classification of certain nonorientable 4-manifolds with cyclic fundamental group of order 2 mod 4
items.summary: The classification up to homeomorphism of closed topological nonorientable 4-manifolds with fundamental group of order 2 due to Hambleton-Kreck-Teichner can be used to classify a large set of 4-manifolds with $π_1 = \Z/2p$ for odd $p > 1$. It is plausible that this set comprises all homeomorphism classes of such 4-manifolds. This is done through a cut-and-paste construction, which is then used to calculate an extension of the Hausmann-Weinberger invariant for every cyclic group of even order and to produce 4-manifolds that are not homotopy equivalent to a connected sum and which need not be smoothable.

items.title: On the Milnor classes of local complete intersections
items.summary: In this work we study algebraic, geometric and topological properties of the Milnor classes of local complete intersections with arbitrary singularities. We describe first the Milnor class of the intersection of a finite number of hypersurfaces, under certain conditions of transversality, in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurfaces. Using this description we obtain a Parusiński-Pragacz type formula, an Aluffi type formula and a description of the Milnor class of the local complete intersection in terms of the global Lê cycles of the hypersurfaces that define it. We consider next the general case of a local complete intersection $Z(s)$ defined by a regular section $s$ of a rank $r$ holomorphic bundle $E$ over a compact manifold $M$, $r \geq 2$. We notice that $s$ determines a hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$ in the total space of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E^{\vee})$ of the dual bundle $E^{\vee}$, and we give a formula expressing the total Milnor class of the local complete intersection $Z(s)$ in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$.

items.title: Well-Balanced Schemes for Hyperbolic Kinetic Relaxation
items.summary: This paper introduces a novel class of well-balanced numerical schemes for hyperbolic systems of balance laws in 1D using the kinetic relaxation framework. Kinetic relaxation methods approximate nonlinear hyperbolic systems via a linear system of transport equations where nonlinearities are relegated to the source term. While these methods simplify the Riemann problem, they fail to preserve the discrete steady-state solutions of the original system because of the modified source term. We propose two distinct strategies to achieve the well-balanced property: a modified Finite Volume (FV) approach using well-balanced reconstruction operators and a well-balanced Semi-Lagrangian (SL) approach based on characteristic backtracking. Both methods ensure that the steady solutions of the original system remain invariant during the transport and projection steps. We demonstrate the efficacy of these schemes with first-, second-, and third-order accuracy using palindromic splitting techniques. Numerical results for Burgers' equation, the Shallow Water Equations with bathymetry, and the Euler equations with gravitational potential confirm that our relaxation schemes maintain steady states to machine precision while capturing complex transient dynamics.

items.title: Finite presentations for Thompson monoids
items.summary: Thompson's group $V$ was introduced in 1965 as one of the first examples of an infinite finitely presented simple group. The Higman-Thompson groups $V_{k, r}$ naturally generalize $V$; they exhibit many of the same interesting properties and have been extensively studied in the literature. Monoid theoretic analogues $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ of the Higman-Thompson groups were first considered by Thompson, and published many years later in work of Birget. The monoid theoretic analogue of the symmetric group is the full transformation monoid, in that every monoid is isomorphic to a submonoid of some full transformation monoid. The analogous role for inverse monoids is played by the symmetric inverse monoid. Birget's three monoids $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ are to $V_{n, r}$ what the full, and partial transformation monoids, and the symmetric inverse monoid are to the symmetric group. The second author and De Witt recently showed that $TV_{k, r}$ is finitely presented. In this paper we show that the remaining two monoids $PTV_{k, r}$ and $IV_{k, r}$ are also finitely presented.

items.title: Stabilization of finite-energy grid states of a quantum harmonic oscillator by reservoir engineering with two dissipation channels
items.summary: We propose and analyze an experimentally accessible Lindblad master equation for a quantum harmonic oscillator, simplifying a previous proposal to alleviate implementation constraints. It approximately stabilizes periodic grid states introduced in 2001 by Gottesman, Kitaev and Preskill (GKP), with applications for quantum error correction and quantum metrology. We obtain explicit estimates for the energy of the solutions of the Lindblad master equation. We estimate the convergence rate to the codespace when stabilizing a GKP qubit, and numerically study the effect of noise. We then present simulations illustrating how a modification of parameters allows preparing states of metrological interest in steady-state.

items.title: The Local Embedding Problem for Hardy Spaces of Dirichlet Series
items.summary: We solve the local embedding problem for Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. For every $2<p<\infty$, the global $\mathscr{H}^p$-norm controls the $L^p$-norm of a Dirichlet polynomial on every unit interval of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1/2$: $\sup_{θ\in\mathbb{R}}\int_θ^{θ+1}\left|P\left(\frac12+\mathrm{i}t\right)\right|^p\mathrm{d}t\le C_p\left\lVert P\right\rVert_{\mathscr{H}^p}^{p}$, where $C_p$ depends only on $p$, not on the interval or on the number and choice of primes occurring in $P$. The inequality was previously known at $p=2$ and, by taking powers, at every even exponent; it had been conjectured that these were the only positive cases above $2$. Together with the known counterexamples for $0<p<2$, our theorem shows that the embedding holds for finite $p$ exactly when $p\ge2$. The proof uses duality to control many critical-line evaluations together. A frequency decomposition isolates the contribution for which the relevant frequencies can nearly coincide. We estimate it by replacing the leading terms in the logarithms of the Euler factors with Gaussian variables, using the same variable for each prime at all evaluation points; the accumulated errors remain bounded. Comparison with a critical branching random walk and estimates for a finite-cyclic square function then give a bound independent of the number of prime variables. For $1\le p<\infty$, known equivalences also give the sharp range for the conformally invariant half-plane embedding, the reverse transfer of local Carleson-measure estimates, and boundedness of all characteristic-zero Gordon--Hedenmalm composition operators.

items.title: Approximating parametric suprema for constructible and power-constructible functions
items.summary: We prove that one may approximate parametric suprema of constructible and power-constructible functions using functions within the same class. This resolves a conjecture by Adiceam and Cluckers, which was posited after studying a question posed by Sarnak. We apply our result to prove that a certain subclass of Cexp-class distributions is tempered and to make uniform a bound concerning pushforward measures.

items.title: Infinite projections and failure of pure infiniteness in simple nuclear $C^*$-algebras
items.summary: We construct a separable, unital, simple, nuclear $C^*$-algebra in the UCT class such that every nonzero projection in its stabilization is infinite, while it contains a nonzero projectionless hereditary subalgebra. The construction gives a negative answer to the question whether infiniteness of all nonzero projections in a unital simple nuclear $C^*$-algebra implies pure infiniteness.

items.title: Exact Algorithms for Edge Deletion to Cactus
items.summary: We study two related problems on simple, un-directed graphs: Edge Deletion to Cactus and Spanning Tree to Cactus. Edge Deletion to Cactus has been known to be NP-hard on general graphs at least since 1988. We show improved exact algorithms for the former and a polynomial time algorithm for the latter.

items.title: Weak error of approximation of a Lévy-type process using dynamic cutting
items.summary: In this note we consider, on one hand, the implementation of the parametrix method for estimation of the distance between functionals $\Ee^x f(X_t)$ and $\Ee^x f(\widetilde X_t)$ of two Lévy-type processes $X$ and $\tilde X$. On the other hand, we estimate the weak error appearing by substituting small jumps by a (time-inhomogeneous) diffusion. Both methods rely on the time-dependent cutting procedure, designed to remove small jumps in a time-dependent way.

items.title: Simultaneous reconstruction of an obstacle and its wavenumber for the Helmholtz equation: a robust optimization approach
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a method to recover simultaneously the shape and wavenumber of an object from noisy radar or sonar measurements. The physical problem is modeled in a bounded domain with the Helmholtz equation and appropriate transmission conditions. The approach relies on a Kohn-Vogelius formulation of the inverse problem and uses Nesterov's accelerated gradient descent combined with shape optimization techniques. To address the robustness of the method with respect to measurement noise, we are looking to minimize a convex combination of the expected value and variance, which we achieve by using a Karhunen-Lo{è}ve expansion. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through twodimensional numerical experiments.

items.title: Orthogonal Vector-Valued Rational Functions with Applications in Rational Approximation
items.summary: We present two algorithms for constructing orthonormal bases of vector-valued rational functions with respect to a discrete inner product. \rev{Every pole is prescribed together with a tangential direction, which fixes the direction of the residue at that pole.} Building on the pencil formulation of the inverse eigenvalue problem for scalar rational functions by Van Buggenhout, Van Barel and Vandebril (2022), we show that, for functions with $k$ components, the recurrence relations are represented by a pencil of $k$-Hessenberg matrices, i.e., matrices with at most $k$ nonzero subdiagonals, \rev{and that the poles are the ratios of the entries on the $k$th subdiagonal. This extends the banded Hessenberg structure of orthogonal vector-valued polynomials to rational functions, and it replaces the semiseparable-plus-diagonal representation of Delvaux and Van Barel (2005), in which every pole belongs to a single component, by a pencil.} We derive an updating algorithm based on rotations and a Krylov-type algorithm \rev{that orthogonalizes a tangential rational Krylov subspace, and we compare their accuracy. Finally, we show that the lightning method and the AAA algorithm fit in our framework; for AAA, the barycentric weights follow from a singular value decomposition of a small block of the pencil.} The approximation of $\sqrt{z}$ on $[0,1]$ with exponentially clustered poles and sample points serves as a stress test for our methods.

items.title: Fiberwise criteria for Fourier--Mukai equivalences
items.summary: We prove fiberwise criteria for full faithfulness and equivalences of integral transforms between proper flat families of schemes over a separated Noetherian base. The kernels are bounded pseudocoherent complexes which are relatively perfect over each factor, and need not be perfect. A key ingredient is the calculus of mates, which controls the units and counits of adjoint integral transforms under base change. In particular, we give a complete argument for a fiberwise criterion of Hernández Ruipérez--López Martín--Sancho de Salas, and extend it to arbitrary separated Noetherian bases. As applications, we extend a result of Orlov on field extensions to singular varieties, and show that over a Noetherian local ring these properties can be detected on the special fiber.

items.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
items.summary: In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves. The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

items.title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
items.summary: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

items.title: Elections, Fractional Dichromatic Number and Domination in Tournaments and Digraphs
items.summary: The dichromatic number of a digraph is the minimum number of induced acyclic sets into which its vertex set can be partitioned. The fractional dichromatic number is its fractional relaxation. Bourneuf, Charbit and Thomassé showed that the domination number of a tournament can be bounded as an (exponential) function of its fractional dichromatic number. This naturally leads to the question of finding a polynomial bound. We show that this bound is linear. To do this, we show a connection between undominated sets in elections and dominating sets in tournaments with bounded fractional dichromatic number. Within this framework, we also connect the well-known question of the existence of small Condorcet winning sets in elections to domination problems in digraphs with fractional dichromatic number less than 2. Thus, we open a new path to investigating these popular open problems in social choice from the perspective of graph theory.

items.title: A necessary regularity condition for finite-time stopping of the string with dry friction
items.summary: We consider the one-dimensional wave equation with dry (Coulomb) friction, u\_{tt} -u\_{xx} + Sgn(u\_t )= 0, with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Whether every finite-energy solution stops in finite time has been open since 1978. We show that stopping in finite time is impossible whenever the initial slope or the initial velocity is unbounded: the space W 1,$\infty$ x L $\infty$ for (u, u t ) is invariant under the flow in both time directions, while stopped states are Lipschitz. In particular the answer is negative for general finite-energy data, and the open question is reduced to Lipschitz data.

items.title: Explicit cohomological transfer for Morita equivalent Lie groupoids
items.summary: It is well known that Morita equivalent Lie groupoids have isomorphic differentiable cohomology. At the cochain level, however, explicitly transporting a cocycle from one groupoid to a Morita equivalent one is less straightforward. We provide explicit formulas for such cohomological transfers in arbitrary degree. More precisely, for the pullback of a Lie groupoid along a surjective submersion, we construct an explicit cochain-level homotopy inverse to the natural pullback map. We first treat Čech groupoids, where the construction only involves a partition of unity, and then extend it to arbitrary surjective submersions, for which the extra choice of local sections is needed. We also show that the resulting operators preserve the complexes associated with $\mathcal{VB}$-groupoids, including homogeneous and $\mathcal{VB}$-cochains. As an application, we obtain explicit transfer maps for deformation cocycles of Morita equivalent Lie groupoids and recover the Morita invariance of deformation cohomology.

items.title: On the Green's functions and Martin boundary structure of a planar diffusion in a discontinuous layered medium
items.summary: We consider a two-dimensional diffusion process in a two-layered plane, governed by distinct covariance matrices in the upper and lower half-planes and by two drift vectors pointed away from the $x$-axis. We first analyze the case where the generator of the process is in divergence form, that is, when the flux is continuous across the interface. Then we extend the study to a broader class of processes whose behavior at the interface forms an oblique two-dimensional analogue of the skew Brownian motion. We provide a detailed theoretical analysis of this transient process. Our main results are as follows: (i) we derive explicit Laplace transforms of the Green's functions; (ii) we compute exact asymptotics of the Green's functions along all possible trajectories in the plane; (iii) We determine all positive harmonic functions, identifying the full and minimal Martin boundaries, which turn out to be distinct. The nonminimality of the Martin boundary is a noteworthy phenomenon for diffusions with regular coefficients. To obtain an analytical description of the process, we fully develop a three-variable version of the so-called kernel method by deriving and exploiting a functional equation involving unknown Laplace transforms of Green's functions and two known kernels $γ_+(x,y)$ and $γ_{-}(x,z)$. The introduction of independent auxiliary variables $y$ and $z$, associated with each half-plane, is a key idea.

items.title: Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for unramified maximal parahoric level
items.summary: We prove the Kudla--Rapoport conjecture for unramified unitary groups with maximal parahoric level structure. Our approach differs from the local proof of C. Li and W. Zhang. We reduce the conjecture to a global intersection problem using local-global compatibility. Then we apply an inductive procedure based on the modularity of generating series of global special divisors. This strategy follows the framework developed in the proof of the arithmetic fundamental lemma by W. Zhang and Mihatsch--Zhang and arithmetic transfer identities by Z. Zhang and Luo--Mihatsch--Zhang.

items.title: Full-Cover and Non-Overlapping Uni-domination in Graphs: Bounds and Complexity
items.summary: A vertex is uni-dominated by a set $S \subseteq V(G)$ if exactly one vertex of $S$ lies in its closed neighborhood, and the uni-domination number $\mathrm{ud}^*(G)$ is the largest number of vertices a single set can uni-dominate. The graphs admitting an efficient dominating set are those with $\mathrm{ud}^*(G) = n$. Hedetniemi and Rall asked for the largest constant $c$ with $\mathrm{ud}^*(T) \geq c \cdot n$ for every tree $T$ of order $n$. We answer their question: the constant is $4/5$, and a set attaining it can be computed in linear time. This set is moreover a dominating set. Recall that an efficient dominating set satisfies two requirements at once: it dominates every vertex, and it dominates no vertex twice. Our set satisfies the first one, which leads us to study $\mathrm{ud}^*$ under each of the two requirements separately, giving the Full-Cover variant $\mathrm{ud}^*_0$ and the Non-Overlapping variant $\mathrm{ud}^*_+$. The two behave very differently: on arbitrarily large graphs $\mathrm{ud}^*_0$ may remain bounded by a constant, whereas $\mathrm{ud}^*_+$ always grows with the order. We present bounds for both, and show that the associated decision problems are polynomial for constant thresholds and NP-complete for the thresholds $\lceil \sqrt[c]{n} \rceil$ and $4\sqrt{n}$, respectively, the latter even on split graphs. Finally, we show that neither of the two parameters bounds the other.

items.title: Relative Fourier--Mukai theory for algebraic spaces
items.summary: We study the variation of Fourier--Mukai equivalences in proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. For bounded pseudocoherent kernels, we prove that the equivalence locus is open and commutes with arbitrary Noetherian base change. To do so, we develop a theory of relative perfectness and relative quasi-perfectness for algebraic spaces. This includes a fiberwise criteria for integral transforms with nonperfect kernels. As an application, we construct an explicit autoequivalence for elliptic fibrations.

items.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
items.summary: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the Künneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

items.title: Zeta Functions of Polygonal Numbers: Analytic Continuation, Poles and Zero Scattering
items.summary: We study the Zeta functions associated with polygonal numbers, focusing on their meromorphic continuation, poles, residues, and trivial zeros. We then investigate the distribution of their nontrivial zeros. Under explicit hypotheses, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean real part of zeros in long height windows. The formula predicts convergence of this mean to 1/4 as the height tends to infinity. We also formulate a stronger concentration conjecture and examine numerical evidence for it.

items.title: Möbius-Pseudorandomness for Algebraic Circuits
items.summary: We define a notion of Möbius-pseudorandomness for integer sequences generated by multivariate polynomials computed by small and simple algebraic circuits. This mirrors a related definition of Kalai that concerns boolean functions computed by small boolean circuits. We then prove Möbius-pseudorandomness results for polynomials computed by algebraic circuits with few multiplication gates (of any depth), for polynomials with small-dimensional partial derivative space, and for the determinant and permanent. We conjecture that these results hold in general for polynomial-size algebraic circuits.

items.title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
items.summary: Let $\mathscr{E}=\{E_α\}_{α\in I}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$, indexed by a linearly ordered set $I$ with no greatest element. We call a nonnegative finitely additive $σ$-finite measure on the Borel $σ$-algebra of $G$ admissible if it takes finite values on the sets in $\mathscr{E}$ and these values are not bounded above. Every admissible measure $μ$ can be normalized to have total mass one by applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{μ(B\cap E_α)}{μ(E_α)}\right\}_{α\in I}$, defined for all sufficiently large $α$. We study invariant finitely additive measures obtained by normalizing admissible measures. We show that every invariant measure constructed in this way can be obtained by normalizing a measure of a special form. An example is given showing that not every measure of the type under consideration can be obtained by normalizing a countably additive measure. We obtain a generalization of the Yosida-Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $σ$-finite measures.

items.title: Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
items.summary: We show that curves of genus 10 which are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line provide counterexamples to Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves. This leads to a 9-dimensional family of explicit counterexamples to Green's Conjecture. We also show that the same curves provide counterexamples to the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture. Both Green's Conjecture and the Secant Conjecture are know to be true in the generic case, as well as in many other situations.

items.title: On a Problem of Kac concerning Anisotropic Lacunary Sums
items.summary: Given a sequence of integers $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfying $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty}\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge q > 1$, a scheme of real-valued weights $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$, and a function $f: \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$, it is a classical problem to determine whether \[ S_N(x):=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N} f(n_k x)}{ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N}^2}} \] converges to a normal distribution as $N \rightarrow \infty$. This question can be traced back to early works of Kac and Erdős and has since then been investigated. It is well known that the asymptotic behavior of $S_N$ is determined not only by the analytic properties of $f$, but also by the arithmetic properties of the sequence $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and by the subtle interaction between the two. In this article, we identify conditions on $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, $f$ and $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$ that can be regarded as minimal for a central limit theorem to hold for $S_N$. This addresses a question raised by Mark Kac [Ann. of Math., 1946].

items.title: A Local Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Dirichlet Boundary Control Problems
items.summary: In this paper, we consider control constrained $L^2-$Dirichlet boundary control of a convection-diffusion equation on a two dimensional convex polygonal domain. We discretize the control problem based on the local discontinuous Galerkin method with piecewise linear ansatz functions for the flux and potential. We derive a priori error estimates for the full as well as for the variational discrete control approximation. We present a selection of numerical results to demonstrate the performance of our approach and to underpin the theoretical findings.

items.title: On Mean Field Games with Focusing Logarithmic Local Couplings
items.summary: In this note we study the existence theory of classical solutions to a second order stationary discounted Mean Field Games (MFG) system with focusing logarithmic local coupling in one space dimension. We then show the convergence of classical solutions to the discounted stationary MFG system in the large discount/cheap control limit in the spirit of the work of Bardi--Cardaliaguet.

items.title: Sharp Bounds for the Nodal Measure of Clamped Plate Eigenfunctions in Smooth Domains
items.summary: We investigate measure estimates for the nodal sets of nonzero real eigenfunctions $u$ of the biharmonic operator, satisfying $Δ^2u=λu$ in $Ω$ with clamped boundary conditions $u=\partial_νu=0$ on $\partialΩ$. We establish the optimal upper bound of order $λ^{1/4}$ for the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of their nodal sets on general bounded connected $C^\infty$ domains. Our approach combines an enhanced annular Carleman estimate with propagation of mass along a finite chain of balls, these yield a doubling index bounded uniformly up to the boundary.Interior analyticity then gives the nodal measure away from the boundary. To estimate the measure near the boundary, we develop a subdivision argument using the boundary values of $Δu$ and $\partial_νΔu$. Estimates from these data reduce large doubling indices and control the nodal measure in the region associated with a selected child cube whenever both the doubling index of the parent cube and $rλ^{1/4}$ are bounded, where $r$ is the side length of the parent cube.

items.title: Borel--Serre Callias Classes and Cuspidal Localization
items.summary: We construct equivariant Callias classes on the Borel--Serre space of a Hilbert modular group and prove a Kasparov product formula. For torsion-free normal congruence subgroups and twists by powers $m_j\geq2$ of the holomorphic cotangent line bundles, we identify the image of the maximal higher index in the representation ring of the finite quotient with the equivariant index of the cuspidal Dolbeault operator on total forms. The comparison uses a Fredholm homotopy that separates an invertible noncuspidal block. As an application, we compute the $A_5$-equivariant index on the principal level-two Hilbert modular surface over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$ for all parallel powers $m\geq2$. The resulting class in $R(A_5)$ is $15$-periodic in $m$ and has virtual dimension four. We express this class as an alternating sum of Hilbert cusp-form representations and deduce dimension identities for the full Hilbert modular group.

items.title: Symmetric Chemical Reaction Networks: Realizations and Steady States
items.summary: We investigate symmetric chemical reaction networks and their steady states. From classical equivariant dynamical systems and network theory it is known that the mass- action ODE of any symmetric chemical reaction network is equivariant. For symmetries that permute the species, we prove that any equivariant mass-action ODE is realized by a symmetric chemical reaction network and construct a sparsest such realization. We apply the half-degree principle to show that a symmetric CRN that has a steady state also has one with few distinct coordinates.

items.title: Sharp angle estimates for second order divergence operators
items.summary: This article is about the (minimal) sector containing the numerical range of the principal part of a linear second-order elliptic differential operator defined by a form on closed subspaces $V$ of the first-order Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(Ω)$ incorporating mixed boundary conditions. We relate the angle of sectoriality and the $\mathcal{H}^\infty$-angle of realizations of the elliptic operator to two reference angles: the optimal angle of the $L^2$-realization and the optimal angle of the coefficient function. We thereby consider the operator in several scales of Banach spaces: the Lebesgue space, the negative Sobolev space, and their interpolation scale. For the latter two types of spaces, we rely on recent results regarding the Kato square root property. We focus on minimal assumptions on geometry, and we consider both real and complex coefficients, in particular aiming at explicit estimates built on readily accessible problem data. New results include an explicit estimate for the angle of sectoriality for the elliptic operator on $L^p(Ω)$ with complex coefficients without any assumptions on geometry, which reduces to the known sharp angle for real coefficients, a new estimate on the angle of the sector containing the numerical range of a linear, continuous and coercive Hilbert space operator, and an estimate on the $\mathcal{H}^{\infty}$-angle for the elliptic operator on $L^p(Ω)$ with real coefficients.

items.title: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in dimension ten contains the Fourier pair or three product bases
items.summary: With computer-assisted proofs that $\mathbb{C}^6$ admits at most three mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) now available, $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is the smallest dimension in which it is unknown whether a complete set of $d+1=11$ MUBs exists; only three MUBs are known. We prove that every triple of mutually unbiased product bases of $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^5$ is strongly unextendible: no vector is unbiased to all three bases. Consequently no set of four MUBs in dimension ten, and in particular no complete set, contains three product bases. This settles the case $d=2\times5$ anticipated by McNulty, Pammer and Weigert; it was known only for the Heisenberg-Weyl triple. The proof covers all ten equivalence classes with explicit Nullstellensatz certificates modulo one prime on $91$ charts of $\mathbb{P}^9\times\mathbb{P}^9$ for each class ($910$ in all), transferred to characteristic zero by a projective reduction lemma, together with an independent rank certificate for eight of the ten classes. We also prove that the pair formed by the standard and the Fourier basis of $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is contained in no set of four MUBs. Exactly $3040$ rays are unbiased to both bases (this confirms the count found numerically by Führ and Rzeszotnik), each of them is unbiased to at most eight of the others, and every triple formed by the pair and a third MUB is strongly unextendible. For this we certify $34,940$ cyclic $10$-roots in Krawczyk uniqueness boxes, decide unimodularity exactly through an involution, and prove completeness by a four-dimensional interval branch-and-bound obtained from the Chinese-remainder splitting $\mathbb{Z}_{10}=\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_5$.

items.title: A Polynomial Time Algorithm for Finding a Minimum 5-Partition of a Submodular Function
items.summary: Given a real-valued submodular function on a finite ground set, the minimum $k$-partition problem asks for a partition into $k$ nonempty parts minimizing the sum of their function values. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for $k=5$. The idea follows directly from the previous $k=4$ result, where there is precisely one obstruction for generalizing it to $k=5$. We show the special case can be handled by reasoning about a restricted family of $3$-partitions.

items.title: On Iwasawa invariants of modular forms with reducible and non-$p$-distinguished residual Galois representations
items.summary: Let $f$ be the ordinary $p$-stabilization of the weight-one Eisenstein series, where $χ$ is odd and $χ(p)=1$. Under a Gorenstein hypothesis on the cuspidal Hecke algebra, we prove a factorization of the even branches of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function of $f$ by evaluating a cup product of cyclotomic units via local reciprocity. The odd branches follow from the Eisenstein specialization formula of Fukaya and Kato with a minor modification for the exceptional character considered here. We then obtain results on the $μ$- and $λ$-invariants. On the algebraic side, we compute the Selmer characteristic ideals at $f$ and the Iwasawa invariants of the higher-weight specializations. For every nontrivial twist of $f$, the ordinary characteristic ideal is generated by the corresponding $p$-adic $L$-function. On the untwisted branch it has one additional factor, the cyclotomic augmentation parameter. Imposing the strict local condition at $p$ removes this factor. For higher-weight specializations coming from newforms of level prime to $p$, Kato's divisibility then gives the cyclotomic main conjecture after inverting $p$.

items.title: A Diffeological Construction of Singer's Universal Connection
items.summary: We provide a rigorous construction of I.M. Singer's universal connection, a natural connection on a bundle of paths associated to any manifold, using the theory of diffeology. Furthermore, we generalize the universal connection to the diffeological setting, which enables the reconstruction of diffeological principal bundles with connections from their holonomy representations, extending known bundle-reconstruction results into diffeology. In particular, any two diffeological bundle-connection pairs with conjugate holonomy representations must be isomorphic as bundles, with the isomorphism taking horizontal paths to horizontal paths. Finally, we show that reconstruction and holonomy are functorial and, for a fixed diffeological group $G$, form an adjoint equivalence between the category of smooth homomorphisms from based loop groups into $G$ and the category of pointed diffeological principal $G$-bundle-connection pairs, extending to the diffeological setting the known equivalences for manifolds and Lie groups.

items.title: A note on meromorphicity in infinite dimensions
items.summary: In this note we develop the notion of a meromorphic mapping between infinite-dimensional complex manifolds. We restrict ourselves with second countable Hilbert manifolds modelled on a separable Hilbert space.

items.title: Uniformly Positive Scalar Curvature on Manifold Interiors
items.summary: We obtain topological obstructions to the existence of a complete Riemannian metric with uniformly positive scalar curvature on the interiors of certain 4-manifolds using Seiberg--Witten theory. In particular, no punctured blowups of a homotopy K3 manifold admit complete metrics of uniformly positive scalar curvature. Further, let $X$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n$. We show that if $n=6,7$ and $\operatorname{Int}X$ admits a complete metric of uniformly positive scalar curvature, then $X$ admits a positive scalar curvature metric which is a product near the boundary. In dimension 5, an analogous result holds under additional hypotheses and after possibly changing the smooth structure on $X$. If $n=5,6,7$ and $\operatorname{Int}X$ admits a complete metric of positive scalar curvature, then $X$ admits a positive scalar curvature metric with minimal boundary. One ingredient is a new PSC deformation result.

items.title: Average character degree below 14/3
items.summary: We prove that a finite group with average irreducible character degree less than $14/3$ is solvable if it has no chief factor isomorphic to $A_5$. This answers a question of Aziziheris and Eivazzadeh.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions for nonautonomous pressureless gas dynamics
items.summary: We study the Cauchy problem for one-dimensional pressureless gas dynamics with a continuous positive transport coefficient $α(t)$ and a continuous nonnegative linear damping coefficient $σ(t)$, for every nonnegative locally finite Radon measure $ρ_0$ as initial density and every $u_0\in L^\infty(dρ_0)$ as initial velocity. A central contribution of this paper is a new and direct proof of uniqueness under the original assumptions of Huang and Wang. It is carried out on the generalized potentials, and the energy condition enters only through the vanishing of the velocity dispersion at the initial time. The proof applies on every finite time strip and requires neither finite mass nor finite moments. We then show that time-dependent transport and damping act on entropy solutions only through an effective time, so that the nonautonomous system is the homogeneous one observed on a time interval $[0,A_\infty)$. Together with uniqueness on strips, this yields a global entropy solution, unique in density and momentum at every time, for all such coefficients. We also show that the energy condition cannot be dropped, and that its defect equals the mass of an atom times the variance of the velocities into which it splits. As consequences, we obtain an explicit representation of the solution by a generalized potential, the Riemann solutions with delta shocks, and the vanishing-damping limit.

items.title: Irregular SLE(4) martingales and isomonodromic deformations
items.summary: We consider non-Fuchsian monodromy preserving deformations on a Riemann sphere. The associated isomonodromic deformation parameters on this surface comprise the positions of the singularities, together with the Birkhoff (spectral) invariants owing to the presence of irregular singularities.
