Our first main result is the derivation of the Loewner evolution of these isomonodromic deformation parameters. Using this result, we construct martingale observables for Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE(4)) processes in the presence of double poles. Geometrically, the expressions contain the pre-Schwarzian and Schwarzian of the Loewner evolution, arising from conformal covariance of the observable. Furthermore, we characterize these SLE(4) observables uniquely in terms of confluent BPZ equations of a CFT with central charge c=1.

items.title: Transfer Learning for High-dimensional Quantile Regression with Distribution Shift
items.summary: Information from related source studies can often enhance the findings of a target study. However, the distribution shift between target and source studies can severely impact the efficiency of knowledge transfer. In the high-dimensional regression setting, existing transfer approaches mainly focus on the parameter shift. In this paper, we focus on the high-dimensional quantile regression with knowledge transfer under three types of distribution shift: parameter shift, covariate shift, and residual shift. We propose a novel transferable set and a new transfer framework to address the above three discrepancies. Non-asymptotic estimation error bounds and source detection consistency are established to validate the availability and superiority of our method in the presence of distribution shift. Additionally, an orthogonal debiased approach is proposed for statistical inference with knowledge transfer, leading to sharper asymptotic results. Extensive simulation results as well as real data applications further demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed procedure.

items.title: On the regularity of branching loci for $\mathbb{Z}_2$-harmonic spinors
items.summary: We show that the branching locus of a $\mathbb Z_2$-harmonic spinor is smooth (resp. real-analytic) near every point of frequency $\frac{1}{2}$ for smooth (resp. real-analytic) ambient defining data. This partially strengthens the previous regularity results obtained by Clifford Taubes and Boyu Zhang.

items.title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
items.summary: We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor. As rational functions of the framing parameters, we determine the polar parts of these invariants by exploring the equivariant geometry of the Gieseker-Uhlenbeck map $\mathcal{M}(r,n)\to\mathcal{M}_0(r,n)$. We determine the polynomial part of these invariants by relating their large framing limits to the results \cite{ILPT} for the rank $1$ case, namely $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)$. The degree-$0$ invariants with one divisor insertion are evaluated by studying the combinatorics of multi-partitions. We also prove reconstruction results for invariants with multiple insertions. Under the assumption that the eigenvalues of the divisor operator are linearly independent as functions of the Novikov variable, these results determine the full genus $1$ theory from the one-divisor series and the genus $0$ divisor operator.

items.title: Long-time asymptotics of advection-diffusion of finite element differential forms
items.summary: This paper establishes global numerical analysis for the long-time behavior of Lie advection--diffusion of differential forms discretized by finite element exterior calculus (FEEC). For potential flows we prove a weighted Hodge decomposition implying convergence to harmonic forms of dimension equal to the Betti number, yielding a differential-form antidynamo theorem. For general advection, a mixed FEEC scheme is introduced and shown to preserve key structural properties: the dimension of closed stationary discrete $k$-forms is at least $b_k$. Under verified spectral-preservation assumptions (satisfied for small $h$ by spectral approximation and for arbitrary $h$ by a lowest-order exponential-fitting $M$-matrix discretization), discrete antidynamo theorems are obtained. In particular, on two-dimensional manifolds the numerical $1$-forms converge exponentially to a uniquely determined closed stationary form for every diffusion coefficient $η>0$, rigorously excluding spurious dynamo growth. The results guarantee that FEEC faithfully inherits the topological long-time asymptotics of the continuous system.

items.title: Presentation of Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local rings
items.summary: We obtain presentations of Borel subgroups of certain Chevalley groups and Kac-Moody groups of simply laced type. More precisely, we show that Borel subgroups of simply laced Chevalley groups over a commutative, unital ring (satisfying a minor technical condition), are the amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups, generalising a result of Tits over fields (different from $\mathbb{F}_2$). We moreover show that Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local Bézout domains also have a presentation as an amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups as soon as this holds for their rank 3 subgroups. In particular we deduce that Borel subgroups of simply laced Kac-Moody groups over a local Bézout domain (with residue field different from $\mathbb{F}_2$) have such a presentation if and only if they are of 3-spherical type.

items.title: Iterated Steiner symmetrization of convex bodies always converges in shape
items.summary: We prove that every sequence of iterated Steiner symmetrals of a convex body converges in shape. That is, every such sequence can be corrected by a sequence of rotations to achieve convergence in Hausdorff distance. Moreover, for a fixed corresponding family of subspaces, the same rotations can be used for every initial convex body, and their successive increments can be chosen to be square-summable.

items.title: On the Matlis duals of $\mathcal D$-modules in characteristic zero
items.summary: Let $R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ be a formal power series ring over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(R,k)$ be the ring of $k$-linear differential operators. We prove that if $\mathcal M$ is a nonzero left $\mathcal D$-module with $(0)\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(\mathcal M)$, then $(0)\in\operatorname{Ass}_R D(\mathcal M)$, where $D(-)$ denotes Matlis duality, without assuming holonomicity or finite generation over $\mathcal D$. As a significant consequence of this result, we establish the Lyubeznik--Yıldırım conjecture in equicharacteristic zero. We also obtain a criterion for the Matlis dual of a $\mathcal D$-module to be non-holonomic.

items.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
items.summary: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.

items.title: Summary Sufficiency in Simulation-Based Inference via Mutual Information
items.summary: Simulation-based inference (SBI) enables posterior estimation when the likelihood is intractable but data can be simulated from the model. For high-dimensional or variable-length data, SBI methods typically rely on low-dimensional summary statistics as conditioning inputs for posterior estimation, making their sufficiency crucial for accurate inference. Mutual information (MI) provides a natural information-theoretic characterization of sufficiency, quantifying how much parameter information a summary retains. However, these MI quantities are generally intractable in likelihood-free settings. Sui et al. (2026) estimate MI from a trained neural posterior using the Barber--Agakov (BA) lower bound, while discussing, but not computing, a Fisher-information upper bound. This makes the estimate ambiguous: a small lower bound may indicate either an insufficient summary or an inaccurate density estimator. We address this limitation with a tractable diagnostic that estimates the BA gap and reveals what the difference between bounds has actually measured. We extend the resulting sufficiency metric to observation-centered restricted data spaces, allowing simulations to focus on a neighborhood of the data while preserving the target posterior and enabling valid sufficiency comparisons between summaries. We illustrate the use of this diagnostic tool on a temporal epidemic-type aftershock sequence model by comparing learned and hand-crafted summary statistics for variable-length earthquake catalogs.

items.title: Orbifold Morse Handles I. Morse Indices and Isomorphism Classes of Ordered Handles
items.summary: We classify the Morse indices and ordered handles arising from nondegenerate critical points of smooth functions on effective orientable four-dimensional orbifolds. Let $ρ\colon G\to\mathrm{SO}(4)$ be a faithful representation of a finite group. Let $V\subset\mathbb R^4$ be the negative eigenspace of a nondegenerate Hessian that is invariant under $ρ(G)$. The splitting $\mathbb R^4=V\oplus V^\perp$ determines an ordered quotient handle. Two such ordered handles admit an orientation-preserving isomorphism if and only if their negative eigenspaces lie in the same orbit under $N_{\mathrm{SO}(4)}(ρ(G))$. We determine the possible Morse indices and the normalizer orbits for every family in the completed Du Val list.

items.title: On Pseudo-Effectivity and Volumes of Adjoint Classes in Kähler Families with Projective Central Fiber
items.summary: This paper is devoted to studying the deformation behavior of pseudo-effective canonical divisors and volumes of adjoint classes in Kähler families. Based on recent developments in the Kähler minimal model program, for flat families with fiberwise canonical singularities, we establish the global stability of the pseudo-effectivity of canonical divisors and uniruledness, assuming in addition that one fiber is projective, while the same conclusion for Kähler threefolds is also true without the projectivity assumption of the central fiber. For a smooth Kähler family whose central fiber is projective with a big adjoint class, we show that its volume remains locally constant. Finally, using the (relative) minimal model program for Kähler threefolds, we verify the deformation invariance of volumes of adjoint classes and plurigenera for smooth Kähler families of threefolds, thereby partially confirming Siu's invariance of plurigenera conjecture in dimension three.

items.title: Resolution of ladder representations
items.summary: Let $π$ be a ladder representation of $\mathbf{GL}_m(F)$, $F$ a non-Archimedean local field. We construct an exact sequence of costandard modules, indexed by a lower Bruhat interval of a symmetric group and graded by the length, whose Euler characteristic is the determinantal formula of Tadić and Lapid--Mínguez. This is an analogue of the dual Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand resolution. The proof is combinatorial, through Jacquet modules and the Bruhat order; we also interpret the coresolution as a Cousin complex on Zelevinsky's space, which extends it to the balanced representations of Lapid--Mínguez.

items.title: Infinite Euclidean Distance Discriminants
items.summary: We study infinite Euclidean distance discriminants of algebraic varieties, defined as the loci of data points whose fibers under the second projection from the Euclidean distance correspondence are positive-dimensional. In particular, these discriminants contain all data points with infinitely many critical points for the nearest-point problem. We present computer code that computes the infinite Euclidean distance discriminant, and use it to present numerous varieties with nonempty such discriminants. Moreover, we prove that for any data point, the fiber under the second projection is contained in a finite union of hyperspheres centered at that point. For curves, we include a complete characterization; their infinite Euclidean distance discriminants turn out to be affine linear spaces. Finally, we introduce and characterize skew-tube surfaces in three-dimensional space. By construction, these have a one-dimensional infinite Euclidean distance discriminant. We further demonstrate that many skew-tubes have significantly lower Euclidean distance degrees than generic surfaces of the same degree.

items.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with localized boundary data
items.summary: We study separation points for the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and boundary data compactly supported in space and time. We call a space-time point on the boundary and outside the spatial support of the data a separation point of a velocity component if the component takes both signs on sets of positive measure in every sufficiently small adjacent neighborhood. The main ingredient of the analysis is the explicit representation of the velocity and pressure in terms of the boundary data using the confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, under the regularity and unimodality assumptions, log-concavity of the temporal profile yields a unique separation time for the tangential component at every boundary point with \(|x_i|>1\), while the normal component has exactly two separation times for sufficiently large \(|x'|\). For every nonzero nonnegative temporal profile satisfying the regularity assumption, \(\partial_{x_n}^2w_n(x',0,\cdot)\) has a unique simple zero for \(t>1\) when \(|x'|\) is sufficiently large. We also obtain monotonicity and asymptotic behavior of the separation times and quantitative rates at which the corresponding normal derivatives vanish. For tangential data in \(n\geq3\), a separation time for the parallel component exists precisely when \(\partial_{x_1}R_1'ψ(x')>0\), with \(R_1'\) the first Riesz transform; log-concavity makes the separation time unique. For the remaining components, we also prove existence and uniqueness. In both cases, we derive asymptotic formulas involving spatial moments and the geometry of \(\suppψ\). We determine signs of tangential pressure derivatives and, for radial \(ψ\), establish uniqueness and asymptotics of their zeros.

items.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
items.summary: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.

items.title: On the Residue Sequence in Logarithmic Topological Cyclic Homology
items.summary: Algebraic K-theory participates in localization sequences, as first established by Quillen. We identify their boundary maps with the \emph{residue} map from logarithmic TC under the cyclotomic trace, resolving a conjecture of Rognes. As a consequence, we obtain e.g. a trace map from the K-theory of periodic complex K-theory to the logarithmic TC of connective complex K-theory. Moreover, we find that there exists a stable infinity-category C such that TC(C) realizes logarithmic TC for specific log structures, such as the natural ones on discrete valuation rings, connective complex K-theory, and truncated Brown--Peterson spectra. This provides evidence for the existence of a category of modules in the context of logarithmic geometry. We conjecture that such a category can be chosen to reflect additional structure on logarithmic TC, and we give evidence for this for discrete valuation rings.

items.title: Cassini ovals, translated polynomials, and the arithmetic of their discriminants and resultants
items.summary: For a polynomial $f$, $a>0$ and $b,ω\in\mathbb{C}$, consider the translate $J^{(a,b,ω)}f(z)=f(z/a)-ωf(b/a)$. We show that for $f(x)=(x^{2}-1)^{n}$ and $ω=\pm1$ every zero of $J^{(a,b,ω)}f$ lies on the Cassini oval $|z^{2}-a^{2}|=|b^{2}-a^{2}|$. We call these translates \emph{Cassini polynomials} and give their zeros explicitly, prove that the zeros for $ω=1$ and $ω=-1$ strictly interlace on each component of the oval, and evaluate their discriminants and resultants in closed form. We then prove the reduced monic polynomials $Q_{n}=a^{2n}J^{(a,b,ω)}f/(z^{2}-b^{2})$ factor into homogenized cyclotomic polynomials, satisfying $\operatorname{Res}(Q_{m},Q_{n})=(b^{2}-a^{2})^{2(m-1)(n-1)}$ for coprime $m,n$, and have discriminants governed by a Lucas sequence. We then prove a comparison principle: if $f$ is even or odd with all zeros in $[-1,1]$, $b\in\mathbb{R}$ and $|ω|\le1$, then every zero of $J^{(a,ib,ω)}f$ satisfies $|z^{2}-a^{2}|\le a^{2}+b^{2}$, and the symmetry hypothesis cannot be removed. As an application, every solution of $\det(A(P_{n})-λI)=F_{n+1}$, where $A(P_{n})$ is the adjacency matrix of the path on $n$ vertices and $F_{n+1}$ is a Fibonacci number, satisfies $|λ^{2}-4|\le5$. This disproves, for every $n$, a conjecture of Gullerud, Johnson and Mbirika that the real parts of these solutions are unbounded.

items.title: On Schroedinger operators with subordinated complex potentials
items.summary: We disprove a decade-old conjecture about a spectral stability of Schroedinger operators with potentials which are small in a subordination sense. Our counterexample is based on a complex perturbation of a critical attractive square well.

items.title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
items.summary: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

items.title: Sums of Integers with Small Prime Factors
items.summary: Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$, with $P^+(1)=1$. We prove that, for every $β>103/(256\sqrt e)$, there is a constant $C=C(β)>0$ such that every sufficiently large integer $N$ can be written as $N=a+b$, where $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and $$ P^+(a)\leq N^β,\qquad P^+(b)\leq(\log N)^C. $$ This strengthens Balog's result, which gives two $N^β$-smooth summands for $β>4/(9\sqrt e)$. The proof combines Balog's argument with convolution estimates that are uniform in the residue class.

items.title: Preserver Problems for Products of Operator Differences
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate surjective maps $Φ:\mathscr B(H)\to\mathscr B(H)$ preserving various operator quantities associated with products of differences, namely, $$α\big((Φ(A)-Φ(B))Φ(C)\big) =α\big((A-B)C\big) \quad \text{for all}~ A,B,C\in\mathscr B(H),$$ where $α$ denotes one of the following: the numerical radius, maximal numerical range, minimum modulus, surjectivity modulus, reduced minimum modulus, or spectral radius. Under suitable assumptions, we establish structural characterizations of these maps and determine their possible forms.

items.title: Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
items.summary: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $σ$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.

items.title: Vanishing Dissipation Limit to Planar Euler Shock for the Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$
items.summary: We prove the vanishing dissipation limit to a weak planar Euler shock for the full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The viscosity and heat conductivity are proportional to $\varepsilon$, with their ratio fixed. The conservative initial perturbation may depend on all three spatial variables and is assumed small only in the scaled $H^2 \cap \dot H^{-1}$ norm. No $L^1$ bound or zero-mass condition is required. For these data, we obtain a unique global strong solution and an energy estimate uniform in time and in $\varepsilon$. On every cylinder with a measurable transverse section of finite positive area, the $L^2$ error has an explicit leading term, yielding the sharp rate $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$. The remainder has order $\varepsilon^{3/2}$ times the scaled initial norm; both estimates are uniform for $t \geq 0$. If this norm tends to zero, convergence away from the shock front is uniform in time, including at $t=0$. The entropy production measures converge locally weakly to the measure carried by the Euler shock. Low frequencies are controlled by an entropy-weighted elliptic estimate. At second order, integration by parts in the pressure and viscous heating terms leaves at most two derivatives on the density, while third derivatives of velocity and temperature enter only through the time-integrated dissipation.

items.title: Group classification and equivalence of two classes of evolution equations of arbitrary order
items.summary: We revisit the group classification of the $(1{+}1)$-dimensional evolution equations $u_t=F(u_n)$ and $u_t+uu_x=F(u_n)$ of arbitrary order $n\geq2$, where $u_n=\partial_x^n u$, and describe the usual point equivalence groups of the two classes. We recover the known contact equivalences between the three second-order equations with seven-dimensional maximal Lie invariance algebras and extend the hodograph construction to points where $u_x=0$. For $n>2$, the dimensions of the contact symmetry algebras distinguish the two classes. We give reciprocal transformations linking the two classes at order three and formulate a nonlocal classification problem. We also classify the extensions of the Lie invariance algebra of the Burgers equation in a wider class of Galilei-invariant equations.

items.title: Policy Iteration Convergence for Exploratory Two-State Mean-Field Control Problems
items.summary: This paper studies the theoretical policy iteration convergence for two-state mean-field control (MFC) problems with Wright--Fisher common noise under entropy regularization. The population dynamics lead to a degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation of Kimura type. After an arcsine transformation, the degeneracy becomes a singular Bessel drift whose coefficients and weights depend on the feedback stochastic policy. This policy dependence prevents a direct application of estimates for a fixed operator. We establish weighted Sobolev estimates and Hölder embeddings uniformly over the admissible policy class. Combining these estimates with logarithmic entropy bounds and boundary estimates that remain valid when the policy changes, we prove the well-posedness, monotone improvement and convergence of policy iteration to the optimal solution. We also establish the convergence to the original MFC problem when the entropy parameter $λ$ tends to zero. Both the regularization error and the performance loss of the regularized optimal policy are bounded by $O(λ(1+|\lnλ|))$ in a weighted Hölder norm. An epidemic containment example of MFC is presented to illustrate the policy iteration convergence and the vanishing entropy convergence.

items.title: Néron Functions on Jacobians of Odd-Degree Hyperelliptic Curves
items.summary: We express Néron functions on Jacobians of odd-degree hyperelliptic curves of arbitrary genus in terms of admissible pairings, using the pullback of the theta divisor via a generalized Abel--Jacobi morphism. Over non-archimedean local fields, we relate Néron functions to local Néron pairings on the curve and, moreover, deduce a comparison between unramified $p$-adic Néron functions and unramified local Coleman--Gross height functions. Furthermore, we decompose the Néron function into an intersection term $I$ and a Green function term $T$, and compute $T$ for specific semistable reduction types. We compare our decomposition with other decompositions in the literature.

items.title: Intersection theory and Chern classes on normal varieties II
items.summary: We prove a uniform bound linear in the rank for the local correction terms in the Riemann--Roch formula for reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We also establish the usual tensor and symmetric-power formulas for second Chern characters and prove Wahl's asymptotic Riemann--Roch conjecture and its higher-rank generalization. These results yield second Chern classes of reflexive sheaves on arbitrary normal projective varieties, compatible with pullback by finite surjective morphisms. We characterize their discriminants as infima of normalized discriminants of compatible vector bundles on smooth alterations. As applications we prove Bogomolov's inequality, effective restriction and boundedness theorems on normal projective varieties, a Miyaoka-type inequality, and a Segre-class criterion for bigness of reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces.

items.title: Explicit Tartakowsky theorem and universality criterion sets over totally real number fields
items.summary: We prove an explicit version of Tartakowsky's theorem over all totally real number fields. Namely, a positive definite integral lattice of rank at least five represents every totally positive integer that it represents locally, provided that the norm of the integer exceeds an explicit bound, exponential in powers of the volume of the lattice and of the discriminant of the field. As an application, we give explicit criterion sets for universal quadratic forms over all but finitely many real quadratic fields. Finally, we determine the minimal criterion sets for an infinite family of real quadratic fields.

items.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
items.summary: We prove that $G$-Fano threefolds which are given by the blow-up of a smooth quadric along a twisted quartic curve are $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. We also prove that the action of $G$ is linearisable if and only if $G$ does not contain a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.

items.title: Mixed-Precision Lloyd's Algorithm for k-means Clustering
items.summary: As low-precision arithmetic becomes more widely available on modern hardware, we develop mixed-precision variants of Lloyd's algorithm for k-means clustering, with a family of mixed-precision kernels for Euclidean distance computation as the main ingredient. These kernels are guided by rounding-error analysis and use a simple reliability test to decide whether the expanded distance formula can be evaluated safely with low precision or a higher-precision correction by the direct distance formula is required. Thus, most distance computations can be carried out with low precision, while high-precision arithmetic is used selectively when cancellation may lead to a loss of accuracy. We evaluate the proposed methods on large-scale distance-computation benchmarks, synthetic clustering problems, and image-segmentation tasks. The experiments verify that the mixed-precision kernels on GPUs can substantially improve performance while retaining accuracy and convergence behavior of higher-precision baselines. In particular, our implemented distance computation in CUDA achieves speedups of up to $4\times$ over the \texttt{PyTorch} baseline that evaluates the expanded formula in FP64 on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, with overall maximum relative errors of order $10^{-3}$, while providing increased numerical robustness in cancellation-prone calculations. The resulting mixed-precision kernels show efficiency for clustering and image segmentation, although the observed gains depend on factors such as feature dimension, and number of clusters. The mixed-precision kernels offer a favorable trade-off between performance and accuracy for clustering, and suggest that similar ideas may be beneficial for other distance-based machine learning methods.

items.title: Online Neural Network Training via Closed-Loop Model-Free Tracking Control: An Empirical Study
items.summary: Training artificial neural networks predominantly relies on offline, gradient-based backpropagation algorithms. In contrast, biological circuits process and retain information through decentralized, continuous-time adaptation. In this work, we explore an online, gradient-free learning methodology by formulating the tuning of synaptic weights as a closed-loop trajectory tracking problem driven by model-free control principles. Rather than performing global optimization across static parameters, decentralized controllers adjust synaptic interactions in real-time using solely local input-output tracking errors. We present an exploratory benchmark neural architecture, whose purpose is to assess the dynamic resilience of the proposed approach, particularly in tracking target outputs and adapting to abrupt non-stationarities and structural perturbations (such as topological changes or dynamic dropout) without requiring offline retraining. This empirical preliminary study provides a proof-of-concept for control-theoretic learning paradigms and outlines the foundation for scalable, dynamically evolving connectome frameworks.

items.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
items.summary: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra when $2 \in R^\times$, costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $π\colon S \to R$ with $π(1) = 1$. In particular, the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over these fields is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ when $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. An implementation for the standard tower over $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{F}_q$ for $q = p^k$ with $p \le 2^{31}-1$ an odd prime and $k \le 12$ is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface pyfastcd, available on PyPI. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method over $\mathbb{R}$, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$ for both single and batched products and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication.

items.title: On the optimality of the HOD dichotomy
items.summary: In the first part of the manuscript, we establish several consistency results concerning Woodin's HOD hypothesis and large cardinals around the level of extendibility. First, we prove that the first extendible cardinal can be the first strongly compact in HOD. Second, answering a question in \cite{CFH}, we prove that the first supercompact cardinal can be the first strongly compact, non supercompact, of HOD. We extend a former result of Woodin by showing that under the HOD hypothesis the first extendible cardinal is $C^{(1)}$-supercompact in HOD. We also show that the first cardinal-correct extendible may not be extendible, thus answering a question by Gitman and Osinski \cite[\S9]{GitOsi}. In the second part of the manuscript, we discuss the extent to which weak covering can fail below the first supercompact cardinal $δ$ in a context where the HOD hypothesis holds. Answering a question of Cummings et al. \cite{CumFriGol}, we show that under the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis there are many singulars $κ<δ$ where $\mathrm{cf}^{\mathrm{HOD}}(κ)=\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ and $κ^{+\mathrm{HOD}}=κ^{+}.$ In contrast, we also show that the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis is consistent with $δ$ carrying a club of $\mathrm{HOD}$-regulars cardinals $κ$ such that $κ^{+\mathrm{HOD}}<κ^{+}$. Finally, we close the manuscript with a discussion about the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis and $ω$-strong measurability.

items.title: Stationarity with Occasionally Binding Constraints
items.summary: This paper studies a class of multivariate threshold autoregressive models, known as censored and kinked structural vector autoregressions (CKSVAR), which are notably able to accommodate series that are subject to occasionally binding constraints. We develop a set of sufficient conditions for the processes generated by a CKSVAR to be stationary, ergodic, and weakly dependent. Our conditions relate directly to the stability of the deterministic part of the model, and are therefore less conservative than those typically available for general vector threshold autoregressive (VTAR) models. Though our criteria refer to quantities, such as refinements of the joint spectral radius, that cannot feasibly be computed exactly, they can be approximated numerically to a high degree of precision.

items.title: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy
items.summary: We construct an autonomous Lipschitz fast dynamo on the flat three-torus whose particle flow has zero topological entropy and whose ideal induction equation has no exponential growth. We perform a multiscale construction starting from the Ponomarenko flow. For every sufficiently small positive magnetic diffusivity, the induction operator on $\mathbb{T}^3$ has an eigenvalue with real part bounded below by a positive constant independent of the diffusivity. A corresponding non-zero real-valued magnetic field satisfies an exact exponential growth law in $\mathrm{L}^2$. For the same velocity field, every solution of the ideal problem grows at most linearly in $\mathrm{L}^2$. Moreover, the particle flow and its inverse have Lipschitz constants growing at most linearly in time and thus zero topological entropy. The velocity field is real-valued, divergence-free, differentiable everywhere and smooth away from one circle, but is not $\mathrm{C}^1$.

items.title: Design of an optimal positive state observer for a diffusion system with point observation
items.summary: An optimal state observer design problem for a diffusion system with point observation is studied. As the considered system is positive, the analysis takes into account this additional condition. The solution of the optimization problem is derived by means of a discretization approach, which consists in considering the analogous problem adapted for a spatially discretized version of the pure diffusion system.

items.title: A Chvátal--Erdős type condition for supereulerian digraphs with $α_{2}=4$
items.summary: A digraph is \textbf{supereulerian} if it contains a spanning closed trail. Let $α_2(D)$ denote the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing no 2-cycle. In this paper, we study the supereulerianity of digraphs with arc-strong connectivity at least 2. We identify a family $\mathcal H$ of nonsupereulerian 2-arc-strong digraphs and prove that every 2-arc-strong digraph $D$ with $α_2(D)\leq 4$ is supereulerian if and only if $D\notin\mathcal H$. In particular, every digraph $D$ satisfying $α_2(D) \le 4$ and $λ(D) \ge 3$ is supereulerian.

items.title: Stochastic control representations for extremal solutions of HJB Dirichlet problems with measurable coefficients
items.summary: We study stochastic control problems for uniformly elliptic controlled diffusions on bounded domains whose coefficients are merely measurable in the state variable and whose drift is dominated by an $L_d$-function. The associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) Dirichlet problems may have more than one $L_p$-viscosity solution, so that the equation alone does not determine the value function. We show that the control problem selects the minimal solution: for all $p$ in a range $(d_0,d)$ determined by the spatial dimension, the ellipticity constant and the drift bound, the value function is the minimal $L_p$-viscosity supersolution of the HJB Dirichlet problem. In particular, every continuous $L_p$-viscosity supersolution bounds the optimal cost from above, which yields a one-sided verification theorem without regularity assumptions. We further prove the existence of optimal relaxed control rules for running costs dominated by an $L_p$-function, and the lower semicontinuity of the value function under perturbations of the coefficients. An example shows that upper semicontinuity may fail even when the coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in the control variable and the approximating coefficients are smooth, so that regularization may overestimate the optimal cost. The proof approximates arbitrary supersolutions from below by Sobolev supersolutions of HJB equations whose coefficients are modified only on sets of vanishing measure, and passes to the limit by means of Krylov estimates and martingale problem techniques.

items.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
items.summary: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.

items.title: A Spectral Framework for Closed-Form Relative Density Estimation
items.summary: We propose a closed-form spectral framework for relative log-density estimation in linearly parameterized probabilistic models, including unnormalized and conditional models. This is achieved by representing the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence as an integral of weighted chi-squared divergences, converting KL estimation into a family of least-squares problems. We derive an explicit spectral formula based only on first- and second-order feature moments, yielding closed-form estimators of both divergences and log-density potentials for fixed features. The framework extends to a broad class of $f$-divergences and can be combined with kernelization or feature learning with neural networks (with then only a closed form for the last layer). We prove convergence guarantees for the resulting estimators and empirically compare them on synthetic data with optimization-based variational formulations, including logistic and softmax regression for normalized conditional models.

items.title: The random analyst
items.summary: Modern data-analysis pipelines increasingly involve searching among candidate analyses before reporting an estimate. We investigate the replicability of the resulting conclusions by studying independent repetitions of the entire search-and-report procedure on new samples. Can the reported estimates become increasingly similar across studies while remaining systematically displaced from the scientific target? We first show that this can happen in a simple Gaussian model. Although every prespecified candidate estimator is unbiased and consistent, searching over exponentially many candidates within each study yields a selected estimator converging to a limit different from the target, a selection-induced pseudotruth. Across independent repetitions, the reported estimates thus become replicable but systematically inaccurate, while the selected candidates differ with probability tending to one. We then study dependent Gaussian candidates, including marginal regression coefficients, and show that Gaussian width governs the displacement, which persists when squared width is of the same order as sample size. Metric entropy and generic chaining reveal that the effective complexity of the search is determined by the geometry of statistically distinguishable analyses rather than by their nominal number. Large-deviation arguments further extend the phenomenon beyond Gaussian models. Numerical agreement between independent studies therefore need not indicate either a stable analytical path or proximity to the scientific target.

items.title: Percolation Markov Decision Processes
items.summary: We study Percolation Markov Decision Processes (PMDPs), where the decision maker repeatedly moves a token through the d-dimensional integer lattice with deterministic transitions and random payoffs assigned to the edges. Payoffs are revealed before the beginning of the decision process and the decision maker aims to maximize the average accumulated payoff over a fixed horizon. First, we address general asymptotic control-theoretic questions by proving the existence of the uniform value and 0-optimal strategies. Furthermore, we examine the structural properties of optimal strategies: we establish the existence of stationary 0-optimal strategies for a class where the token moves in a fixed direction independent of the player's actions, and we provide low-dimensional examples to illustrate their complexity. Moreover, we introduce a dimensional lifting property that allows PMDPs to be approximated by lower-dimensional PMDPs, offering a representation of the approximation of critical probability thresholds in percolation theory via PMDPs.

items.title: On statistical and causal models associated with acyclic directed mixed graphs
items.summary: Causal models in statistics are often described using acyclic directed mixed graphs (ADMGs), which contain directed and bidirected edges and no directed cycles. This article surveys various interpretations of ADMGs, discusses their relations in different sub-classes of ADMGs, and argues that one of them---the noise expansion (NE) model---should be used as the default interpretation. Our endorsement of the NE model is based on two observations. First, in a subclass of ADMGs called exogenously bidirected graphs (which retain most of the good properties of directed acyclic graphs and bidirected graphs), the NE model is equivalent to many other interpretations, including the ordinary Markov and nested Markov models. Second, the NE model for an arbitrary ADMG is exactly the union of the observed margins of NE models on its exogenously bidirected expansions. This property is referred to as completeness, as it shows that the model does not commit to any specific latent variable explanation. In proving the nested Markov property, we also develop an ADMG-based theory for causality and its complete characterization via the potential outcome calculus. Finally, we compare the NE model with the closely related but different interpretation of ADMGs as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with latent variables that is commonly used in the literature. We argue that the ``latent DAG'' interpretation is mathematically unnecessary, makes obscure ontological assumptions, and discourages practitioners from deliberating over important structural assumptions.

items.title: Finite-Step Algorithms for Input-Constrained Control Barrier Function-Based Safety Filters
items.summary: Control barrier function (CBF) safety filters commonly rely on quadratic programs (QPs) to modify nominal control inputs while satisfying safety constraints. For safety-critical applications, however, the solution must be computed reliably under actuator limitations and with predictable computational effort. General-purpose QP solvers typically rely on numerical convergence criteria, which do not directly provide finite bounds on algorithmic steps or distinguish solver failure from mathematical infeasibility. This paper considers CBF-QPs with a single affine safety constraint, componentwise input bounds, and diagonal quadratic weights. Exploiting the established scalar dual structure of continuous quadratic knapsack problems, we obtain a necessary and sufficient pointwise feasibility condition and an exact breakpoint-based solution procedure. The algorithm requires at most 2n positive breakpoint events for n inputs, reducing to at most n events when the nominal input is admissible. In the latter case, an exact saturation--redistribution algorithm computes the optimal solution in at most n passes. We further describe how the structured solution can be combined with verified floating-point constraint evaluation to distinguish certified feasible commands, certified infeasibility, and unresolved numerical cases. The resulting framework provides an exact and computationally predictable solution procedure for a practically relevant class of input-constrained CBF safety filters.

items.title: Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
items.summary: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, Øbro, Fujita and the first author. The proof was found using ChatGPT 6.1.

items.title: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
items.summary: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and in practice behaves like an accelerated method. This led to the conjecture that it is uniformly accelerated on strongly convex functions as well. The conjecture is false. Consider exact subspace methods whose memory is a window of recent gradients and steps plus finitely many fixed cumulative sums. Uniform acceleration then requires either a window whose length grows as the square root of the condition number or a sum that forgets at a rate of at least the order of the inverse square root. For one filter pair with a fixed factor and a bounded window this scale of forgetting is necessary and sufficient up to constants. SESOP remembers too much and the plane form of conjugate gradients too little: neither is uniformly accelerated, even on infinitely differentiable functions that are quadratic near the minimizer. A short window, in contrast, converges locally quadratically over blocks of steps when the Hessian is Lipschitz near the minimizer and equals a multiple of the identity plus a low-rank term there. Pairs of geometric filters created at fixed times give a uniformly accelerated method with logarithmic memory and no problem constants, also with inexact subproblems. A single pair with a smoothly adapted factor needs two vectors and is accelerated up to a prefactor polynomial in the condition number.

items.title: Centralizers in Catalan Monoids
items.summary: Fix a chain $X_n=\{1<\cdots<n\}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. The Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_n$ consists of all decreasing and order-preserving transformations of $X_n$, with function composition as the operation. For $β\in\mathcal{C}_n$, its centralizer is $C(β)=\{α\in\mathcal{C}_n:αβ=βα\}$. We characterize the elements of $C(\varepsilon)$, $C(μ)$, and $C(β)$, where $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is an idempotent, $μ\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a nilpotent, and $β\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a general element. For an idempotent $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we derive formulas for the cardinality of $C(\varepsilon)$, as well as formulas for the numbers of idempotents and nilpotents of $C(\varepsilon)$. We relate indexing sets arising in these formulas to Dyck paths and Narayana numbers. For a nilpotent $μ\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we present algorithms that construct $C(μ)$, its subset of idempotents, and its subsemigroup of nilpotents, thereby determining their cardinalities. We also describe the nilpotents whose centralizers consist only of idempotents, of nilpotents together with the identity, or of nilpotents and idempotents. We extend these descriptions to arbitrary elements of $\mathcal{C}_n$. To obtain our results, we represent $β\in\mathcal{C}_n$ as a sequence $\langle T_1,\ldots,T_m\rangle$ of rooted trees. The sets of vertices of the trees form a partition of $X_n$. Each tree is level-ordered, which means that it can be drawn in such a way that moving from the root down, level by level, from left to right at each level, we pass through an increasing sequence of consecutive elements of $X_n$.

items.title: Stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients and unbounded drift
items.summary: We consider controlled SDEs with measurable coefficients, a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient and an $L_d$-drift. In this framework we investigate the relationship among value functions, PDEs, and operator semigroups. First, for a cost with an infinite time horizon on a bounded domain, we identify the value function as an $L_{d_0}$-viscosity solution to an HJB equation and we establish quantitative regularity estimates. The constant $d_0 \in (d/2, d)$ only depends on the space dimension $d$, the ellipticity constants of the diffusion coefficient and the $L_d$-bound of the drift. To illustrate applications of these results, we provide a uniqueness theorem under an additional assumption on the diffusion coefficient, showing a stochastic representation, and we discuss stability of value functions. Second, we consider a cost with a finite time horizon, terminal and running terms, assuming an $L_{d + 1}$-drift. We show that the value function indexed over the terminal cost is a nonlinear semigroup on $C_b (\mathbb{R}^d)$ and we establish a regularization by noise effect, which shows that the semigroup regularizes lower semicontinuity to local Hölder continuity. We also establish quantitative regularity estimates for the semigroup that are local in time and global in space. Lastly, under an additional $L_{d + 2, loc}$-assumption on the drift, we relate the semigroup to a parabolic PDE, showing that the associated value function is an $L_{d + 1}$-viscosity solution. Our proofs of the regularity of the value functions, the $C_b$-Feller property of the semigroup and its regularization by noise effects are based on a strong Markov selection principle and analytic estimates for linear diffusions that were recently established by N. V. Krylov in a series of papers. We highlight that our method covers frameworks without uniqueness of the controlled SDEs, as well as the associated PDEs.

items.title: Boundedness properties of bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate mapping properties on Lebesgue spaces of bilinear Fourier integral operators (FIOs) with complex phases. Indeed, we provide for bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases boundedness theorems for the corresponding Seeger-Sogge-Stein orders, including the endpoint estimates. Our results extend the same boundedness property in the case of real-valued phases proved by Rodriguez-López, Rule, and Staubach, and provide the bilinear version for the linear one proved earlier by Ruzhansky for phases of positive type. Also, our Seeger-Sogge-Stein theorem for bilinear operators with complex phases cannot be directly deduced from its real counterpart. A new approach used in this article consists of providing directly the boundedness theorems on Lebesgue spaces without the use of the multilinear Fefferman-Stein interpolation theorem. For this, a maximal function theorem due to Bourgain is applied. As a byproduct, we also consider transference boundedness theorems of FIOs with complex phases from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to the torus $\mathbb{T}^n\equiv \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ and then, we provide new criteria for the boundedness of Fourier integral operators on the torus with complex phases (Fourier series operators in the sense of Ruzhansky and Turunen).

items.title: Segregated normalized solutions for a nonlinear Schrödinger system with two mass constraints
items.summary: We study a two-component nonlinear Schrödinger system with two prescribed positive $L^2$ masses and a fixed competitive coupling $β<0$, for $N=1,2,3$ and $4\le p<2^*$. We first consider families whose peak heights diverge and whose components converge uniformly to zero away from disjoint finite peak sets. For such families, we prove that both Lagrange multipliers tend to $-\infty$ and that the mass of each component concentrates at its own peaks. We also construct positive multi-peak solutions near prescribed nondegenerate critical points of the respective potentials and compute the leading displacement of each peak. The target frequencies may grow at different rates, provided that $Λ_*\to\infty$ and $\log(2+Λ^*)=o(\sqrt{Λ_*})$, where $Λ_*$ and $Λ^*$ denote their minimum and maximum. In the $L^2$-noncritical case, the first frequency correction is minus the average potential at the prescribed points. In the $L^2$-critical case, the leading mass term is independent of the frequencies. For each component, we compute the mass correction of order \(λ_i^{-2}\) in terms of the sum of the Laplacians of its potential at the prescribed points. When both sums are nonzero, these corrections determine the leading-order asymptotics of the two frequencies and the side from which each self-interaction coefficient approaches its critical value.

items.title: Comparing the reliability of coherent systems with heterogeneous, dependent and distribution-free components
items.summary: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in comparing the reliability of systems with dependent components. Most of the recent works consider Archimedean copulas to define the dependency structure of systems and examine specific familiy of distributions. In this work, we provide distribution-free results to compare, in the usual stochastic order under some majorization conditions, coherent systems with heterogeneous and dependent components where the dependency structure can be defined by any copula. Applications of our main results for specific copulas and different families of marginal distributions are also given.

items.title: A Deterministic Algorithm for Eigenvalue Separation in Tridiagonal Matrices
items.summary: We develop a deterministic algorithm for separating the eigenvalues of Hermitian tridiagonal matrices by small diagonal perturbations. For $\|T\|_2\leq1$, $0<δ<1/2$, and $X=\mathrm{diag}(1,\ldots,n)$, our algorithm selects $t\in[0,δ/n]$ such that $D=tX$ satisfies $\|D\|_2\leqδ$ and $\mathrm{gap}(T+D)>c\,δ^2n^{-12}$ for an absolute constant $c>0$. The construction uses a classical convex weighted eigenvalue sum and its finite-scale slope variation. A tridiagonal localization argument turns near-degenerate eigenvalues into separated responses to the fixed diagonal direction, yielding a quantitative gap certificate. An adaptive interval selector then identifies a certifying window in at most $\lceil\log_2(16n^3)\rceil$ refinements, using $O(\log n)$ evaluations of the weighted eigenvalue sum to inverse-polynomial accuracy. A structure-exploiting implementation uses rigorous Sturm eigenvalue enclosures and adaptive precision to certify the stopping condition on six families of test matrices. The directly certified gaps are substantially larger than the worst-case analytical bounds, illustrating both the effectiveness of the construction and the conservatism of the universal certificate. Our results give a deterministic answer to the eigenvalue-separation question underlying the deterministic Minami perturbation problem for tridiagonal matrices.

items.title: Singular Kähler-Ricci solitons and complete gradient shrinking Kähler-Ricci solitons on non-compact manifolds
items.summary: We construct a class of complete gradient shrinking Kähler-Ricci solitons on non-compact toric manifolds by exhausting a family of singular Kähler-Ricci solitons associated to multiple divisors. The construction method will be also extended on non-compact $\mathbf G$-manifolds.

items.title: Rigidity of Stationary Domains for Robin Torsion in the Plane
items.summary: For every positive Robin parameter, we prove that a bounded simply connected planar domain with $C^{2,α}$ boundary is stationary for Robin torsional rigidity under an area constraint if and only if it is a disk. No convexity, curvature bound, or additional condition on the overdetermined constant is assumed. The difficulty is that the stationarity condition couples the boundary trace of the Robin torsion function, its tangential derivative, and the boundary curvature. We encode this condition through a normalized Airy stress function and construct a superharmonic auxiliary function by a quartic minimization calibrated on disks. The boundary structure of this auxiliary function allows us to identify a point where it attains its minimum on the boundary and has a nonnegative outward normal derivative. The strong maximum principle and Hopf's boundary point lemma then force the auxiliary function to be constant. Consequently, for any stationary domain in the class under consideration, the Robin torsion function has a constant boundary trace, and the stationarity condition forces the boundary curvature to be constant.

items.title: Fast HOSVD via Randomized Preconditioning and Mixed Precision
items.summary: Computing dominant mode subspaces is a major cost in the higher-order singular value decomposition (HOSVD) and its sequentially truncated variant (STHOSVD). Randomized Tucker algorithms can reduce this cost by approximating the required subspaces from small sketches, but may introduce additional approximation errors. We exploit the extreme aspect ratios of tensor unfoldings, whose mode dimensions can remain manageable while being orders of magnitude smaller than the products of the remaining dimensions. Instead of directly approximating the desired subspaces, we sketch the entire unfolding at a scale comparable to its mode dimension to preserve its full row-space geometry, and use randomized preconditioning to recover the desired singular subspaces through small matrix factorizations. We develop randomized preconditioned HOSVD and STHOSVD algorithms incorporating numerical truncation, and further accelerate their large matrix multiplications using mixed precision. Our analysis shows that truncation adds only a term quadratic in the numerical threshold to the classical HOSVD tail-energy bound, while mixed precision introduces a relative \(O(\sqrt{u_\ell})\) correction to the tail-energy term and an additive \(O(u_\ell)\) term under suitable conditions, where \(u_\ell\) is the lower-precision unit roundoff. On synthetic and real tensors, our methods achieve speedups of a fewfold to several dozenfold over classical HOSVD and STHOSVD, with runtimes competitive with those of other randomized methods. The double-precision versions match the classical reconstruction errors to numerical precision, and the mixed-precision variants yield nearly identical errors.

items.title: Fractional Calculus Operator Emerging from the 2D Biorthogonal Hermite Konhauser Polynomials
items.summary: In the present paper, we introduce a method to construct two variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. By using this new technique, we define 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and we investigate several properties of them such as biorthogonality property, operational formula and integral representation. We further inverstigate their images under the Laplace transformations, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function and obtain the similar properties for them. In order to establish new fractional calculus, we add two new parameters and consider 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function. We introduce an integral operator containing the modified bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function in the kernel. We show that it satisify the semigroup property and obtain its left inverse operator, which corresponds to its fractional derivative operator.

items.title: Equilibria for Time-inconsistent Regular-singular Control Problems with Non-exponential Discount
items.summary: This paper studies a time-inconsistent mixed regular-singular control problem in continuous time with non-exponential discount. We seek time-consistent equilibria in an intrapersonal game framework and propose two novel definitions of regular-singular equilibrium where both regular and singular controls are unified via control laws. The standard equilibrium definition allows simultaneous perturbations of both controls, while a mild definition restricts perturbations to one control at a time. Verification theorems providing sufficient conditions are established for both definitions. We illustrate the applicability of the theory through an effort and dividend problem. First, a mild equilibrium is constructed, yet not a standard equilibrium, highlighting the distinction between the two definitions. Moreover, we derive semi-explicit threshold-type equilibria under both a mixture of exponential discount functions and a pseudo-exponential discount function. In both cases, the convexity of the value function is rigorously established, the equilibrium conditions are verified, and the existence of the effort and dividend thresholds is proved. Numerical results reveal the impacts of exogenous parameters on the effort and dividend thresholds and the equilibrium value function, along with their economic implications.

items.title: Duality Relations of Graph Polynomials
items.summary: The duality theorem of Lass relates the matching polynomials of a simple graph $G$ with the matching polynomials of its complement $\bar G$. In particular, this relation gives rise to Godsil's result, which offers a nice interpretation of the Lebesgue integral associated with the Hermite orthogonality measure. In this work, we show that similar to matching polynomials, the path-cover polynomials also satisfy duality relations and give combinatorial interpretations of the Lebesgue integral and the inner product in the space of associated Laguerre polynomials. Similar duality relations hold for clique-cover polynomials and chromatic polynomials. As applications, we find an efficient algorithm that computes these graph polynomials for cographs. We also give explicit formulas to compute the number of Hamiltonian paths and cycles in complete multipartite graphs.

items.title: Complement Cancellation and the Spectral Characterization of Three-Point Recurrence
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate both two-sided and one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence within the framework of weakly mixing measure-preserving systems. As our principal result, we establish an exact spectral characterization for the failure of two-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence: namely, a subset \(R\subseteq\mathbb N\) fails to possess this property if and only if there exist a continuous symmetric probability measure \(σ\) on \(\mathbb T\) and a constant \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying \[ 2\widehatσ(n)+\widehatσ(2n)\leq-\varepsilon \qquad(n\in R). \] Our proof of the necessity relies upon a complement-symmetrized correlation identity, whereas the converse is achieved through a construction involving a stationary Gaussian system, a bounded odd observable, Hermite expansions, and an independent Bernoulli extension. Furthermore, we extend this characterization to three-point polynomial configurations as well as to actions of countable abelian groups. In addition, we derive an unconditional analogue in which arbitrary symmetric probability measures take the place of continuous ones, thereby demonstrating a strict separation between the ergodic and weakly mixing classes of recurrence. Subsequently, we turn our attention to the distinction between two-sided and ordinary one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence. It is shown that a suitable negative spectral condition compels the failure of one-sided recurrence. More remarkably, we construct an explicit weakly mixing system wherein the quadratic spectral expression remains uniformly positive, yet the presence of a negative cubic correlation still induces a one-sided recurrence deficit. Consequently, it follows that two-point spectral data alone are insufficient to govern one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence.

items.title: Rank 1 phenomena for groups of positive deficiency
items.summary: We examine second bounded cohomology and mod p homology in finite index subgroups of 1-relator groups and groups with a presentation of positive deficiency. We use this to determine exactly which subgroups of 1-relator groups are boundedly generated.

items.title: On the invariants of L-functions of degree 2, II: twisted conductor
items.summary: We continue our study of the invariants of the $L$-functions of deree 2 twisted by Dirichlet characters. In a previous paper, we proved that twisting does not change degree and internal shift. Our aim now is to show a corresponding theorem for the conductor. This paper is intended as the second part of a series aiming to prove a general version of the Weil converse theorem with minimal assumptions on the shape of the functional equation of twists.

items.title: Nonlinear Joint State and Noise Estimation under Packet Dropouts and Additive Measurement Corruption
items.summary: This paper investigates joint state and noise covariance estimation for nonlinear systems subject to dual reliability impairments: random packet dropouts and additive measurement corruption. This scenario poses challenging nonconjugate inference, as clean and corrupted measurements share an unknown baseline covariance $\boldsymbol{R}_k$ with fixed known corruption covariance $\boldsymbol{E}_k$. Packet reception is observable, whereas the authenticity of received measurements remains latent and must be inferred. To resolve this intractable estimation problem, we cast joint posterior inference as a variational optimization problem and develop a conjugate variational inference adaptive Kalman filter with dual reliability (CVIAKF-DR). The proposed method retains analytical updates for the prediction covariance and two reliability probabilities, while adopting CVI to estimate the state and baseline measurement covariance. The covariance update combines the analytical contribution from clean measurements with Monte Carlo gradient estimates for corrupted measurements. Numerical results on a re-entry tracking benchmark demonstrate the superior accuracy of the proposed method in both state and noise covariance estimation. Remarkably, even built upon the linear Kalman filtering (KF) framework that is originally designed for linear systems, our method achieves more accurate estimation performance than dedicated nonlinear filtering algorithms based on the cubature Kalman filter (CKF).

items.title: Multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules
items.summary: The goal of this article is to introduce the category of effective filtered multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and the category of multivariable $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules of finite $E_Δ$-height over the rigid-analytic open polydisk $\mathcal{O}_Δ$, and to establish an exact tensor equivalence between them. This generalizes Kisin's analytic classification of filtered $(\varphi, N)$-modules and provides the rigid-analytic foundation for multivariable $p$-adic Hodge theory.

items.title: Quantitative homogenization of Stokes flow in a perforated domain under low regularity of data and geometry
items.summary: We study the homogenization of the steady Stokes equations with no-slip conditions in a domain perforated by $\varepsilon$-periodic obstacles, whose limit is Darcy's law for the homogenized pressure $p^\ast$. We prove the quantitative error estimate with rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, natural in the presence of a boundary layer, only assuming that $f-\nabla p^\ast\in H^1$. Such estimates were previously available only under strong smoothness assumptions, such as $f\in C^{1,1/2}$. Our geometrical assumptions are also less stringent than in the previous analyses. The outer domain and the reference fluid cell need only be Lipschitz, the perforations may deviate from periodicity in a layer of width $O(\varepsilon)$ near the outer boundary, and the solid part may be connected (in three dimensions) and attached to the outer wall. In the absence of a boundary layer, the same argument yields the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ assuming only $f\in H^1$.

items.title: On Bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Polynomials
items.summary: Recently, Özarslan and Elidemir (2023) introduced a methodology for constructing two-variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one-variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. The primary objective of the paper is to introduce novel class of two-variable biorthogonal polynomials namley bivariate Jacobi Konhauser polynomials. We investigate several fundamental properties of these polynomials including their biorthogonality property, operational formula, generating function, and integral representation. Furthermore, We inverstigate their images under the Laplace transform, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Mittag Leffler (JKML) function and obtain the similar properties for them.

items.title: Rigidity and equidistribution of random walks by diffeomorphisms near the conservative regime
items.summary: We consider a random walk on a closed manifold $M$ driven by a probability measure $μ$ on the set of $C^2$-diffeomorphisms. Provided $μ$ has compact support, satisfies certain gap, pinching, and ergodicity conditions, and is weak-$*$ close to volume-preserving, we prove $M$ carries exactly one atom-free stationary probability measure $Υ_μ$. It has finite high-dimensional Riesz energy and coincides with volume in the volume-preserving setting. Moreover, for every $x\in M$, the $n$-step distribution $μ^{*n}*δ_{x}$ converges to $Υ_μ$ unless $x$ is trapped in a finite $μ$-invariant set. Our result applies to a variety of situations: bi-expanding random walks on surfaces, non-linear perturbations of Zariski-dense random walks on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, on cocompact lattice quotients of $\mathrm{SO}(2,1), \mathrm{SO}(3,1)$, or on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$.

items.title: Manin's conjecture for semi-integral curves and $\mathbb A^1$-connectedness
items.summary: We explore log Manin's conjecture for integral points and its connections to $\mathbb A^1$-connectedness. We prove log Manin's conjecture for Campana rational curves and for $\mathbb A^1$-curves on split toric varieties. Our arguments combine the Cox ring description of the moduli space of rational curves with Batyrev's heuristic-type counting arguments. As our proofs are geometric in nature, they give a geometric explanation of the mysterious leading constant for Campana points proposed by Chow--Loughran--Takloo-Bighash--Tanimoto.

items.title: Learning Morse Lyapunov functions through invertible neural networks
items.summary: Towards data-driven stability certificates of dynamical systems, we are witnessing renewed interest in studying and exploiting the structure of Lyapunov functions. Especially Lyapunov functions that are locally quadratic (i.e., Morse) gained popularity ever since it was understood that they can be written as the norm squared of a diffeomorphism. This topological representation alludes to parametrizations using invertible neural networks. In this note we discuss when and how such functions can be learned. In particular, using neural ODEs (NODEs), we characterize Sobolev approximation of these diffeomorphisms on compact sets and show how this naturally relates to stability. We also connect our results to PLNets and supply numerical experiments for illustration.

items.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
items.summary: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.

items.title: Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality implies superreflexivity
items.summary: We prove that if \(X\) is a Banach space for which Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality holds, then \(X\) is superreflexive. We also present an example of a superreflexive Banach space for which the vector-valued Stein property fails.

items.title: Classes of non-invertible simple derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$
items.summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $n\geq 3$ be an integer. For $2\leq j\leq n-1$, let $a_j\in k$, and $g_j(x_j)\in k[x_j]\setminus k.$ We give two classes of simple and non-invertible $k$-derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n].$ The first class consists of the $k$-derivations $(1 +x_1^{m_2}x_2)\partial_{x_1}+x_1^{m_1}\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $m_1$ and $m_2$ are two positive integers such that $m_2$ does not divide $m_1$. The second class consists of $k$-derivations $(1-x_2^α x_1^β)\partial_{x_1} +x_1^m\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $α\geq 1,β\geq 1$ and $m\geq β+1$ are integers, under the assumption that $a_j=0,$ for all $2\leq j\leq n-1$ or deg$_{x_2}g_2(x_2)=1$.

items.title: On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
items.summary: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is the theoretical core of the dimensionality reduction methods based on random projections. While a standard probabilistic proof uses matrices with Gaussian entries, the computational cost of random projections can be drastically reduced by the use of simpler variables, especially if they vanish with a high probability. In this paper, we propose an elementary analysis of random projections under classical assumptions that emphasizes the key role of sub-Gaussianity: any 1-sub-Gaussian distribution with variance 1 yields the same sufficient target dimension as the Gaussian distribution. We then extend the analysis to sparse projections, with data-dependent sparsity conditions on the pairwise differences of the points, and we quantify the cost of sparsity on the target dimension. A complementary lower bound shows the limits induced by the sparsity of the data itself.

items.title: Angular-Pole Flag Curvature and Conformal Control of Radial Jacobi Fields in Diagonal Conic Finsler Optics
items.summary: We study diagonal conic Finsler optical structures with radial coefficients and an arbitrary angular Finsler norm. We obtain the spray curvature block and identify the angular-pole radial-transverse flag curvature at a critical radius with the negative optical-arclength radial Jacobi coefficient. We prove that a compactly supported radial conformal two-jet determines the critical radius and any signed radial coefficient. A navigation Randers sphere yields unequal oriented periods with a common radial coefficient.

items.title: The least Carmichael numbers with $k$ prime factors
items.summary: Let $S_k$ denote the least Carmichael number with exactly $k$ prime factors. Like the later searches of Pinch, our algorithm builds the prime factors of a candidate in increasing order and stops as soon as the preproduct $P$ satisfies $Pλ(P) > B$. At that point there is at most one possible cofactor, and we recover all of its prime factors at once in polynomial time. We prove an unconditional bound on the number of candidates the search examines, in terms of how far $B$ exceeds the product of the first $k$ primes. When the search is run in doubling passes, this gives a running time of $e^{O(k)} = S_k^{O(1/\log k)}$ under a natural conjecture on the size of $S_k$. We also show that the constant in the exponent is sharp for the set of square-free numbers that the bound counts. Finally, we compute $S_k$ for every $k \leq 64$; Pinch had computed it for $k \leq 35$.

items.title: $C^0$-Contact Anosov flows
items.summary: We prove that smooth reparametrizations of the geodesic flow on a manifold of constant negative curvature are contact Anosov flows. In particular we give a new class of exponentially mixing Anosov flows. Moreover, this introduces the notion of $C^0$-contact and we prove that the classical Gray stability theorem that is known in the smooth case fails in this setting.

items.title: The Singular LeBrun Transform: Complex Conformal and Contact Geometry
items.summary: A holomorphic conformal structure is rigid in the presence of rational curves: a complex conformal manifold that is not conformally flat contains no immersed rational null geodesic. So a natural compactification of such a manifold, on which its null geodesics close up, must degenerate along the boundary. We study this phenomenon for the complex conformal manifold that LeBrun attached to a complex contact manifold $Z$ in inverting Salamon's twistor construction: the space $M_{\mathbb{C}}$ of balanced conics of $Z$ transverse to the contact distribution, with its holomorphic Riemannian metric of holonomy contained in $\mathrm{Sp}(n,\mathbb{C})\mathrm{Sp}(1,\mathbb{C})$. Its compactification by the degenerate conics of $Z$ forces the metric to become singular at the boundary. We develop a framework, the singular LeBrun transform, in which these singularities are a source of information rather than an obstacle: the singularities of the metric and of its curvature are read off from the degenerate rational curves of $Z$, locally through the contact neighbourhood of a curve and globally through the incidence variety. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture that all positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds are symmetric, which was recently claimed by OpenAI and by Hu, Liu and Wan. The emphasis of the paper, however, is less on this result than on the framework developed here, which should apply to other problems of the same kind; we conclude with two such directions, negative quaternionic-Kähler manifolds and a singular Merkulov transform for Legendre moduli spaces.

items.title: The Odd Shift is not sofic in dimensions $d \ge 3$
items.summary: In this paper, we prove that the Odd Shift $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimensions $d \ge 3$. Our proof uses lower bounds from communication complexity, specifically the result of Raz and Spieker on the nondeterministic communication complexity for the connectivity problem. We also prove that $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimension $d=2$ under the assumption we call Mute Ocean.

items.title: Radial symmetry for the positive Kähler--Einstein Dirichlet problem on the ball
