items.summary: We prove radial symmetry for every strictly plurisubharmonic function $u$ on the unit ball in $\C^n$, $n\ge2$, that is smooth up to the boundary, vanishes there, and has complex Hessian determinant $μe^{-u}$ for a constant $μ>0$. The known Fubini--Study family therefore exhausts all such solutions. For the corresponding complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation, this establishes the Berman--Berndtsson symmetry conjecture in the smooth class and gives uniqueness throughout the known existence range. The classification also yields the sharp Moser--Trudinger inequality on the ball in Cegrell's finite-energy class.

items.title: Optimal Quadrature and the Curse of Dimensionality for a Veronese Class
items.summary: We study integration on a $3^d$-dimensional trigonometric space whose unit ball has all coordinate mixed partial derivatives bounded by one. With evaluations anywhere in $\mathbb{R}^d$, we determine the exact minimal worst-case error among all deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ function values. An optimal quadrature formula is obtained by truncating an exact product quadrature formula on $\{1/2, 1/2+π\}^d$. All weights are positive. For each error tolerance $0<\varepsilon<1$, the information complexity grows exponentially in $d$ with the common base $Λ\approx 1.10546546$. The correction of order $\sqrt{d}$ to the logarithm of the information complexity and the corresponding error limit are determined by the standard normal distribution function. For $b\ge 1$ and $n=\lceil b^d\rceil$, the error tends to one, one half, or zero according as $b<Λ$, $b=Λ$, or $b>Λ$.

items.title: Null flag curvature of anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics
items.summary: We consider the Zermelo navigation problem for a time-dependent Finsler metric, which can be recast as the study of lightlike geodesics of a Lorentz--Finsler metric on a non-relativistic spacetime. To control how such geodesics separate, we introduce a null flag curvature, defined for any pseudo-Finsler metric with a lightlike cone, and show that it governs the Taylor expansion of the norm of a Jacobi field. We then prove a formula relating the null flag curvatures of two anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics. Applying it to the spacetime associated with a time-independent Randers metric, which is anisotropically conformal to a stationary spacetime, we obtain compact expressions for the flag curvature of Randers metrics, both in terms of their $(α,β)$ data and of their Zermelo data $(h,W)$. These expressions allow us to compute explicitly the flag curvature when $W$ is conformal, affine or projective, and when $α$ is a Kähler metric. We also introduce a Weyl-type curvature, invariant under anisotropic conformal changes, whose vanishing characterizes Finsler manifolds of scalar flag curvature, and we obtain the flag curvature of $F + \mathrm{d}f$, showing in particular that $F$ has scalar flag curvature if and only if $F + \mathrm{d}f$ does.

items.title: A biregular classification of smooth quotients of abelian surfaces
items.summary: We classify smooth projective surfaces that are quotients of abelian surfaces by finite groups. We also record the orbifold boundary associated to a quotient map and describe its structure explicitly in the case of augmented irregularity one.

items.title: Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift
items.summary: We study a class of discrete-time random walks in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose conditional drift decays polynomially in time and grows polynomially with the distance from the origin to the current position. This class is related to several models of self-interacting random processes. We determine the asymptotic behavior of the walk under the assumption that its increments have moments of order $p$ for some $p>2$. In the linear case, where the drift depends linearly on the current position, we establish a phase transition in the convergence in distribution of the normalized process to Gaussian limits. In the nonlinear case, we identify three distinct regimes separated by a critical line and show that the normalized process exhibits qualitatively different behaviors in each regime, including convergence in distribution to a Gaussian law, convergence to a non-Gaussian limit given by the stationary distribution of a stochastic differential equation, and almost sure localization on a hypersphere.

items.title: Curvature condition on the Wasserstein space over a closed Riemannian manifold
items.summary: We establish regularity results for the solution flow of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDE) on the Wasserstein space $\mathscr{P}(M)$ over a closed Riemannian manifold, under suitable assumptions on the driving vector fields. We derive the SDE governing the associated tangent process and prove its well-posedness by means of the framework developped in \cite{Martin2025} for Covariant SDEs on Inverse Limit Hilbert vector bundles over the diffeomorphism group. We introduce the $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$ condition, a geometric curvature-type condition which generalizes, in the setting of SDEs on $¶(M)$, both the $\mathrm{H.C.K.}$ condition introduced in \cite{cattiaux:hal-00805299} and the ergodicity condition of \cite[Section 4]{wang2020}. Finally, combining this condition with the theory of entropic interpolations (see \cite{Leonard2014}), we establish several consequences of $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$, including control of the distance between two trajectories, gradient estimates for the associated Markov semigroup and a local Poincar{é} inequality. In the case $K >0$, we further obtain the existence and uniqueness of an ergodic invariant measure for the associated semigroup.

items.title: The monoid of orientation preserving mappings on a chain
items.summary: We introduce new kinds of regular monoids of transformations consisting of mappings which preserve or reverse the orientation of a finite cycle.

items.title: A Rollout-Based Approach to Real-Time Topology and Dispatch Control in the AI4RealNet L2RPN Benchmark
items.summary: Operating transmission networks under uncertain outages requires coordinating discrete network topology actions with continuous adjustments to generation and storage, while respecting operational constraints and real-time computational limits. We present a rollout-based controller that combines discrete and continuous decisions under the uncertain contingency policy of the L2RPN AI4RealNet 2026 challenge. Power-flow approximations and convex optimization identify the most promising actions, followed by short-horizon simulations to predict their effect on congestion, renewable curtailment, and redispatching costs. A further policy exploits the benchmark's specific attack protocol: keeping selected lines disconnected prevents some adversarial outages from being initiated. On the benchmark's $118$-bus network, the controller completed $189$ of $208$ final-test scenarios (score $64.39$) and achieved the second-best ratio of score to computation time among the five top-ranked entries, behind one that scored lower. Our results show that combining structured optimization with simulation-based action selection is effective even without a learned decision rule, and fast enough for real-time control. Code and reproduction material: https://github.com/DavidKrame/RAD_agent__AI4RealNet_competition.

items.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
items.summary: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

items.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the unit disc
items.summary: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface with canonical bundle $K_X$ and holomorphic tangent bundle $T_X=K_X^{-1}$. For each integer $r\geq 2$, each $q\in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of a square root of $K_X$, we obtain a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal harmonic metric $h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)$ induces Hermitian metrics $H_j=h_j^{-1}\otimes h_{j+1}$ on $T_X$ for $j=1,\ldots,r-1$, together with a possibly degenerate Hermitian metric $H_r$ determined by $h_1,h_r$, and $q$. We call $h$ complete if the Kähler metrics induced by $H_1,\ldots,H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki proved that if $q$ is nonzero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete harmonic metric on the corresponding cyclic Higgs bundle satisfying $\det(h)=1$. The Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through the subharmonic weight $φ_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X$. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for general subharmonic weight functions $\varphi$ whose exponentials are $C^2$ outside a compact subset of $X$. On the unit disc $\mathbb D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$, we also prove that a real complete solution exists for every subharmonic weight function. We further establish a monotone approximation theorem. If $\varphi_ε$ are smooth subharmonic weight functions on the discs $\mathbb D_ε=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1-ε\}$ decreasing to $\varphi$ as $ε\searrow0$, the corresponding complete solutions $h_ε$, normalized by $\det(h_ε)=1$, converge monotonically to a complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$.

items.title: Relaxation of one-dimensional variational problems without growth constraints
items.summary: We study the integral representation of the relaxation of integral functionals of the form u-> \int f(x,u(x),u'(x)) dx, for Sobolev functions u\,: (a, b) $\rightarrow$ RN with fixed Dirichlet boundary conditions. Unlike classical works on the subject, we require a very mild growth condition on the Lagrangian f to make our statement as natural and general as possible. We state four different situations in which we manage to obtain an explicit expression for the relaxation on BV , which is usually the natural framework for such weak growth conditions. Our goal is also to express a few unifying assumptions on the Lagrangian to obtain the expected relaxation formula.

items.title: The Narrow Corridor of Stable Solutions in an Extended Osipov--Lanchester Model with Constant Total Population
items.summary: This paper studies a modification of the classical Osipov-Lanchester model in which the total population of the two sides, $N=R+B$, stays constant. In this model the ratio $y=R/B$ obeys the Riccati equation $\dot y=αy^2-β$, which is solvable in elementary functions for all values of the parameters. The main result is a complete classification of the stable regimes. An asymptotically stable invariant set in the quadrant $R,B\ge 0$ exists only in three cases: $α<0,\ β<0$ gives a stable interior equilibrium; $α=0,\ β<0$ makes the boundary $B=0$ stable; $α<0,\ β=0$ makes the boundary $R=0$ stable. If $α>0$ or $β>0$, every solution except one unstable equilibrium reaches a boundary of the quadrant in finite time, where the model stops being applicable. If the parameters vary in time, a fixed distance from the boundaries is kept when $α(t)$ and $β(t)$ obey buffer dynamics that push them away from zero. Finally, in the case $α<0,\ β<0$ the original system grows exponentially, while in the two degenerate cases it grows at most linearly. Growth demanded of a given cost, the sum of the two channels, bounds their imbalance and, with the perturbation bound, confines the parameters to an explicit wedge about $|α|=|β|$ truncated near the origin: the narrow corridor of the model.

items.title: Homotopy $n$-types of cubical sets and graphs
items.summary: We give a new construction of the model structure on the category of simplicial sets for homotopy $n$-types, originally due to Elvira-Donazar and Hernandez-Paricio, using a right transfer along the coskeleton functor. We observe that an analogous model structure can be constructed on the category of cubical sets, and use it to equip the category of (simple) graphs with a fibration category structure whose weak equivalences are discrete $n$-equivalences.

items.title: Projective planes with abelian collineation groups of type (F) are Desarguesian
items.summary: We use prime ideal factorization and residue class fields of cyclotomic integer rings to prove that every abelian direct product difference set is classical. This implies that every projective plane of order $n$ with an abelian collineation group of order $n(n-1)$ is Desarguesian, proving a conjecture of Jungnickel and de Resmini. As a consequence, we obtain the classification of circular Costas maps and of Costas polynomials conjectured by Muratovic-Ribic, Pott, Thomson and Wang and by Torres and Rubio.

items.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states
items.summary: Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,\varphi)$ has a unique equilibrium state $μ$ and $μ(f)=0$. The system $(T,μ)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for Hölder observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem. The main results have been formalised in Lean 4.

items.title: Discriminants and resultants of orthogonal polynomials
items.summary: The concept of a linked pair of two sequences of polynomials, one of which is orthogonal, is introduced. Such a pair always has a resultant that factors. Two methods for producing such linked pairs are given: one for general orthogonal polynomials and the other for any polynomial in the Askey scheme. Generalized discriminants are introduced and evaluated, including a general product formula for each operator in the Askey scheme. A new notion of companion orthogonal polynomials is also introduced and used to evaluate the discriminants of orthogonal polynomials. These methods recover all known formulas for the generalized discriminants of classical polynomials and provide new ones.

items.title: Triples in matroid circuits
items.summary: We prove that, if $X$ is a four-element independent set in a vertically $5$-connected representable matroid $M$, then either there is a circuit of $M$ that contains at least three elements of $X$, or there is a representation $A$ of $M$ such that each column of $A$ has at most two non-zero elements and each of the columns indexed by $X$ has exactly one non-zero element. We also prove a version of this result without the connectivity assumptions.

items.title: Branch-and-Cut for Maximum $k$-Independent Sets with Spectral Bounds
items.summary: We develop a branch-and-cut method for finding maximum distance-independent sets in graphs. Our approach solves a sequence of fixed-size clique problems, combining graph reductions with combinatorial and spectral bounds. We give a compact formulation, derive strengthened inequalities, establish conditions for using spectral information, and evaluate them in a comprehensive computational study.

items.title: A Convergence Analysis of the Random Feature Method for Linear PDEs
items.summary: The Random Feature Method (RFM) distinguishes itself among machine learning approaches to partial differential equations (PDEs) through its superior accuracy and computational efficiency. Nevertheless, the theoretical underpinnings of RFM remain incompletely elucidated. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of RFM within the framework of kernel methods, focusing on two principal aspects: (i) approximation by finitely many random features in Sobolev norms and the PDE residual seminorm, and (ii) estimation over the induced reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) from finitely many noiseless collocation observations. We relate both problems to kernel ridge regression (KRR) and establish upper and lower bounds in terms of the eigenvalues of the associated integral operators under the respective assumptions. Combining the approximation and estimation lower bounds, we establish a lower bound under simultaneous restrictions on the numbers of random features and collocation observations. We further quantify how activation regularity affects these eigenvalues, obtaining algebraic upper bounds for finitely smooth activations and stretched-exponential upper bounds for analytic activations.

items.title: List colouring of circular-arc graphs
items.summary: A circular-arc graph takes a set of nonempty closed arcs on a circle as its vertex set, and two vertices are adjacent when their corresponding arcs intersect on the circle. We show the chromatic number of any circular-arc graph equals its list chromatic number. Our methodology is an application of Schauz's coefficient formula within the Alon-Tarsi and Combinatorial Nullstellensatz framework.

items.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
items.summary:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<θ<π/2$, we consider \[ σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) = f(ξ)h^{p-1} rac{ρ^{k+1}}{\varphi(ρ)}, \qquad ρ=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_μh=\cotθ\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

items.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
items.summary: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)-h, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+δ, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_μ}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cotθ, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<θ\leπ/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_μ\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<θ<π$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.

items.title: Vanishing geodesic distance phenomenon and boundedness of curvatures
items.summary: This article concerns a conjecture proposed by Michor and Mumford in their 2005 paper, in which the vanishing of the geodesic distance is associated to the local unboundedness of the sectional curvature. In this article, we consider a Riemannian Banach manifold with all of its curvature tensors locally bounded. We derive several properties regarding the local boundedness of curvature tensors, and give a sufficient condition for a non-degenerate geodesic distance, which partially verifies the conjecture in its converse form.

items.title: A Block-Activated Decomposition Algorithm for Multi-Stage Stochastic Variational Inequalities
items.summary: We develop a block-activated decomposition algorithm for multi-stage stochastic variational inequalities with nonanticipativity constraints. The algorithm features two computational novelties: (i) At each iteration, it activates only a user-chosen subset of scenarios. (ii) For each activated scenario, it employs the resolvent of the cost operator and the projector onto the constraint set separately. These reduce computational load and enhance tractability, in contrast with existing approaches, which often require evaluating the resolvent of the sum of the cost operator and the normal cone operator of the constraint set. As an application, we demonstrate that in risk-averse stochastic programming with conditional value-at-risk objective functions, our method requires only projecting onto constraint sets, together with solving univariate equations involving the proximity operators of the cost functions, thereby avoiding solving high-dimensional constrained subproblems as required by existing methods.

items.title: Existence of three solutions for parametric $p$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
items.summary: In this paper we deal with a nonlinear elliptic problem in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^N$ involving the $p$-Laplacian operator with $p>N$. Under suitable assumptions on the potential term and on the nonlinearity, we establish the existence of at least three distinct weak solutions. Our approach is variational and relies on two different three critical points theorems. The results extend to higher dimensions some recent multiplicity theorems for one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian equations on the real line, and provide explicit ranges for the parameter $λ> 0$ ensuring the existence of multiple solutions, which are nonnegative under additional sign conditions. The nontriviality of the solutions is also discussed. Finally, applications to problems whose nonlinearities have separated variables are presented.

items.title: Convergence rates of moment--SOS hierarchies with correlative sparsity via gluing and projection
items.summary: This paper studies convergence rates of moment--SOS hierarchies with correlative sparsity. Following the method proposed in~\cite{tran}, we bound the Hausdorff distance between the set of sparse truncated moment sequences and sparse truncated pseudo-moment sequences. The central step is a quantitative gluing lemma on a clique tree: local moment errors and separator discrepancies in total variation control the error of a joint approximating measure. Over hypercube, polynomial kernels give the convergence rates $O((\log_2r)^3/r^2)$ for the correlative sparse quadratic module and $O(r^{-2})$ for the correlative sparse preordering, where the certificate degree is $2r$. On compact basic semialgebraic sets, slack variable lifting and global atom projection yield $O((\log_2r)^{3\Lo/2}/r^{\Lo})$ and $O(r^{-\Lo})$ with a Łojasiewicz exponent $0<\Lo \le1$. These bounds hold for fixed-degree Hausdorff distances and polynomial objective gaps. We also extend to result to the correlative sparse quadratic-module rate for scalar objectives with clique-local polynomial matrix constraints.

items.title: Affine pairs of minimizing units in totally real non-Galois cubic fields
items.summary: Let $Γ$ be a rank-two subgroup of the integral norm-one units in a totally real non-Galois cubic field. We prove that two distinct affinely equivalent minima of Godwin's spread on $Γ\setminus\{1\}$ generate $Γ$ and determine its complete minimum set: a pair with sum $\pm2$ or a triple of integral translates of product one. Every minimum generates the order $\mathbb{Z}[Γ]$. For an order whose norm-one units have such a pair, the order generated by its units is the smallest suborder with the same minimum value. We also give explicit families and a maximal order with minima in two distinct affine classes.

items.title: Advancing Cognitive Pairwise Comparisons for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
items.summary: Human-centric artificial intelligence and data science (HCAD) systems increasingly involve human-in-the-loop (HITL) interventions to overcome the limitations of fully automated machine learning algorithms, such as automation bias and the inability to incorporate tacit domain knowledge, and continuously improve predictive performance. Data transformations, feature selection, feature weighting, and model selection usually require laborious human involvement across iterations of artificial intelligence and data science (AI&DS) pipelines, making development a challenging and time-consuming process. The Cognitive Pairwise Comparison (CPC) framework is proposed as a human-centric methodology to elicit preferences and priorities in a structured format. To establish essential facets of human-centricity, this research advances the CPC methodology so that user preference elicitation can be systematically quantified in these challenging AI&DS tasks. To demonstrate the usability and validity of these facets, this study presents several applications within movie recommender systems using the MovieLens dataset. It exemplifies how the extended CPC framework can facilitate interactions between human judgments and data across supervised learning, dimensionality reduction, and unsupervised learning algorithms.

items.title: Linear Algebra over Bands
items.summary: We introduce Eckmann-Hilton operators on bands, which allow for a suite of matroidal constructions, in particular, matroid unions and matroid stable intersections. This enables the construction of general linear monoids over bands. Geometrically, we show that matroid stable intersection extends the transverse intersection of linear spaces over fields and the stable intersection of tropical linear spaces, lending new insight into intersection theory on bands.

items.title: Multiparameter extensions of the Christ-Kiselev maximal theorem: strong variational bounds
items.summary: For a linear operator $T$ bounded from $L^p(Y)$ to $L^q(X)$, the Christ--Kiselev theorem gives $L^p \to L^q$ bounds for the maximal function $T^{*}$ associated to a filtration on $Y$. This result has been extended to the multiparameter setting, establishing bounds for the maximal function associated to a product of filtrations. In this note, we strengthen these results by proving $ρ$-variational bounds for the multiparameter truncations when $ρ>p$. Furthermore, we give a multilinear extension of the Christ--Kiselev theorem, establishing strong variational bounds for the multiparameter truncations for a general multilinear operator.

items.title: Homogeneous Bracket Flows with Three-Form Flux on the Full Flag Manifold SU(3)/T^2
items.summary: We develop an algebraic framework for homogeneous metric flows with closed three-form flux on reductive homogeneous spaces. The geometric data are encoded by the complete reductive bracket $μ$ on $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak k\oplus\mathfrak m$, while the flux is treated as an additional invariant datum $H$ satisfying $d_μH=0$. For the metric equation \[ \partial_tg = -2\operatorname{Ric}_g + \frac12\mathcal K_{g,H}, \] we derive the corresponding bracket evolution \[ \dotμ= -π(P_{μ,H})μ, \qquad P_{μ,H} = \operatorname{Ric}_μ^{\sharp} - \frac14\mathcal K_{μ,H}^{\sharp}. \] We apply this formulation to the full flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/T^2$. For a prescribed closed invariant three-form, we compute explicitly the quadratic flux operator, the induced three-parameter metric system, and the evolution of the transported bracket coefficients. The system has exactly four positive stationary points. They correspond to the normal homogeneous Einstein metric and the three invariant Kähler--Einstein metrics. The normal stationary point has unstable index two, whereas each Kähler--Einstein stationary point has unstable index one. When the flux also evolves by the Hodge heat equation, we derive the closed system for its amplitude and the three metric coefficients. Every isotropic solution becomes extinct in finite time, with $h^2/λ^2\to0$. For a nonzero transverse mode the absolute perturbation is of order $(T-t)^{3/5}$, whereas the perturbation relative to the collapsing scale is of order $(T-t)^{-2/5}$. We relate the invariant three-form to the NS--NS sector of the strict $\mathrm{SU}(3)$-structure ansatz in type IIA supergravity.

items.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
items.summary: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories. We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\mathbb{C}$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.

items.title: Revisiting the $β_1$-action on the 3-primary stable homotopy groups of spheres
items.summary: Let $β_1$ be the first 3-torsion class in the stable homotopy groups of spheres in even degree. Toda showed that $β_1^5 \neq 0$, whilst $β_1^6 = 0$. Shimomura generalised this to the 144-periodic family generated by $β_1$, written as $\{β_{1+9s}\}_{s\geq 0}$, and showed that any $5$-fold product $\prod_5 β_{1+9s} \neq 0$, whilst all 6-fold products $\prod_6 β_{1+9s} = 0$. In this article, we give a simple proof of these results as well as some generalisations to other 144-periodic families. Along the way, we also refine known detection results for these families. Our tools include BP-synthetic spectra, and the well-known Adams--Novikov spectral sequence for the spectrum of topological modular forms at the prime $3$ as well as its Adams operations.

items.title: Equilibrium selection and sharp convergence rates for a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with simplex-volume interactions
items.summary: We study a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with diffusion and nonlocal interactions generated by squared simplex volumes. The associated free energy is not isplacement semiconvex when the simplex dimension $n$ is at least two. For $1\leq n<d$, the stationary states are isotropic Gaussian measures, and every solution converges to the equilibrium determined by its conserved mean. At $n=d$, the free energy fixes only the covariance determinant, allowing a noncompact continuum of anisotropic Gaussian equilibria when $d\geq2$. The limit is then selected by the initial covariance, whose eigenvectors and eigenvalue gaps are preserved by the flow. We establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial probability measures with finite second moment, identify stationary states with the global minimizers of the free energy, and prove convergence in quadratic Wasserstein distance with explicit exponential rates. For compactly supported initial data with nonstationary covariance, the sharp rate is the smaller of the covariance relaxation rate and three times the slowest transport rate, provided that the third moments do not vanish along the directions of slowest transport. The skewness of the initial datum, rather than its covariance, may therefore dictate the long-time behavior.

items.title: Mutual arc presentations and braided open books
items.summary: We show that every canonically fibered link in $S^3$ is the binding of a braided open book in $S^3$, addressing a question of Montesinos and Morton. We introduce mutual arc presentations as our main technical tool, which we consider to be of independent interest. We prove that any fibered link admitting such a presentation is the binding of a braided open book.

items.title: Sharp Fourier Extension Inequalities on $ \mathbb{S}^2 $ for All $q>4$
items.summary: For the ordinary Fourier extension operator on $\mathbb S^2$, we determine the optimal $L^2(\mathbb S^2)\to L^q(\mathbb R^3)$ constant for every real $q>4$, and characterize the nonzero complex extremizers. The result extends the sharp quartic theorem of Foschi and the even-exponent results of Oliveira e Silva--Quilodrán to exponents for which the usual convolution identities are unavailable. The proof has two stages. A continuous inequality for the moments of $\sin r/r$, combined with a trace estimate along the symmetry orbit of a maximizer, reduces the problem to $4\leq q\leq6$. On this interval, the second variation imposes a scalar necessary condition. We contradict it by spectral estimates for spherical harmonics, moment comparisons, and, near $q=4$, a quantitative use of the quartic deficit. The resulting constant is attained exactly by scalar multiples of characters.

items.title: Real log canonical thresholds and real log canonical thresholds with signs
items.summary: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.

items.title: A note on finite length for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
items.summary: Let $p>2$ be a prime and $F/\mathbf{Q}_p$ be a finite extension. We prove that every admissible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, with a central character, and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition, has finite length.

items.title: Parameter Recovery for the Modified Leray-alpha Model via Continuous Data Assimilation
items.summary: In this study, we extend the recursive length-scale recovery method for the simplified Bardina model to the three-dimensional modified Leray-alpha model. The main difficulty is that the unknown parameter also occurs in the nonlinear convection term, so estimating the error in the parameter update requires control of second spatial derivatives of the velocity error. We combine continuous data assimilation with a recursive update of the squared length scale, using observed low Fourier modes and computed high Fourier modes. Under uniform regularity bounds on the reference solution and suitable conditions on the observations and the recovery procedure, we prove geometric convergence of both the parameter and velocity errors at the update times. When the update-window lengths are uniformly bounded, this convergence is exponential in time at the update times.

items.title: A discrepancy dichotomy for 1-factorizations of signed complete bipartite graphs
items.summary: Given a signing $σ\colon E(K_{n,n})\to\{-1,+1\}$ of the complete bipartite graph, when does $K_{n,n}$ admit a $1$-factorization in which every perfect matching has discrepancy bounded below by a positive absolute constant? Unlike the complete-graph case resolved by Ai, He, Im, and Lee, the bipartite setting carries an unavoidable obstruction: any balanced one-sided signing---one whose edge signs depend on a single bipartition class, with the two labels split as evenly as possible---forces every perfect matching to have discrepancy at most $1/n$. We prove that this is essentially the only obstruction: For every $0<\varepsilon\leq1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every signing of $K_{n,n}$ either (i) admits a $1$-factorization in which every perfect matching has discrepancy at least $\varepsilon/53$, or (ii) is $\varepsilon$-close, in normalized Hamming distance, to a balanced one-sided signing. The linear dependence on $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to an absolute factor. A key ingredient is a rank-one stability argument: if the density of rank-two $2\times 2$ switching patterns is small, then the sign matrix is close in Hamming distance to a rank-one sign matrix.

items.title: Higher cotangent cohomology for Stanley-Reisner rings
items.summary: Inspired by work of Altmann and Christophersen, we study the graded pieces of the cotangent cohomology $T^i_{S_{\mathcal{K}}}$, $i\geq 3$ of the Stanley-Reisner ring $S_{\mathcal{K}}$ associated to a simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$. We prove a localization formula allowing one to reduce to the case of negative weights. Our results give a complete description of $T^3$ and $T^4$ in terms of the topology of $\mathcal{K}$ whenever $\mathcal{K}$ is a flag complex. As an application, we give a sufficient criterion for the vanishing of $T^3$ for simplicial spheres, classify two-spheres that have vanishing $T^3$, and show that the boundary complex of the dual associahedron has vanishing $T^3$. Our results make use of the arborescent resolutions considered by Hancharuk, Laurent-Gengoux, and Strobl. We give an alternative and self-contained treatment of these resolutions that may be of independent interest.

items.title: Resurgent Analysis of the Single-Orbit Term in the Selberg Trace Formula
items.summary: We study the large-time asymptotic expansion, the Borel-Laplace transforms and the Stokes phenomenon of the single-orbit term in the Selberg trace formula. By a single-orbit term we mean the contribution from a primitive closed geodesic orbit and its iterations on a compact hyperbolic surface, and its formal large-time expansion is divergent. We prove that the divergent formal series is uniformly $1$-Gevrey asymptotic to the convergent single-orbit term and recover the single-orbit term by a Laplace integral along the positive real axis. Other directions for the Laplace integration are also explored by analyzing the singularities of the Borel transform of this $1$-Gevrey formal series. It turns out that the series obtained by Borel transform is meromorphic on the two-sheeted Riemann surface of $\sqrtξ$, with simple poles corresponding to the resonance spectra of the hyperbolic cylinder. The Laplace transform can be performed along almost every direction on the two-sheeted Riemann surface. Finally, the Stokes structure as the limit of the difference between Laplace integrals along different directions can be computed by a convergent sum of the exponential of resonance spectrum. These results demonstrate the phenomenon that the resurgent structure of a single-orbit term in the Selberg trace formula is reflected by its associated cylinder resonance spectra.

items.title: What Does Machine Learning Learn from Numerical Calabi--Yau Geometry? A Controlled Study on the Fermat Quintic
items.summary: We study polynomial regression of numerical metric errors on the Fermat quintic. A known hypersurface volume-ratio identity gives the exact reference $C-\log p_4$ relative to the induced Fubini--Study metric, where $p_4=\sum_i|z_i|^8$ on unit-normalized homogeneous coordinates. We optimize algebraic metrics at degrees $6,8,10,12$ while preserving finite Fermat symmetry, then fit their remaining logarithmic volume-form error. Regression splits and bootstrap draws keep the five roots of each sampled line together, with all compared teachers evaluated on common clouds. Warm-start replication correlations exceed $0.9997$ at $k=8,10,12$. Across degrees, source-derived modes fall short of target-specific fits, including in a post-hoc quartic check, but outperform random spans of matched rank in the tested libraries. Two independent random-invariant $k=10$ starts have residual correlations $0.768$--$0.803$, while their fitted cubic modes correlate at $0.979$--$0.983$ and retain useful calibrated cross-start prediction. Their fitted modes agree poorly with those of the principal warm-start teacher. Adding the phase-sensitive invariant $J_7$ improves prediction beyond the cubic modulus-only library for all seven warm-start teachers. The gain depends on the library: at $k=12$, a quartic modulus-only fit explains about 97--98\% of residual variance and the conditional interval for the added $J_7$ gain includes zero for both replicas under both measures. The gains therefore establish neither phase independence nor irreducible phase necessity; fixed-baseline augmentation preserves this distinction. The fitted components depend on the numerical protocol; global optimality and a universal finite-degree correction remain unestablished.

items.title: Exploring the Scaling Crossover of Generalized Jeffreys-Type Law: Modeling, Analysis, and High-Accuracy Numerical Computation
items.summary: The generalized Jeffreys-type law is formulated as a multi-term time-fractional Jeffreys-type equation, whose dynamics exhibit rich scaling crossover phenomena associated with different diffusion mechanisms. In this work, we provide a microscopic stochastic interpretation of the MT-TFJE through a continuous-time random walk (CTRW) framework with a generalized waiting-time distribution, elucidating the physical mechanisms underlying the scaling crossover. Based on the Laplace-Volterra formulation and spectral analysis, we establish the well-posedness and stability of the MT-TFJE and derive Sobolev regularity estimates under appropriate assumptions on the initial data and source term. We further develop a high-accuracy numerical scheme, termed CIM-CLG, which combines a contour integral method for temporal approximation with a Chebyshev-Legendre Galerkin method for spatial discretization. The proposed method achieves exponential temporal convergence under the stated regularity of the governing equation, together with high-order spatial accuracy. The temporal approximation involves $\mathcal{O}(N)$ independent contour evaluations, while FFT-based transforms have a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(M^n\log M)$ for spatial dimensions $n=1,2$. The resulting algorithm is naturally parallelizable. Detailed implementation procedures and rigorous error estimates are presented. Extensive numerical experiments in one and two dimensions demonstrate the efficiency, accuracy, and robustness of the proposed method, providing a computationally effective framework for generalized nonlocal diffusion problems.

items.title: Quantitative approximation for Fourier neural operators in controlled ordinary differential equations
items.summary: Fourier neural operators (FNOs) avoid the curse of parametric complexity when approximating the solution operator of certain partial differential equations (PDEs). While recent studies primarily focus on PDEs, in this article we derive upper error bounds for approximating the solution operator of controlled ordinary differential equations (CODEs) $\dot{y}=f(y,u)$ using a FNO. Under a Carathéodory setting and suitable regularity assumptions, including a smallness condition, we prove that the size of the FNO grows at most algebraically in $1/\varepsilon$, namely like $\varepsilon^{-(1+d/(2(s-1)))}$ up to logarithmic factors for GELU networks, and is thus sub-quadratic for sufficiently smooth $f$, where $d=1+n_y+n_u$ and $s$ denotes the Sobolev regularity of $f$. Our proof is based on emulating the Picard iteration through the layers of the FNO while exploiting the differentiation formula of the discrete Fourier transform. This result contributes to the quantitative approximation theory of FNOs for physically motivated problems and provides a theoretical foundation for leveraging a FNO as efficient forward surrogate for the solution operator of CODEs, especially in inverse parameter estimation where repeated evaluations of the forward operator are needed.

items.title: A Dynkin condition for manifolds with boundary
items.summary: We propose a Dynkin-type condition for smooth Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We show that this condition implies bi-Lipschitz equivalence with a Bakry-Émery weighted Riemannian manifold obtained via a time change. As a consequence, we obtain various results, including a local doubling property as well as lower bounds on the Neumann spectral gap and logarithmic Sobolev constant. The local doubling property also yields a new precompactness theorem for manifolds with boundary.

items.title: Entropy and frame measures for self-affine measures
items.summary: Let $M$ be a real expanding $d\times d$ matrix and let $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\R^d$ consist of $N\ge2$ distinct vectors. We study the existence of frame measures for the self-affine probability measure $μ$ generated by the maps $S_i(x)=M^{-1}(x+d_i)$ with equal weights $1/N$. Extending the entropy obstruction for self-similar measures with a common scalar contraction, we prove that $μ$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy of the first symbol given the spatial point is positive. In particular, this holds whenever $N>|\det M|$, without assuming absolute continuity or imposing arithmetic conditions. When $M$ has integer entries, $\mathscr D\subset\Z^d$, and $N=|\det M|$, the measure $μ$ admits a frame measure if and only if $μ$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor.

items.title: Positive Regulation of an Axial Dispersion Tubular Reactor by Optimal Boundary Feedback Control
items.summary: The dynamics of the reactant in an isothermal axial dispersion tubular reactor is considered. Our goal consists in designing the inlet reactant concentration, under the form of a state feedback law, in order to modify the state behavior according to relevant process requirements, while keeping the positivity and stability properties of the uncontrolled dynamics. The designed control is also constrained to be positive to respect physical requirements. First, we state and analytically solve a parameterized optimal feedback design problem. Next, we address a positive observer-based feedback stabilization problem. The results are illustrated by means of numerical simulations.

items.title: Sobolev regularity for nondivergence form nonlocal equations with irregular kernels
items.summary: We consider the nonlocal elliptic equation $L_Ku-λu=f$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $L_K$ is a nondivergence form operator of order $σ\in(0,2)$ with kernel $K(x,y)$. We assume that $K(x,y)$ is Dini continuous in $x$ uniformly in $y$ and merely measurable in $y$. Under the usual upper bound assumption, we prove the boundedness of $L_K$ from $H_p^σ(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for any $p\in(1,\infty)$. We also establish maximal $L_p$-regularity and unique solvability for all sufficiently large $λ$, provided that an additional nondegeneracy condition holds. We further extend these results to weighted spaces with arbitrary Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights and obtain estimates that are robust as $σ\to2$. We also construct a kernel that is jointly uniformly continuous in $(x,y)$, for which both operator boundedness and the maximal regularity estimate fail. This is in sharp contrast to the classical $W_p^2$ theory for second-order elliptic equations in nondivergence form, which allows VMO coefficients.

items.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
items.summary: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers. We instead increase computational capacity: the number of active computational states a model maintains. We introduce the Lattice of Latents, a set of per-layer horizontal latent streams that run recurrently along time, alongside the vertical residual stream that flows through depth. Like hyper-connections, mHC, and attention or value residuals, the Lattice enhances the residual stream, but rather than adding or rerouting residual pathways through depth, it provides companion computational states that persist across tokens. Unlike hybrid Transformer-SSM architectures, whose recurrent states primarily serve as internal memory for sequence mixing, these latents directly condition the vertical stream's attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding. On Transformers trained on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens, a 406M-parameter Lattice model lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 to 14.40 over a parameter-matched Transformer. These gains extend across architectural variants. The Lattice composes with prior residual-stream enhancements: with hyper-connections and input residuals, it lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 (base Transformer) and 14.22 (Transformer with the same enhancements) to 13.61. On Gated DeltaNet, Mamba-2, Triadic GDN, and GDN-Mamba-2 hybrids, it improves perplexity at every tested native state size, with Lattice-GDN and Lattice-Triadic-GDN variants outperforming pure baselines with 4x larger native states. These results identify persistent per-layer state as a complementary axis for scaling language-model computation.

items.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
items.summary: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

items.title: AI4BayesCode: From Natural Language Descriptions to Validated Modular Stateful Bayesian Samplers
items.summary: Coding and computation remain major bottlenecks in Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) workflows, especially as modern sampling algorithms have become increasingly complex and existing probabilistic programming systems remain limited in model support, extensibility, and composability. We introduce AI4BayesCode, an extensible LLM-driven system that translates natural-language Bayesian model descriptions into runnable, validated MCMC samplers. To improve reliability, AI4BayesCode adopts a modular design that decomposes models into modular sampling blocks and maps each block to a built-in sampling component, reducing the need to implement complex sampling algorithms from scratch. Reliability is further improved through pre-generation validation of model specifications and post-generation validation of generated sampler code. AI4BayesCode also introduces a novel recursively stateful coding paradigm for MCMC, allowing modular sampling components, potentially developed by different contributors, to be composed coherently within larger MCMC procedures. We develop a benchmark suite to evaluate AI4BayesCode for sampler-generation. Experiments show that AI4BayesCode can implement a wide range of Bayesian models from natural-language descriptions alone. As an open-ended system, its capability can continue to expand with improvements in the underlying AI agent and the addition of new built-in blocks. The software is available at https://ai4bayescode.com/.

items.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
items.summary: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets. A contrast set asks one question about several versions of an image that differ only in a small region with the evidence and have different answers, so only reading the evidence solves the whole set. CrossRPO rewards solving the whole set, and we prove that it does not reinforce a set answered from common sense. We build contrast sets for training (ViRA-Train) and evaluation (ViRA-Bench) by editing one small object in images of 21 to 120 megapixels, and we photograph further sets with real changes (ViRA-Bench-Real) to exclude editing traces. We train two Visual Reasoning Agents, ViRA-9B and ViRA-27B, with CrossRPO on only about 3,500 items of ViRA-Train each. CrossRPO achieves 63.3% set accuracy on ViRA-Bench at the maximum resolution, against 59.3% for GRPO. ViRA-9B is the most accurate open model of its size on all benchmarks, and ViRA-27B outperforms Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6-Luna, both at their highest thinking level, on most benchmarks.

items.title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
items.summary: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets. We present FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions. Following the Jev formulation, FaceJev answers eight independent questions about facial parts using a shared image encoding and reads anomaly probabilities from the native answer logits. A face is classified as forged if any part is predicted to be abnormal, directly linking the detection result to the part decisions. We construct PartForensics, a dataset of approximately 160k images with binary anomaly targets for the eight facial parts, to supervise these decisions. We further propose FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards. FaceJev outperforms the strongest baseline by 7.25 percentage points on unseen manipulations. Extensive ablation studies validate our design choices and the effectiveness of the main components.

items.title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
items.summary: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors. For 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific tropical cyclones from the 2002-2023 hurricane seasons, we analyze the discussion text and its combination with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields, for forecasting intensity changes at lead times of 24 to 120 hours using three modeling methods. In one approach, an end-to-end deep learning framework for the text shows that the discussions alone offer comparable value for 24-hour intensity forecasts to the SHIPS predictors. Adding discussion information to the SHIPS predictors in an ensemble of five such models reduces the mean absolute error of 24-hour maximum sustained wind forecasts for 2022-2023 cyclones from 9.89 to 8.90 kt, with a confidence interval that excludes zero when whole storms are resampled. The ERA5 wind fields have a minor effect on mean absolute error in wind predictions, and model rankings differ across predicted variables, lead times and model types. We provide prediction intervals for these forecasts, whose coverage falls below the 90% target during rapid intensification. Analysis of the text shows that words related to intensity and intensity change (such as intensify, weaken, eyewall and category) are important for the model predictions. This retrospective study shows the added value of the forecasters' discussions and suggests that multi-modal learning can help understand the predictive contribution of expert human judgment. The reanalysis data differ from real-time analyses, and the discussions are issued at least three hours after the valid time of the other inputs, so these results should not be interpreted operationally.

items.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
items.summary: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks. The mechanism has four main parts. First, binding heads match the relevant text tokens against the image and resolve them into pointers to the matched image region. Second, the same binding heads bind each written answer to the region it came from, and the model turns it into a progress signal: a cursor, the position in the image up to which the list has been written. Third, a select step chooses the nearest unwritten region after the cursor, or stops. Finally, gaze heads execute the chosen pointer and return a concept of what is drawn there, which language heads and the late MLPs turn into a word in the language of the question. We validate each part of this mechanism through causal patching in Qwen3-VL models on a synthetic visual retrieval task, and test our mechanisms against alternative hypotheses. We further show that the mechanism holds across input formats, natural photographs, and languages, and that its binding, relay, and gaze heads appear at every model size from 2B to 32B. This work allows us to investigate how a VLM turns a question and an image into a sequence of answers, layer by layer and token by token. More broadly, it opens a way to study how models plan over complex multi-step tasks with long rollouts. Our project is available at https://plan.baulab.info/

items.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent
items.summary: Continual reinforcement learning requires adaptation to changing conditions while preserving performance under previously encountered dynamics. It was investigated whether specialists generated by evolutionary search can provide a reusable memory when combined with environment detection and failure-driven search. The Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent (ENA) evolves small neural networks without gradients, archives selected policies by detected dynamic regime, and retrieves them through Bayesian policy reuse. The architecture was evaluated in non-stationary CartPole and HalfCheetah environments. In the 30-replicate CartPole ablation, the complete architecture achieved a mean success rate of 83.2% across the five test environments. Among variants that learned the harder CartPole environments, the complete architecture showed the most consistent retention. A selection ablation also showed that the retrieval rule affected performance. In the evaluated sequences, ENA adapted more slowly than PPO on CartPole and achieved lower returns than SAC on HalfCheetah. The evidence concerns the complete architecture and does not isolate gradient-free optimization as the cause of retention or establish superiority over other continual-learning methods.

items.title: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging
items.summary: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$. We present a simple algorithm based on bagging, which outputs a majority vote of generators that are trained to be CoT-consistent on bootstrap samples of the training data. For binary token sets, it achieves the optimal sample complexity of $O((d_{\mathrm{VC}}+\log(1/δ))/ε)$, independent of the CoT length $T$, where $d_{\mathrm{VC}}$ is the VC dimension of $\mathcal{F}$. For finite token sets $Σ$, the VC dimension is replaced by a multiclass analogue, the Graph dimension $d_{\mathrm{G}}$, and the sample complexity is optimal up to a $\log|Σ|$ factor. The number of generators in the majority-vote ensemble is $O(\log(T/δ))$, and we show that the ensemble can be distilled into a single generator in $\mathcal{F}$ at the expense of $n\log(nT)$ unlabeled prompts.

items.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
items.summary: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. A batch-normalized projector removes this component, so regularization after the projector cannot correct it, and the differences between representations shrink until they collapse. We propose SADL (Supply And Demand Loss), which keeps the original training objective and constrains the encoder directly when needed. SADL compares the representation differences that the projector output demands with the differences the encoder can retain and pass on to the projector, and adds a constraint on the encoder only when supply falls short of demand. It works with different Demand Regularizers and introduces no auxiliary networks, additional trainable parameters, or architectural changes. In single-task and jointly trained four-task LeWorldModel (LeWM) and INTACT experiments, SADL lowers the collapse rate over ten random seeds from 50% to 0%. After one epoch of training, encoder effective rank is 3.4-6.4 times that of the corresponding baseline without SADL, and latent prediction error falls to 1/20-1/303 of it. Without additional tuning, SADL stays robust as its loss weight spans orders of magnitude, and with several Demand Regularizers INTACT exceeds 95% mean search-free control success. On four image datasets, SADL also consistently improves accuracy and stability across random seeds. These results show that matching the representation differences a regularizer demands with the differences the encoder can supply leads to faster and more stable representation learning in control and image classification.

items.title: The Provenance-Privacy Paradox: Can Private Cloud Compute (PCC) Prove That Apple Reference Images Are Not Used for Learning?
items.summary: Apple Reference Image (ARI) combines camera-sensor signatures, Secure Enclave attestation (SEP), cryptographic timestamp bounds, Private Cloud Compute (PCC), and a final post-quantum signature to establish photographic provenance. PCC is central to this process because it validates the secure digital negative and develops authenticated raw sensor measurements into a reference JPEG. Although the secure digital negative is encrypted during transmission, the authorized PCC workload must process the raw pixels in plaintext. This requirement creates a provenance-privacy paradox: cloud processing strengthens the provenance guarantee while giving an Apple-authorized, machine-learning-capable workload access to valuable, hardware-authenticated raw imagery. We argue that workload attestation and transparency-log inclusion verify software identity and authorization but do not, by themselves, prove that an authorized workload cannot learn from or retain information derived from the photograph. We implement this counterexample in a Python- and Docker-based experimental testbed that models relevant ARI and PCC functions. Across 27 public-domain photographs, a baseline workload and a learning-enabled workload both passed the same verification checks and returned byte-for-byte identical JPEGs. However, the learning-enabled workload retained a first-layer gradient of approximately 48 KB from which its 64 x 64 input was reconstructed with a maximum absolute per-pixel error of 6 x 10^-8. The additional processing overhead was small relative to image decoding and processing. These results do not demonstrate that Apple currently trains on ARI photographs or reproduce production PCC, but identify non-learning and non-retention as independently verifiable assurance requirements.

items.title: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
items.summary: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market. To assess how such roles differ in their work and industry applications, we design and compare two methods based on deep learning and transformer representations using 36,081 early-career job postings collected from LinkedIn in the United States between December 2025 and October 2026. We first apply PERC, short for Preprocessing (P), Embedding (E), Dimensionality Reduction (R) and Clustering (C). We employ GPT-6 Luna to classify job description passages into Team context, Role task and Qualifications. We then create combinations of these sections and examine whether embedding and clustering the segmented passages produce meaningful semantic clusters about different job roles. We use Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) to rank observed differences between embedding distributions and employ a pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) to extract features from layer-19 representations of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Lastly, we employ GPT-6 Luna to come up with hypotheses about job roles' feature patterns, and GPT-6.1 Terra to investigate whether those patterns exist in held-out job descriptions from unseen companies. Some example findings include Data Scientist advertisements placing more emphasis on machine learning model development, Data Analyst advertisements on reporting business performance, and Machine Learning Engineer advertisements on applying developed models in real-world settings. We also observe differences in the applications described by Data Analyst and Business Analyst advertisements across selected months, although our dataset's scale and uneven coverage limit their interpretation. Overall, we present a realistic application of SAEs and PERC to unstructured textual data and examine how automated insight extraction could support manual analysis of job descriptions.

items.title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
items.summary: Training with MXFP4, a 4-bit microscaling format, is non-deterministic: identical inputs can produce different results across parallelism layouts and GPU vendors. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree. We present CertiSum to make MXFP4 training bitwise invariant across runs, parallelism layouts, and GPU vendors. Its key insight is that native FP32 accumulation of MXFP4 products is often already exact for every summation order. CertiSum collects statistics during quantization to certify native matrix multiplication results, recomputes uncertified outputs exactly, and uses exact kernels directly where certification rarely succeeds. CertiSum keeps quantization blocks unchanged across layouts and merges partial sums without rounding, including in attention and weight-gradient computation. In 200-step Qwen3-8B-Base experiments, CertiSum preserves training states bit for bit across AMD MI350X and NVIDIA GB200 and across changes in data, tensor, and context parallelism on MI350X. Across three 8B--14B models on FineWeb-Edu using MI350X, it adds 11.8--60.5% to training-step latency relative to its non-exact MXFP4 counterpart at the larger evaluated input shapes, with speedups of up to $1.24\times$ over BF16 and $1.70\times$ over deterministic BF16.

items.title: Escaping Alignment: A Physical Trap Model of Best-of-N Jailbreaking
items.summary: Best-of-$N$ jailbreaking (BoN) bypasses safeguards of aligned models by drawing $N$ independent augmentations of an unsafe prompt and sampling $M$ completions of each. Previous works have shown that the attack success rate (ASR) seems to follow a power-law in $N$, which we challenge. The exponent drifts with $N$, and the reported exponential crossover is consistent with a finite-size effect of the adversarial dataset. Little work has been done to explore the entire two-budget ($N, M$) attack surface as well as its dependence on the generation temperature $T$. We introduce a simple barrier model where each prompt has a baseline safety level and each augmentation a random thermally activated barrier. Then five numbers, each backed by an interpretable safety mechanism, determine the entire ($N, M$) attack surface. They extrapolate predictions from $N \leq 100$ to $N = 10^4$, collapse five distinct models on the same scaling function and predict ASR at different temperatures from the one they were fitted at. The extrapolation holds under two automated judges and on held-out prompts.

items.title: A Systematic Analysis of Out-of-Distribution Detection Under Representation and Training Paradigm Shifts
items.summary: We present a systematic benchmark of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection confidence scoring functions (CSFs) through a representation-centric lens. Our study spans CNN and ViT backbones, multiple training paradigms, four image-classification source datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SuperCIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet), and OOD datasets grouped into near, mid, and far regimes based on CLIP-derived semantic distances. To compare CSFs across these settings, we employ a rank-based pipeline of Friedman and Conover tests that identifies top cliques of statistically indistinguishable winners under threshold-free ranking metrics (AURC and AUGRC). The main empirical finding is that the family of CSFs that are competitive detectors correlates with characteristics of the learned representation. For both CNNs and ViTs, simple probabilistic scores dominate misclassification detection. On CNNs, margin-based scores are strongest in near-OOD regimes, while geometry-aware scores such as NNGuide, fDBD, and CTM become more competitive as shift severity increases. On fine-tuned ViTs, the top cliques are led mainly by reconstruction- and residual-based scores. To interpret these ranking shifts, we analyze the last-layer representation using Neural Collapse (NC) metrics. The resulting picture is consistent across architectures: prototype- and boundary-aware scores become stronger when the representation is more collapsed and better aligned with classifier weights, whereas weaker-collapse regimes favor gradient- and manifold-based scores. Building on these insights, we propose two contributions: a simple PCA-based projection-filtering procedure that improves detector performance, and an approach that uses only the NC measurements of a trained classifier to predict its competitive out-of-distribution detector shortlist, without OOD data for that classifier and without knowledge of the shift.

items.title: ScenarioForge: Resource-Grounded Generation and Execution Validation of Cyber Exercises
items.summary: Cyber-range and capture-the-flag scenario construction remains labor-intensive because authors must coordinate infrastructure, vulnerable services, attack paths, artifacts, and success conditions. LLMs can propose detailed exercises, but plausible descriptions do not guarantee deployable software or verifiable objectives. We present ScenarioForge, which turns high-level requirements into resource-grounded topologies, services, traffic, segmentation, and challenge chains, then instantiates and validates them in the Common Open Research Emulator (CORE). The ScenarioForge Execution Dataset contains 226 materialized scenarios covering 294 Vulhub images and all 85 custom-built challenge-resource generators developed with our AI-assisted scaffolding. All 226 passed construction, preview, sequencing, deployment, strict runtime validation, and live artifact checks; their 867 steps, each an individually verifiable challenge objective, comprise 457 vulnerability-backed and 410 generated-resource-backed instances. In a separate 50-prompt matched benchmark, ScenarioForge+Qwen3.8 and ScenarioForge+GPT5.6 each achieved 50/50 (100%) topology/build success and 160/160 intent fields; direct frontier generation reached 41/50 builds and 147/160 fields only with the full cumulative scaffold: structure, vocabulary, policy, and container-image guidance. The test still omitted ScenarioForge's downstream challenge-resource generation, dependency/flag sequencing, deployment, and live validation. The artifacts support operationally rich, reproducible exercises for training and evaluation.

items.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. However, tool metadata used for discovery and selection is not, by itself, necessarily bound to a verified provider identity. This paper studies this gap as tool-provider misbinding: a failure in which a request intended for a legitimate provider is instead resolved to an attacker-controlled tool. The attacker does not compromise the host, LLM, legitimate server, or network channel; it only operates another MCP server that advertises tools with chosen metadata. We formulate tool provider misbinding as an attacker-controlled tool-selection optimization problem and evaluate it in a controlled MCP environment across five LLM-based clients. The results show that interactions drive misbinding. The strongest failures occur when exact-name collision, task-aligned description, and compatible schema reinforce one another, but authority-enhanced descriptions with compatible schema can also cause wrong-provider execution or unresolved provider ambiguity without name collision. Different models expose the same provider-binding weakness differently, including attacker-controlled provider selection, clarification requests, and unstable or inconsistent provider resolution.

items.title: What Does CLIP Learn for Regional Geolocalization? Probing Visual Cues and Scene Configuration After Adaptation
items.summary: Large collections of street-view imagery provide rich visual information about urban environments, but extracting fine-grained geographic information from such data remains challenging. In particular, fine-grained regional geolocalization is challenging because nearby areas often share coarse geographic cues. We study regional geolocalization within a metropolitan area and ask whether pretrained CLIP features are sufficient for regional discrimination, and what visual information supports performance after adaptation. Using 9,085 street-view images from eight Greater Los Angeles regions, we compare zero-shot CLIP, frozen-encoder readouts, partial encoder updating, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), and full fine-tuning. Frozen readouts remain near the 39.03% zero-shot accuracy, whereas encoder adaptation achieves 75.94-82.10%. Full fine-tuning also reduces the mean distance to the predicted region center from 12.30 km to 3.86 km. We probe these gains through semantic cue removal, appearance reduction using edge maps and blur, and scene-configuration disruption using patch scrambling. Adapted models achieve higher edge and blur accuracy and switch 42.92-45.56% of predictions after scrambling, compared with 10.79-14.60% for frozen methods. However, adaptation does not improve the fraction of performance retained after appearance reduction, while vegetation and sky remain influential. A Caltech101 control further shows that scrambling sensitivity is not unique to geolocalization. Overall, encoder adaptation substantially improves nearby-region discrimination and is associated with greater sensitivity to intact scene configuration, without evidence that coarse structure alone becomes sufficient for prediction. These conclusions concern viewpoint variation near known locations rather than geographically disjoint generalization.

items.title: DynSurvX: Time-Resolved Explanations for Dynamic Survival Predictions
items.summary: Recent survival models integrating longitudinal data achieve strong predictive performance, but their predictions are often difficult to interpret, limiting their clinical use. We propose DynSurvX, a model-agnostic explainability framework for dynamic survival prediction with mixed static and longitudinal covariates. Based on Shapley values, DynSurvX introduces a hierarchical two-phase strategy that first identifies influential longitudinal features and then adaptively refines their temporal importance, enabling fine-grained explanations while reducing computational cost. The framework provides time-resolved explanations that evolve as new patient data become available. Experiments on simulated and two clinical datasets show varying agreement with theoretical importance across prediction models, with closer agreement for better-performing models, alongside clinically interpretable insights in real-world settings. It remains robust across prediction settings and reduces computation time by 41--80\% relative to the temporal explanation baseline, making dynamic explanations practical.

items.title: Perceive-to-Reason: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning
items.summary: Fine-grained visual reasoning remains challenging for vision-language models, especially when small but critical visual cues are buried in high-resolution images. Existing approaches rely on repeated cropping or test-time visual search to introduce local evidence, but they typically do not explicitly distinguish perception from reasoning. In this paper, we propose Perceive-to-Reason (P2R), a unified framework that formulates fine-grained visual reasoning as a two-stage process: the model first localizes question-relevant evidence as a Perceiver, and then answers the question as a Reasoner based on the annotated image and cropped regions. To better align training with this decoupled formulation, we further introduce Perception-Reasoning Alternating GRPO (PRA-GRPO), a role-aware reinforcement learning strategy that alternates between perception-focused and reasoning-focused updates using only final-answer supervision. Built on top of Qwen3-VL-Instruct-2B/4B/8B, P2R consistently improves performance across model scales. In particular, P2R-4B achieves 93.2% on V-Star, 81.9% on HR-Bench-4K, and 80.5% on HR-Bench-8K, substantially outperforming its corresponding backbone. Further experiments show that the benefits of P2R extend beyond high-resolution benchmarks to broader multimodal reasoning tasks.
