items.title: Clinician Assessment of Laryngeal Disease with Auditory AI before Laryngoscopy: A Paired Reader Study
items.summary: Background: Before laryngoscopy, clinicians assess the likely cause of hoarseness and whether to suspect a precancerous or malignant lesion. Whether voice-based artificial intelligence (AI) supports pre-laryngoscopic categorization is unknown. Methods: We developed an auditory large language model that generates a patient-level assessment card (provisional category, voice-quality ratings, and rationale) and a prespecified malignancy alert from voice recordings, patient information, and acoustic measures obtained before laryngoscopy at one center. We evaluated both in a held-out test set and a later cohort. In a sequential reader study, 32 otolaryngology clinicians categorized held-out cases without AI and, 1 to 2 weeks later, reviewed their initial categories with the card (without the alert). Results: Across 800 paired assessments, reader accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after review (difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed from incorrect to correct and 43 from correct to incorrect (ratio, 2.30; 95% CI, 1.22 to 5.31). Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect. Provisional-category accuracy was 72% in held-out testing and 67% in temporal validation. The malignancy alert flagged 85.7% and 86.8% of precancerous or malignant lesions. Sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions increased from 53.9% to 75.0% after AI-assisted review (difference, 21.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.3 to 42.0). Conclusions: In this single-center study, clinicians' pre-laryngoscopic categorization accuracy was higher after reviewing the AI assessment card, although the sequential design cannot fully separate AI assistance from reassessment; gains depended on model correctness without clearly selective adoption. Randomized and external evaluations, including of the malignancy alert, are needed.

items.title: Provable Method of Moments for Cryo-EM
items.summary: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional volume in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) from noisy tomographic projections acquired at unknown viewing rotations, drawn independently and uniformly from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. We show that, in a spherical-shell representation satisfying an explicit shell-separation condition, the first three moments generically determine the underlying real volume up to its intrinsic global $\mathrm{O}(3)$ ambiguity. The proof is constructive and yields a frequency-marching procedure that successively recovers the volume. Consequently, consistent recovery in the high-noise regime has sample complexity $n=ω(σ^6)$, where $n$ is the number of observations and $σ^2$ is the noise variance. Numerical experiments validate the constructive recovery scheme under finite sampling and additive noise, and indicate that direct third-moment optimization can succeed beyond the structural assumptions required by the constructive proof.

items.title: Boundary Collisions and Weak Excitation in LQR Policy-Gradient Flows
items.summary: Closed-loop stability concerns all initial states, whereas an LQR cost evaluates only the directions excited by a prescribed initial-state distribution. We study how this distinction affects Euclidean policy-gradient flows. For every nonzero deficient covariance rank, we construct relatively open families of controllable data and open sets of stabilizing initial gains whose exact gradient trajectories reach the stability boundary in finite optimization time. The state Gramian can remain positive definite at every time before collision. By separating the cost contribution of a critical mode, we obtain a local collision criterion based on direction attraction and motion toward the stability boundary. Adding excitation of strength $\varepsilon$ yields matching $Θ(\sqrt\varepsilon)$ bounds on the local minimum stability margin for trajectories that would otherwise collide. For a class of single-input, corank-one systems, these bounds hold over the entire trajectory without a common compact-set assumption. Numerical examples further illustrate the dynamics and scaling laws.

items.title: Machine Learning for Near Real-Time Identification of Wildfire Burned Areas
items.summary: In this article, we present a near real-time method that estimates burned probability anywhere in the world using satellite images. Our approach takes advantage of the state-of-the-art pix2pix model to translate a preprocessed index calculated from Landsat 8/9 images into an approximate of USGS Burn Probability indicating per pixel burn probability. Since this is a machine learning-based approach, it can be automated with a minimum amount of human intervention with significantly less time delays and geographic restrictions compared to other contemporary methods. We include results from our experiments and compare our approximation with the USGS Burn Probability using RMSE score.

items.title: The Grid's Own Language: A Common Information Model Layer for LLM Grid Assistants
items.summary: Assistants built on large language models (LLMs) are entering power system operation. Current designs delegate computations to validated solvers, but the agent still infers the type, role and state of each element from its name and tool-specific formats, and errors propagate to every study. The Common Information Model (CIM), the IEC standard in which operators already exchange network models, defines unambiguously what each element is and how it connects. We propose a CIM layer for LLM grid assistants and implement it in CONDUCTOR, an open-source assistant. Both the agent and its power-system studies read the layer. It labels the provenance of each fact (stated in the data, suggested only by a name, or inferred from topology), loads operators' CGMES models directly, and builds in $\leq$1\,s on the 9,241-bus PEGASE network. Deterministic checks compare every answer with solver results and the layer. On 37 tasks about the CIGRE medium-voltage and IEEE 30-bus networks, the agent gets right 97\,\% of the graded facts with the layer, such as a unit's energy source or a switch's normal state, against 55\,\% without it. We argue that a CIM layer should be a default component of grid assistants.

items.title: LEAF: A Learning-Enabled ADMM Framework for Accelerated Convex Optimization
items.summary: We propose LEAF, a learning-enabled ADMM framework for accelerated convex optimization. The key idea is to approximate the Moreau envelope of the objective function using an Input Convex Neural Network (ICNN), resulting in a learned model that preserves convexity and smoothness. This leads to the proposed Moreau Envelope Learning ADMM (MEL-ADMM) and its splitting variant sMEL-ADMM. Unlike existing approaches that learn high-dimensional operators directly, LEAF learns a scalar-valued Moreau envelope, significantly reducing model complexity and improving data efficiency. The framework accommodates a broad class of convex problems with smooth and non-smooth objectives. By embedding convexity explicitly through the ICNN architecture, the proposed approach maintains high approximation accuracy while preserving key structural properties of the optimization problem. Both MEL-ADMM and sMEL-ADMM are developed with theoretical guarantees of convergence and feasibility under the learned model. Rigorous analysis shows that the proposed methods achieve convergence rates comparable to classical ADMM while reducing per-iteration computational cost. Numerical experiments demonstrate up to an order-of-magnitude speedup over state-of-the-art solvers while maintaining low optimality gaps

items.title: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
items.summary: Benchmarks for scientific image editing test whether a model draws the outcome of a described process, leaving open which representations carry its errors and whether correcting them yields the right quantity. We study this question with an airbrush of fixed deposition profile, under which exchanging rate and duration preserves the dose and should preserve the endpoint, yet changes the edited coverage. Matched-norm activation patches across text positions and denoising stages show that, in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, representations at unchanged text positions (context) carry this discrepancy: early context transfers 3.51 of the 3.98 percentage-point (pp) signed route difference, against 0.09 pp for equal-norm updates at the two changed digits. Early image latents transmit native (unpatched) route differences across two FLUX configurations and OmniGen, while text-position effects depend on configuration. The trace predicts an intervention: share early context between routes while each retains its own digits. On independent English layouts, this reduces the distilled-FLUX absolute route gap from 1.13 to 0.60 pp, outperforms early digit sharing, and improves agreement more than in base FLUX under directly paired tests. Calibrated evaluation, which prescribes an area for each dose, separates this gain from accuracy: sharing the full prompt encoding produces identical route images with target errors of 8-16 pp, and stating the target percentage directly retains a compressed area response. Localization predicts a consistency gain on new layouts, and calibration measures the quantity error that agreement leaves unresolved.

items.title: Wideband Hybrid Beamforming via Programmable Unitary Mixer--TTD RF Networks
items.summary: This paper proposes a wideband hybrid beamforming architecture whose analog front-end consists of fixed unitary mixers interlaced with programmable diagonal phase-shift/true-time-delay (TTD) layers. Under ideal passive-component assumptions, the analog beamformer is semi-unitary on every OFDM subcarrier, so the injected RF-chain power reaches the antenna ports without analog-network loss. We design the phase shifts and delays of the programmable diagonal phase-shift/TTD layers for OFDM sum-rate maximization. Numerical results show that increasing mixer--TTD depth improves the sum rate under ideal component assumptions and a common injected RF-power budget. With component losses included, a shallow design retains an advantage over the evaluated hybrid baselines at low-to-moderate powers, motivating deeper implementations with low accumulated loss.

items.title: WTMOS: A Robust WavLM-Transformer Framework and ViViT Benchmarking for Cross-Corpus Audio MOS Prediction
items.summary: Automatic Mean Opinion Score (MOS) prediction is essential for evaluating large-scale synthetic speech and audio enhancement systems, yet models frequently struggle with domain shift. This study presents WTMOS, a robust WavLM-Transformer framework and Video Vision Transformer (ViViT) benchmarking suite across three architectural configurations: Frozen Self-Supervised Learning (SSL-FRZ), Fine-Tuned SSL (SSL-FT), and ViViT. Evaluation is conducted in two phases: Part I utilizes a consolidated corpus of 130,652 samples across 19 diverse datasets, while Part II focuses on a purified 17-dataset English-only corpus. To assess robustness, a systematic Leave-One-Dataset-Out (LODO) protocol is employed to quantify the generalization gap between seen and unseen distributions. Finally, the top-performing model is benchmarked against 18 state-of-the-art (SOTA) metrics using the ARECHO framework. Results demonstrate that an English-only purified corpus consistently yields higher predictive precision across all architectures. While SSL-FT achieves the highest performance on seen validation data, the SSL-FRZ model provides superior robustness on unseen distributions, achieving a competitive Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.36 on the URGENT 2024 benchmark - closely matching domain-optimized SOTA metrics (MSE 0.30). Although the ViViT architecture remains below SSL-based models in total capacity, it delivers stable results in English-only trials. LODO results confirm that while models perform significantly better on seen samples, frozen SSL embeddings combined with deep Transformer encoders offer the most stable and scalable solution for universal speech quality assessment. To support further research, the top-performing English-only SSL-Transformer model and weights are made publicly available via Hugging Face.

items.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
items.summary: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface configuration. We introduce a functional taxonomy of LLM-enabled wireless resource management strategies and analyze the prompt engineering methodologies employed in recent literature. Furthermore, we develop a generalized analytical framework that categorizes LLM-based optimization architectures, including direct solution generation, closed-loop optimization with external verifiers, and representation encoding within trainable neural pipelines. To demonstrate practical applicability, we present representative case studies on LLM-assisted beam prediction for millimeter-wave systems and adaptive wireless resource allocation. Finally, we discuss emerging hybrid AI approaches for wireless networks.

items.title: Max-Min Throughput in RSMA-Aided SWIPT for Sustainable Internet of Underground Things: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
items.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled wireless-powered underground sensor networks (WPUSNs) allow underground devices (UDs) to harvest radio-frequency energy from a UAV via wireless energy transfer (WET) techniques, enabling sustainable Internet of underground things (IoUT) applications. This paper integrates rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-aided simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) into UAV-enabled WPUSNs to deliver information and energy to UDs. Within this framework, we investigate a max-min fairness problem that jointly optimizes the UAV transmit power, power allocation and message splitting, power-splitting ratios, and time allocation, aiming to maximize the minimum uplink throughput across UDs subject to per-UD downlink throughput requirements and a UAV energy-consumption constraint. To address this non-convex problem under dynamic underground environments, we develop an off-policy deep reinforcement learning approach based on the primal-dual truncated quantile critics (PD-TQC), where a TQC-based reward critic evaluates the fairness objective, cost critics estimate constraint costs, and an actor learns the resource-control policy with adaptive dual-variable updates. Simulations using in-situ soil volumetric water content measurements from a center-pivot irrigation farm demonstrate that PD-TQC achieves the highest annual average minimum uplink throughput compared with four benchmarks while satisfying the per-frame constraints in over 96% of the evaluated frames, and that this throughput advantage is preserved under different Rician factors, numbers of UDs, and downlink throughput thresholds.

items.title: CRFCAN: A Complex-Valued Cross-Domain Residual Network for Joint Channel and Phase Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM Systems
items.summary: The coupling between multipath propagation and phase noise (PN) poses challenges for joint channel and PN estimation in sub-terahertz (sub-THz) cyclic-prefix OFDM systems. This paper proposes CRFCAN, a complex-valued residual FFT convolutional attention network for single-input single-output systems using comb-type pilots only. Its shared backbone alternately refines time- and frequency-domain features through complex-valued residual channel attention and PN-inspired multiplicative updates, producing channel and PN estimates in their respective domains. An unfolded PN refinement tail combines least-squares updates with feature-guided complex-valued CNN corrections. Simulation results show that CRFCAN achieves lower channel estimation error and bit error rate than the evaluated baselines in both training TDL-A/B/E + 3GPP RAN4 and TDL-C/D + 3GPP RAN1 generalization settings, together with lower PN estimation error at medium-to-high signal-to-noise ratios. Further tests without fine-tuning demonstrate its applicability across different data modulations, OFDM parameters, channel models, and PN spectra.

items.title: Sparse Stabilization of Continuous-Time Linear Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Efficient use of communication resources is crucial for stabilizing a networked control system. Employing \emph{sparse inputs} and event-triggered control are efficient ways to utilize communication resources in networked control systems. This work considers the problem of stabilizing a continuous-time linear dynamical system (LDS) using $s$-sparse inputs. For this purpose, we consider \emph{switched} linear feedback control, where we construct a finite number of feedback matrices with at most $s$ nonzero rows. Using switched systems theory, we show that there exists an $s$-sparse input for any sparsity level $s \geq 1$ that ensures stability when the continuous-time LDS is stabilizable. In addition, using our approach, we can compute the required feedback matrices with minimal overhead even if the sparsity budget $s$ varies over time. We also minimize the maximum Frobenius norm of the feedback matrices, yielding sparse inputs with reduced control energy. We show that an upper bound on the control energy required for stabilization using an $s$-sparse input is inversely proportional to $s^2$, while maintaining the same exponential stability rate. Finally, we combine the design of the \emph{sparse inputs} with the event-trigger rule to further reduce communication resource consumption. Our sparse and event-triggered control strategy ensures that any stabilizable continuous-time LDS can be stabilized using $s$-sparse inputs under both state feedback and output feedback, for any $s\geq 1$. We illustrate our theoretical results for the task of stabilizing a mass-spring system.

items.title: ProTTS: End-to-End Prominence-aware Natural and Controllable Text-to-Speech via Automatic Word Stress Discovery
items.summary: Natural speech conveys meaning not only through words, but also through the prominence on a few words. Yet most text-to-speech (TTS) systems remain prominence-unaware, existing prominence-aware TTS require external stress annotations, while unsupervised stress detectors operate in isolation, disconnected from synthesis. This creates a fundamental gap no existing system can automatically discover where stress should be placed, realize it as natural-sounding prosody, and offer user control over emphasis placement, all within a single model. To circumvent this, we propose ProTTS, a unified framework where stress detection emerges from the TTS model itself and, in turn, guides it to synthesize more natural and controllable speech. We incorporate a clustering head into the variance adaptor of FastSpeech_2 that discovers word stress directly from aggregated prosodic features. The discovered stress then drives emphasis variance predictors that modify pitch, energy, and duration for stressed words. The framework is trained end-to-end: TTS reconstruction and clustering losses jointly shape a stress-discriminative feature space without requiring stress labels at any stage. At inference, the same architecture also supports user-controllable emphasis by accepting a custom stress mask. We evaluate ProTTS on ISLE (non-native), LibriTTS, VCTK (native training), and three evaluation benchmarks (Tatoeba, TinyStress-15k, EmphAssess). Listeners prefer ProTTS over the baseline with a MOS of 3.96 vs. 3.12 and 83.5% preference rate. For stress detection, ProTTS achieves 0.839/0.861 F1 on ISLE (German/Italian L2), outperforming unsupervised (0.70) and supervised (0.82) baselines, and 0.933 F1 in zero-shot transfer to Tatoeba.

items.title: Computing GR(1) Assume-Guarantee Contracts
items.summary: Assume-guarantee contracts provide a set of algebraic operations that enable the efficient compositional design and analysis of complex engineering systems. The explicit computation of these operations at component interfaces is currently supported only for some logics lacking a notion of time. This paper develops theory and algorithms to compute these operations when the contracts are expressed in the GR(1) modulo theory. The key challenge is the computation of two quantifier elimination problems for temporal formulas. We develop context-aided variable elimination procedures on GR(1)-modulo formulas, establish their soundness, characterize subproblem-wise optimal solutions within an admissible class of formulas, and use the procedures to compute contract operations, including composition and quotient. We implement the resulting framework in Pacti, automating compositional reasoning over GR(1) contracts. Finally, we demonstrate the framework on an automated emergency-braking case study, where we compute system-level contracts and expose compatibility conditions arising from the interaction of component specifications. Experiments on synthetic families show that the cost is governed by the number of eliminated variables and liveness conjuncts, and a comparison with exact automata-based elimination shows complementary scaling.

items.title: Distance-Certified Polyak-type Stepsizes for Subgradient Methods under Hölder Growth
items.summary: In this paper, we consider nonsmooth convex optimization under a H{ö}lder growth condition, with quadratic growth and weak sharp minima as two important special cases. Existing subgradient methods often employ predetermined decaying stepsize schedules, whereas the classical Polyak stepsize selects its stepsize adaptively but requires knowledge of the optimal value. We introduce a new distance-certified subgradient method (\DCSG) that follows a one-step optimization principle analogous to that underlying the Polyak stepsize, without requiring the optimal value. Specifically, \DCSG{} maintains a valid upper certificate for the current squared distance to the solution set. The method selects each stepsize by minimizing the worst-case upper bound on the next squared distance over all distances consistent with this certificate. We show that the resulting minimax problem admits a closed-form solution, yielding an explicit adaptive stepsize update. Under uniformly bounded subgradients, \DCSG{} improves upon the convergence rate of the classical subgradient method and matches the state-of-the-art rates for Lipschitz convex optimization under H{ö}lder growth. In particular, it achieves linear convergence under sharp growth. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of \DCSG.

items.title: Rethinking Post-Training for Expressive Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
items.summary: Zero-shot voice cloning typically emphasizes preserving the timbre and prosodic characteristics of a reference speaker. However, in real-world use, speech should adapt its delivery to the target text rather than remain tied to a fixed speaking style. In this work, we formulate this problem as text-adaptive prosody synthesis for zero-shot voice cloning and study how post-training can endow a cloning model with this capability. We develop a three-stage framework. First, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) provides a cold start by aligning the model with text-appropriate expressive speech. Second, Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) jointly optimizes prosodic expressiveness, acoustic quality, intelligibility, and speaker similarity. Finally, context-conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) enables self-improvement by transferring expressive behavior from strong-reference to weak-reference conditions. On Qwen3-TTS, our framework improves Emotion from 18.5 to 81.2 and Paralinguistics from 38.4 to 73.9. Extensive ablations validate the role of each stage.

items.title: Full-Time-Scale Power Management for Hybrid AC/DC/DS Microgrid with Dynamic Concatenation and Global Equivalent Circuit Modeling
items.summary: Hybrid AC/DC/distributed energy storage (DS) microgrids (MGs) provide an effective solution for improving power accessibility and supply reliability in remote and isolated areas.Conventional static power management aims to proportionally allocate power based on unit ratings by scheduling the operation of interlinking converters (ILCs). Recent studies on transient power management emphasize inertia coupling among subgrids by dynamically regulating ILC power flows, thereby enhancing the system resilience against disturbances. In existing literature, these two objectives are normally addressed in a separate fashion and a unified scheme to simultaneously achieve them is rarely found. Furthermore, conventional static management neglects droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations which may seriously compromise the safe operation of sensitive loads. To address these limitations, in this paper, we proposes a full-timescale (FTS) power management for the hybrid MG is proposed.Autonomous frequency/voltage restoration controls are deployed in each subgrid to eliminate droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations, based on which a novel FTS dynamic concatenator is proposed to chain up the static power sharing and transient inertia sharing across different timescales. Moreover, a novel global equivalent circuit model (GECM) is presented to interpret the holistic hybrid system from electrical circuit perspective. Then the static and transient performance of the complex hybrid AC/DC/DS MG can be quantitatively characterized to facilitate easier engineering practices. In-house experiments validate that the proposed FTS dynamic concatenator ensures static power sharing and transient inertia sharing through the ILC in full timescales.

items.title: Topology-Transferable Detection of Deep-Learning False Data Injection Attacks Through Residual-Energy Separation
items.summary: Deep learning (DL) false data injection (FDI) attacks can evade both bad data detection (BDD) and data-driven (DD) detectors in AC power system state estimation (SE), and DD detectors lose effectiveness after a topology change unless they are retrained. We argue that BDD fails in its decision rule, not in its statistic. A reconstruction-based DL generator pursues stealth by fitting the measurements closely, and because such a generator tends to act as a denoiser, the attacked residual energy can fall into the lower tail that BDD never inspects. The weighted-least-squares (WLS) residual applies the same projector construction to the noise and to the attack error, and under a spectral suppression condition we prove that the expected residual energies of normal and attacked measurements are separated by a topology-independent margin. Empirically, a rule learned on the residual energy at one topology transfers without retraining and keeps mean cross-topology F1 above 0.98 on the IEEE 14-bus, 39-bus, 57-bus, and 118-bus systems, while a raw measurement DD detector collapses.

items.title: Set-based State Estimation for Unknown Dynamical Systems from Noisy Output Data with Probabilistic Guarantees
items.summary: We develop a methodology for set-based state estimation from noisy input-output trajectories, without a predefined model structure for the unknown state dynamics or access to training state measurements. We derive a bound on the state set diameter that depends on the sensor map and leverage it as a surrogate to formulate a tractable linear program balancing state set tightness against output trajectory coverage. Combining this certificate with deterministic or probabilistically certified measurement noise sets and leveraging the results from scenario optimization with relaxation, we provide joint a posteriori probabilistic guarantees for state inclusion and state set diameter. Numerical simulations corroborate our developed theoretical guarantees.

items.title: Behavioral Denoising: A New Perspective on Nonlinear Behavioral Control Inspired by Closed-Form Diffusion Policies
items.summary: Diffusion policies have become a dominant approach to imitation learning in robotics. Recent work suggests that, in the low-data regime, they largely retrieve or combine the demonstrated actions, which the closed-form diffusion policy does explicitly. This closely resembles behavioral control, where future inputs are formed as linear combinations of recorded trajectories. In this work, we make this connection precise: we show that the weights with which the closed-form diffusion policy combines the demonstrated actions are the unique solution of a regularized behavioral control problem. Building on this connection, we propose an algorithm, termed $χ^2$-projected behavioral denoising, which is a training-free method that combines nearby trajectory data with a limit on extrapolation when the data offer little support. It shows encouraging results on four nonlinear control tasks compared to recent nonlinear behavioral control methods. We hope that this connection offers a useful perspective for understanding both data-driven control and diffusion policies. Code and more visualizations can be found at https://github.com/RoboticExplorationLab/behavioral-denoising.

items.title: Real-Time Air Pollution Monitoring and Tracking via Adaptive Density-Driven Multi-UAV Coordination
items.summary: Accurate and timely air pollution monitoring and tracking are critical for protecting public health and supporting effective environmental management. This paper presents an adaptive Density-Driven Control (D$^2$C) framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions. The proposed framework extends the D$^2$C strategy to guide UAV trajectories based on predictive pollutant propagation and dynamically updated reference densities. A sensor-driven surrogate plume update mechanism is employed, in which reference samples are propagated using locally sensed concentration gradients and wind estimates through gradient attraction, wind advection, inter-sample repulsion, and stochastic diffusion, enabling UAVs to maintain an accurate spatio-temporal representation of the pollution field. The framework utilizes a coordinated structure where individual UAVs share their local measurements with a central coordinator to maintain a unified set of reference samples, facilitating systematic target allocation and trajectory planning. Simulation results under both mild and strong wind conditions demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of Sinkhorn distance. Specifically, in scenarios where the plume drifts beyond a fixed monitoring domain under high-velocity, time-varying wind fields, the tested baseline methods fail to maintain tracking, whereas the proposed D$^2$C framework successfully adapts to the evolving distribution. These findings highlight D$^2$C as an efficient and resilient solution for atmospheric monitoring in dynamic environments.

items.title: Physics-Grounded STL Monitoring from Image Observations
items.summary: Robotic manipulation missions must satisfy timed and conditional requirements that can be expressed in signal temporal logic (STL). While a practical means of monitoring these requirements is from camera images, this is challenging because STL robustness depends on physical margins, such as distances and clearances, that are not directly observed. Rather than learning a separate visual monitor for each formula, we learn a shared latent representation from multi-view images and decode physically meaningful margins for individual predicates. Co-training the encoder with predicate decoders increases the certification rate from 58.7% to 96.3% compared with a frozen encoder, despite nearly unchanged predicate sign accuracy. STL semantics then compose these margins into robustness estimates for any bounded formula over the trained predicates, without retraining. We further calibrate the decoding errors of selected STL clauses using conformal prediction, yielding two-sided intervals that certify both satisfaction and violation and propagate through interval STL to any formula composed from the clauses. In simulated kitchen missions (LIBERO), our monitor correctly predicts satisfaction or violation in 98.9% of 4662 evaluations across 18 unseen formulas. For missions lasting up to 17 min, calibrated bounds establish satisfaction or violation for 96.9% of missions without incorrect conclusions. A single calibration also provides simultaneous 91.0% coverage across all 255 conjunctions of eight clauses, allowing new formulas without recalibration.

items.title: Inequality-Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode Control
items.summary: We present COSMIC (Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode for Inequality Constraints), a continuous-time solver for inequality-constrained optimization. COSMIC couples primal gradient-flow dynamics with multiplier dynamics derived from sliding mode control laws on a manifold defined by the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister function. We prove that COSMIC's trajectories reach this manifold in finite time from any primal initial point, after which the dynamics reduces to the gradient flow of a logarithmic barrier function. This yields a control-theoretic interpretation of barrier methods while allowing infeasible initialization. For strongly convex problems, we further establish exponential convergence to the minimizer. To address the numerical stiffness that arises in discretization, we develop a modified discrete-time algorithm. We validate COSMIC across various machine learning applications, demonstrating its ability to solve optimization problems accurately while scaling effectively to high-dimensional settings.

items.title: Low-Voltage Ride-Through in AI Data Centers via Coordinated Battery and Computing Load Control
items.summary: The ability of large AI data centers to ride through grid voltage sags is critical to power system stability and reliability. This paper frames data center low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) as a DC-link power balance problem. Once the rectifier reaches its current limit, the power drawn from the grid decreases in proportion to the grid voltage. The DC-link capacitor can supply the resulting power deficit only briefly before the DC-link voltage falls low enough to trigger undervoltage protection tripping. To address this issue, this paper proposes effective control strategies for coordinating uninterruptible power supply (UPS) battery and computing load curtailment to offset the power deficit and enable LVRT at minimum control cost. Three control scenarios are studied: UPS battery support alone, computing load curtailment alone, and the coordinated use of both resources. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations using the TAMU-ERCOT AI data center model demonstrate that battery support and the coordinated strategy achieve LVRT for all tested sags, including a near-zero-voltage fault, while load curtailment alone rides through moderate voltage sags.

items.title: WAXAL: A Large-Scale Multilingual African Language Speech Corpus
items.summary: Recent advances in speech technology predominantly favor high-resource languages, leaving speakers of Sub-Saharan African languages underserved. To bridge this divide, we introduce WAXAL, an open, large-scale speech dataset spanning 27 African languages representing over 100 million speakers. WAXAL comprises over 14,100 hours of speech collected in partnership with African academic and community organizations to build local research capacity: an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) corpus with 2,340 hours of transcribed, image-prompted natural speech across 19 languages (plus ~11,760 untranscribed hours) and a studio-quality Text-to-Speech (TTS) corpus of ~247 hours across 15 language configurations. We empirically benchmark three architecturally distinct ASR models -- Gemma 3n 2B, Whisper-Large-v3, and MMS-1B-all -- across the 19 ASR languages on strictly speaker-disjoint splits. Fine-tuning on WAXAL yields substantial gains, reducing macro-average WER by up to 58% for Whisper-Large-v3, 56% for Gemma 3n 2B, and 17% for MMS-1B-all (and Character Error Rate by up to 70%). WAXAL-fine-tuned models generalize zero-shot to three out-of-distribution benchmarks: FLEURS, Mozilla Common Voice, and Sunbird SALT. Finally, an LLM-as-judge semantic evaluation confirms that fine-tuning preserves speaker intent beyond surface-level transcription metrics. WAXAL is released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/WaxalNLP.

items.title: Floorplan-Context-Aware Cross-Environment Human Activity Recognition from mmWave Radar Point Clouds
items.summary: Human activity recognition (HAR) models based on mmWave radar point clouds and trained in controlled open spaces often experience performance degradation when deployed in furnished rooms. We propose a Floorplan-Context-Aware (FCA) HAR enhancement method that augments the input with subject-furniture relative position information to improve cross-environment performance. Because existing mmWave point-cloud datasets lack registered floorplans, we introduce a pseudo-landmark augmentation strategy for training the FCA model. In cross-environment evaluation on the mm-ADL-Home dataset, FCA achieves 77.70% accuracy and 65.49% macro-F1, improving upon the point-cloud-only direct-transfer baseline by 10.73 and 10.05 percentage points, respectively, and exceeding the strongest evaluated adaptation baseline by 7.37 and 6.27 percentage points. At deployment, FCA requires only a one-time registration of furniture landmarks, with no target-domain activity annotations or model weight updates.

items.title: Image Rotation Angle Estimation: Five Circular-Aware Methods Across Sixteen Architectures
items.summary: Automatic image rotation estimation is a key preprocessing step in many vision pipelines, yet challenging because angles have circular topology, creating boundary discontinuities that hinder standard regression. We present a comprehensive study of five circular-aware methods for global orientation estimation: three regression based (direct angle with circular loss, unit vector, phase-shifting coder) and two classification based (angular binning, circular Gaussian distribution). Using transfer learning from ImageNet-pretrained models, we evaluate them across sixteen modern architectures and two data regimes of natural images, small-scale DRC-D and large-scale COCO. Classification approaches are the stronger family, attaining the lowest error on thirteen of the sixteen DRC-D backbones. The decisive ingredient is supervision that encodes angular neighborhood structure: plain cross-entropy lacks it and fails intermittently, while circular smooth labels (CSL) eliminate every observed training failure and reach the lowest DRC-D error, 0.81° mean absolute error (MAE). On COCO, the common rotate-and-crop protocol leaks the applied angle through the rotated JPEG block grid, a shortcut that the classification heads learned and the regression heads largely did not. Re-encoding every training view after rotation suppresses it. Under this trace-free protocol and on re-encoded test views, classification again leads on all three backbones tested, and the circular Gaussian distribution (CGD) with ConvNeXt V2 Base reaches 3.76° on COCO 2017 (three-run mean), against 6.09° for the strongest prior model on the same views. CSL and CGD are also the cheapest methods to train.

items.title: Towards Probabilistically Safe Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Deployment on Humanoid and Aerial Robots
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables robots to acquire complex skills, but standard RL formulations do not guarantee that learned policies satisfy safety constraints, which limits their use in safety-critical settings. Existing safe RL methods with provable guarantees typically support only restricted classes of constraints and require unbiased estimators of the objective and constraint functions, which prevents their direct integration with state-of-the-art algorithms such as proximal policy optimization (PPO). In this paper, we extend the recently introduced robust safe gradient flow-based reinforcement learning (RSGF-RL) framework to overcome these limitations. Our formulation accommodates a general class of trajectory-level safety constraints, including chance constraints such as collision avoidance with a prescribed probability, and our analysis allows for biased value and gradient estimators. We show that, with high probability, the constraint violation throughout training is bounded by the estimator bias plus a term that vanishes as the number of rollouts grows, and decays to this level if the initial policy is unsafe. We also establish the convergence properties of the iterates to approximate KKT points of the original safe RL problem. Finally, we show that RSGF-RL implemented with PPO-style estimates enables zero-shot sim-to-real deployment of whole-body control policies on a Unitree G1 humanoid and collision-free waypoint navigation on a Crazyflie drone.

items.title: Impact of Wind-Solar-Battery Growth on Electricity Prices: Reserve Scarcity and Transmission Congestion
items.summary: This paper asks whether sequential wind, solar, and battery storage additions that eliminate unserved energy also remove modeled reserve scarcity and transmission congestion. Thirty-one cumulative portfolio states are evaluated on a modified IEEE 24-bus system for a constructed stressed day using a 24-hour day-ahead unit commitment model with network constraints, co-optimized energy and upward reserve, chronological battery storage, and an approximation of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas operating reserve demand curve. The thermal baseline has 106 MWh of unserved energy, whereas 450 MW of wind is sufficient to serve all demand. However, with 1,500 MW of wind, the hourly modeled reserve scarcity price still reaches \$5,000/MWh because wind output declines after the system peak. Adding 1,800 MW of solar reduces the load weighted daily average modeled reserve scarcity price from \$1,136.2/MWh to \$101.2/MWh and confines modeled reserve scarcity to three evening hours. Adding 250 MW/1,000 MWh of battery storage further lowers the average to \$4.3/MWh and reduces wind curtailment from 631 MWh to 306 MWh. Transmission congestion nevertheless remains: all residual wind curtailment occurs at bus 21, wind capture prices at buses 21 and 23 differ by \$31.8/MWh, and identical battery storage plants yield normalized net energy market revenues of \$201/(MW$\cdot$day) and \$121/(MW$\cdot$day) at buses 19 and 21, respectively. These results show that unserved energy, modeled reserve scarcity, and locational congestion effects measure distinct operating conditions and should be evaluated separately but interpreted together.

items.title: AC Assessment of DC Power Flow Screening for Data Center Hosting Capacity and Siting
items.summary: A screening procedure based on direct current (DC) power flow estimates the data center hosting capacity of a candidate bus, termed the DC-screened capacity, and selects the generator commitment that supports it. This paper assesses that estimate under the alternating current (AC) network model. With the selected commitment fixed, an AC optimal power flow reoptimizes dispatch and voltages to find the largest data center load the bus can carry, termed the AC-assessed capacity. On a synthetic Texas system with 123 buses, the DC-screened capacity exceeds the AC-assessed capacity at 113 buses. Across all 123, the ratio of DC-screened to AC-assessed capacity has a median of 143% (a 43% overestimate) and a maximum of 1,070%. At these 113 buses, the DC-screened capacity violates a branch apparent power limit or a generator reactive power limit in the AC model, two limits the DC model omits. The overestimate changes decisions: a 1-GW project passes DC screening at every bus but exceeds the AC-assessed capacity at 37, and the bus ranked first by DC screening has 205.5 MW less AC-assessed capacity than the bus ranked second. Reporting the AC-assessed capacity beside each DC-screened capacity lets planners reject oversized projects or choose better sites.

items.title: A Connectively Stable and Robust DAPI Control Scheme for Islanded Networks of Microgrids
items.summary: The transition towards clean energy and the introduction of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) are giving rise to the emergence of Microgrids (MGs) and Networks of MGs (NMGs). MGs and NMGs can operate autonomously in islanded mode. However, they face challenges in terms of secondary level frequency and voltage regulation, due to the variable nature of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and loads. Distributed-Averaging Proportional-Integral (DAPI) control has been proposed in the literature for distributed frequency and voltage control of droop-controlled DERs, but it might not guarantee robustness to cyber-physical disturbances. To address this, we propose a robust DAPI frequency and voltage control scheme that ensures robustness using the concept of connective stability, along with the invariant ellipsoid technique for disturbance rejection. The proposed scheme adds additional degrees of freedom to determine the strength of distributed control, providing an option for more robust action. Simulation of an NMG model in MATLAB/Simulink consisting of 3 MGs and 5 DERs shows that the proposed scheme minimizes frequency and voltage deviations during cyber-physical disturbance events compared to the baseline, dissipativity-based and H-infinity-based techniques.

items.title: Quantification and Regulation of Energy Reserves for Distributed Frequency and Voltage Control of Cyber-Physical Microgrids
items.summary: The introduction of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) has led to the formation of cyber-physical Microgrids (MGs) and Networks of MGs (NMGs). MGs and NMGs can operate in islanded mode, transforming the grid into a more distributed system. This has led to extensive studies in the literature on distributed hierarchical control strategies. Previous works have proposed distributed secondary level frequency and voltage regulation control schemes for Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)- based Grid-Forming (GFM) inverters with State of Charge (SoC) balancing. However, control applications in terms of service-based reserves and local resource adequacy in MGs are largely unexplored. Therefore, this paper proposes a BESS-based GFM inverter energy reserves framework, to quantify reserves for hierarchical control operation. Additionally, to partially regulate the proposed energy reserves, we propose the formulation of a modified Distributed-Averaging Proportional-Integral (DAPI) controller with regulation energy reserve consensus. Modal analysis is performed to demonstrate the stability guarantees of energy consensus under simplified assumptions. Cyber-physical Controller Hardware-In-the-Loop (CHIL) simulation is performed on an MG topologically based on the IEEE 13 bus test feeder system in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed scheme results illustrate effective frequency and voltage regulation along with improved power and energy sharing across droop-controlled and Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) controlled inverters

items.title: Autonomous and Distributed Synchronization and Restoration of an Islanded Network of Microgrids
items.summary: The transition towards clean energy and the introduction of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) are leading to the formation of Microgrids (MGs) and Networks of MGs (NMGs). MGs and NMGs can operate autonomously in islanded mode, which requires Grid-Forming (GFM) IBRs that can perform black start, synchronization, restoration and regulation. However, such IBRs can face synchronization instability issues, which might be worsened by inadequate secondary level frequency and voltage regulation. Accordingly, we propose an autonomous and distributed synchronization and restoration scheme using Distributed-Averaging Proportional-Integral (DAPI) control. To validate the proposed method, we model and simulate a high-fidelity islanded and modified IEEE 123 bus system, modeled as an NMG consisting of 7 MGs. The MATLAB/Simulink simulation results demonstrate an effective autonomous soft- start, synchronization, connection and regulation procedure using DAPI control and distributed breaker operation logic.

items.title: Cooperative Gradient Estimation for Multi-Robot Source Seeking with Heteroskedastic Measurements
items.summary: This paper proposes a novel approach for localizing the source of a three-dimensional scalar field using a team of heterogeneous cooperative mobile robots. Each robot measures the field intensity at its location and shares the information within the team. Measurement noise is explicitly considered, and heterogeneity arises from robot-dependent sensing accuracies, leading to heteroskedastic data. The proposed framework combines a weighted centroidal Voronoi tessellation-based formation strategy, defined on a spherical surface and parameterized by sensor noise variances, with a Weighted Least Squares estimator to compute the field gradient at the formation center. By explicitly accounting for sensor heterogeneity in both formation design and estimation, the method achieves robust gradient estimation under noisy measurements. In particular, we show analytically that this construction is nearly optimal. The covariance of the gradient estimate is derived in closed form, providing a lower bound on the attainable estimation variance for any formation on the sphere, and the proposed tessellation is shown to asymptotically satisfy the conditions under which this bound is attained. The estimated gradient is then exploited within a gradient-ascent strategy to guide the team toward the source location. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to alternative strategies and highlight its intrinsic ability to reconfigure online in response to robot failures, thereby enhancing its adaptability.

items.title: Transmit Coefficients and Receive Combining Vector Design for OTA-FL with Imperfect CSI
items.summary: Over-the-air (OTA) computation has recently gained significant attentions as an effective approach to enhance the communication efficiency of wireless federated learning (FL). By enabling simultaneous transmission and aggregation of local model updates, OTA-FL can substantially reduce both latency and bandwidth consumption. However, a key challenge lies in the imperfect aggregation of global models caused by channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, which introduces distortion to the final learning performance. To address this issue, we study the long-term mean squared error (MSE) minimization problem for OTA-FL under imperfect CSI conditions. Through convergence analysis, we establish an upper bound for the time-averaged MSE, thereby revealing the effect of aggregation errors accumulated throughout multiple communication rounds on the overall training performances. Based on this analysis, an optimization framework is developed to minimize the long-term MSE via the joint design of (i) transmit coefficients at the local devices and (ii) receive combining vectors at the parameter server (PS). Since this alternating optimization approach requires non-causal CSI, a Lyapunov-based optimization method is further introduced to handle causal CSI scenarios. By incorporating virtual queues to characterize long-term energy consumption, the proposed method effectively decouples temporal dependencies and allows transmit coefficients to be optimized based on the causal CSI of each aggregation round. Comprehensive evaluations on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets have demonstrated that the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the degradation of test accuracy caused by imperfect CSI. Comparisons with other benchmark schemes further verify the superiority of our proposed algorithms.

items.title: Jamming-Resilient OTFS-NOMA
items.summary: In this paper we propose a jamming-resilient sparse delay-Doppler NOMA scheme for OTFS and derive closed-form BER expressions from a Marchenko--Pastur conditioning argument on random unitary submatrices, in contrast to the well-known partial-band error floor of conventional OTFS-NOMA. The resulting bound is Hadamard-DFT-Haar invariant and remains valid under compromise of the shared randomization seed. A superincreasing power allocation brings low-complexity per-bin SIC up to the maximum-likelihood detector on the composite constellation, and a pairwise cluster rule scales the design beyond four users. Compared against a fair-baseline, the proposed scheme is the only configuration without a jammer-induced error floor and gives a ~6dB horizontal SNR gain at BER~=10^{-2}.

items.title: A superposition approach for the ISS Lyapunov-Krasovskii theorem with pointwise dissipation
items.summary: For nonlinear time-delay systems, we show that the existence of a Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) with pointwise dissipation (i.e., dissipation in terms of the current solution norm) suffices for input-to-state stability, provided that uniform global stability can also be ensured using the same LKF. To this end, we employ elements of a recently developed stability theory in which the behavior of solutions is not assessed through the classical norm but rather through a specific LKF. As a consequence of our results, we obtain a strengthening and extension of the classical Lyapunov-Krasovskii theorem for undisturbed systems to systems with uniformly bounded disturbances. We discuss the advantages of our approach by means of an example.

items.title: A Re-Keying Game for Encrypted Multi-Agent Control under Persistent Threats
items.summary: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) lets a coordinator control a fleet on encrypted states, but CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic, returns noisy decryptions from which an adversary can recover the secret key. Flooding each decryption with noise defends it, but a fleet must decrypt to act, so the count of decryptions grows every cycle while the loop tolerates only bounded noise. We formulate the choice of flooding and key lifetime as a leader-follower game between the fleet operator and an advanced persistent threat that listens first and then spoofs the agents' sensors. We show that the closed loop decides how long a key may be used: the formation's specification caps each key's decryption budget through the loop's $H_2$ norm, and only re-keying, not bootstrapping, renews it. A spoof consumes part of the specification that flooding needs, and the coordination graph and the cost of an alarm decide in closed form whether the scan alone, a lower flood or nothing deters it. On 196 agents escorting a convoy at 128-bit security, five graphs with the same spectral radius differ 18-fold in key lifetime, a lower flood deters the spoofer on the torus for a twentieth of a key a day, and on the ring it cuts the damage 7 times. More broadly, any system that must repeatedly decrypt to act has a key lifetime set by its tolerance to noise, making key management part of control design.

items.title: Sada-ASR: A Production Multidialectal Arabic Speech Recognition System
items.summary: Callers to Arabic customer-service lines speak their own dialect, while speech recognizers are built and evaluated mainly on Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). A recognizer that mishears the dialect breaks the call before anything else can help. We present Sada-ASR, the speech recognizer of EchoNova's production Arabic voice agent. On a 120-hour test set of MSA and eight dialects, it has the lowest word and character error rates of twelve systems, against eleven from Microsoft, ElevenLabs, Google, OpenAI, Speechmatics, IFM, Cohere, NVIDIA and Audar: 11.69% word error rate against 13.51% for the strongest, Microsoft's MAI-Transcribe-2 (a lead of 0.74 points on clips unaffected by that system's fixed number and script conventions), and 15.52% against 16.96% averaged over varieties. Its largest margins are on Omani (4.30 points), Egyptian (3.78) and Saudi (2.19) speech; it is level on Syrian and loses on Lebanese (24.96% against 23.05%), mostly because it writes Lebanese words in MSA forms and is less verbatim. On six public test sets its average word error rate under the leaderboard's current scoring is 17.17%, below every published figure we found, among them Falcon-ASR (20.92%), Jais-ASR (22.85%) and Audar-ASR-V1-Turbo (23.17%), though none of these states that it used that scoring, so the comparison is indicative. We describe the data pipeline and methodology behind Sada-ASR and release a 20-hour subset of the test set with our scoring code.

items.title: Leveraging Dual-Process Theory for Multimodal Multiparty Turn-Taking Prediction
items.summary: In multiparty conversations, a pause does not always mean a speaker has finished, and another voice does not necessarily indicate a change in who holds the conversational floor. Reliable turn-taking therefore requires recognising not only whether a speaker is ready to yield the floor, but also when a possible transition deserves attention. We propose a dual-process-inspired framework that separates continuous candidate discovery from selective verification. A fast, recall-oriented stage identifies plausible transition points. In contrast, a deliberative stage combines acoustic, linguistic, speaker-related, and predicted future-activity evidence, together with multimodal cues where available, to reject false candidates and refine transition timing. We evaluate the framework through three distinct tasks: SHIFT/HOLD classification at supplied decision points, verification of automatically generated candidates, and continuous discovery and localisation of floor transfers. On VoxConverse, we derive action-aware turn-taking events from speaker-diarization annotations to examine unconstrained conversations with varying numbers of speakers. Multi-TPC provides complementary evaluation of controlled triadic interactions using speech, gaze, motion, and prosodic information. The findings reveal that identifying plausible transitions is considerably easier than reliably confirming and localising genuine floor transfers, while the contribution of individual evidence sources varies across conversational settings. These results highlight the importance of treating multiparty turn-taking as a continuous discovery-and-verification problem rather than classification at predefined boundaries.

items.title: UACS: Uncertainty-Aware Clustering and Sparse Parameter Estimation for Multi-Condition Wheel Center Force
items.summary: Accurate wheel center force (WCF) estimation is important for vehicle durability analysis and condition monitoring, whereas direct measurement requires dedicated transducers and increases instrumentation cost and complexity. As a result, soft sensors have attracted considerable attention as a practical alternative. However, developing reliable soft sensors remains challenging due to varying working conditions, unknown condition relationships, and high-dimensional model representations. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware clustering and sparse parameter estimation framework (UACS) for WCF signal estimation under diverse and unlabeled working conditions. A MISO-FIR model is first constructed using easily accessible sensor signals to estimate the unmeasurable force signal. The uncertainty of estimated parameters is quantified through confidence ellipsoids, and pairwise hypothesis testing is developed to identify statistically similar working conditions. Based on these uncertainty-aware comparisons, working conditions are grouped in an unsupervised manner, and sparse parameter estimation is performed within each cluster. The UACS framework simultaneously reduces the number of required models and active parameters while maintaining estimation accuracy. Experiments using real-world vehicle data demonstrate that the UACS framework achieves estimation accuracy comparable to condition-specific models while substantially reducing the number of required models and outperforming conventional distance-based clustering approaches.

items.title: A convex approach for Markov chain estimation from aggregate data via inverse optimal transport
items.summary: We address the problem of identifying the dynamical law governing the evolution of a population of indistinguishable particles, when only aggregate distributions at successive times are observed. Assuming a Markovian evolution on a discrete state space, the task reduces to estimating the underlying transition probability matrix from distributional data. We formulate this inverse problem within the framework of entropic optimal transport, as a joint optimization over the transition matrix and the transport plans connecting successive distributions. This formulation results in a convex optimization problem, and we propose an efficient iterative algorithm based on the entropic proximal method. We illustrate the accuracy and convergence of the method in two numerical setups, considering estimation from independent snapshots and estimation from a time series of aggregate observations, respectively.

items.title: Representing Differential Inclusions as Monads: A Framework for Compositional Controller Synthesis
items.summary: Sequential composition of safety-certified controllers for hybrid and non-smooth robotic systems is well studied piecewise. Yet no existing framework reduces this question to a single algebraic condition. We construct a \emph{trajectory monad} for Filippov-regular differential inclusions. Its Kleisli category treats controllers as morphisms and sequential execution as trajectory concatenation. Control Barrier Function (CBF) certification, a guarantee of forward invariance, corresponds to a sub-monad of this category. Joint safety of composed controllers then follows from one algebraic condition. All controllers must land in a common sub-monad, which is closed under the monad multiplication. The sub-monad condition recasts recasts existing CBF composition practice categorically. It explains why a smooth intersection of multiple barriers supports safe composition, while enforcing barriers phase by phase does not. For the phase-by-phase case, we derive a closed-form Bernoulli model of the failure rate. We validate it over a randomized sweep of 3{,}000 instances. The same sweep shows that the standard baseline degrades under constraint conflict as the barrier count grows. This baseline enforces all barriers simultaneously as constraints in a single quadratic program (QP). We instantiate the framework on a four-mode piecewise-affine system and on a unicycle reduced-order model over heterogeneous terrain.

items.title: Successive Convexification in Learned World Models for Safe Offline Planning
items.summary: World models learned from offline data allow an agent to plan without further interaction with the environment, but the sampling-based planners used with them handle safety constraints only by scoring or rejecting sampled action sequences. We instead pose safe planning in the latent space of a learned world model as a successive convex program (SCP), in which a learned discrete-time control barrier function is imposed as a constraint at every step of the horizon. SCP requires smooth dynamics, so we build the networks from smoothed MaxMin activations and spectrally normalised layers, and bound the resulting linearisation error in terms of the Lipschitz bound and the smoothing width. As SCP is a local method, we start it from a sampled plan. On two Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks with offline data, this planner has fewer violations than MPPI and CEM drawing 128 times as many samples at equal wall-clock time in our main comparison, though not significantly, and earns greater return at longer horizons, and is much safer than SCP without a sampled start. SCP converged more often on Lipschitz-bounded models. Unlike sampling, it also reports at each step whether its plan is a feasible, first-order optimal KKT point of the planning problem in the model, or that no feasible plan was found nearby. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/scwm.

items.title: DyTransRM: A Unified Simulation-to-Real Framework for Dynamic Radio Map Prediction
items.summary: Dynamic radio map (RM) prediction enables proactive wireless network control by forecasting future propagation conditions from historical observations. However, collecting temporally continuous and spatially dense real-world RMs is prohibitively expensive, while models trained on large-scale simulated data often suffer from limited transferability to real environments. To address this issue, we propose DyTransRM, a unified simulation-to-real framework for dynamic RM prediction under sparse real-world measurements. DyTransRM first introduces RadioCLIP to learn physics-semantic representations by aligning environmental evolution with the corresponding propagation evolution, thereby improving both prediction accuracy and cross-domain transferability. To further bridge the simulation-to-real gap, SparseUOT employs sparse-mask simulation refinement to mimic realistic measurement patterns and unbalanced optimal transport to selectively align compatible propagation representations across domains. Experiments on RadioMapMotion and real-world datasets demonstrate that RadioCLIP achieves an NMSE of 0.0018 and an RMSE of 0.012 in simulation-domain prediction. After sparse real-domain adaptation, DyTransRM achieves an NMSE of 0.023, RMSE of 0.079, and MAE of 0.064, outperforming representative adaptation baselines without requiring spatially complete real RMs. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DyTransRM for transferring simulation-learned dynamic propagation knowledge to practical sparse-measurement scenarios.

items.title: Hydrogen in Practice: A Global Review of Demonstration Projects from Production to Integration
items.summary: Hydrogen technology has the potential to address various challenges related to integrating low- and zero-carbon energy sources, as well as achieving carbon neutrality. It provides valuable solutions for transitioning to net-zero emission energy systems on a global scale. The implementation of hydrogen production and integration demonstration projects has received significant attention around the world and strong support from governments, highlighting the crucial role of such initiatives in the advancement of hydrogen energy. However, research in this area remains limited, particularly in terms of comprehensive and systematic reviews of industrial practices under real-world conditions. To bridge this gap, this article provides an in-depth review of hydrogen production, storage, and industrial applications, summarizing key features of thirteen exemplary hydrogen demonstration projects from around the world. The goal is to offer insights and guidance for the large-scale deployment of hydrogen energy while identifying potential technological pathways for the future.

items.title: Fault Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Operation Strategy for Triple-Port Hydrogen Production System
items.summary: The multi-port converter offers significant advantages in sustainable energy-based hydrogen production, such as high energy density and wide application potential. As the core energy hub in these systems, the multi-port hydrogen converter demands high reliability. However, its numerous switches and complex operation increase the risk of failure. Currently, there are no effective fault diagnosis or fault tolerance solutions for these systems. Current fault diagnosis methods for two-port and multi-port converters rely on many sensors, have low accuracy, and cannot handle multi-switch faults. Additionally, existing fault tolerance strategies fall short in maintaining stable power for the electrolyzer and do not allow capacity sharing among ports. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method for open-circuit faults in a triple-port hydrogen converter and a corresponding fault-tolerant operating strategy. By optimizing a random forest algorithm with a sparrow search algorithm, high-precision multi-switch fault diagnosis is achieved using only three current sensors. Fault-tolerant operation of the system is achieved through an auxiliary switch after a failure. Additionally, power sharing between output ports can be realized. This ensures the efficient and stable operation of the hydrogen production system. The effectiveness of this solution has been validated through simulations and experiments.

items.title: Switching Structure and Finite-Event Optima for One-Orbit Minimum-Fuel In-Plane HCW Maneuvers
items.summary: Under in-plane Hill$\unicode{x2013}$Clohessy$\unicode{x2013}$Wiltshire dynamics with independently bounded radial and along-track thrust, we prove that every target reachable within one orbit has a fixed-time minimum-fuel control with at most ten switches. We first show that regular optima have at most four radial and six along-track switches, coupled through a shared costate. Of the 35 candidate count pairs, 11 require minimum durations, one cannot be optimal, and 23 are attainable at arbitrarily short durations. We then convert singular-arc optima into bang/off optima with at most five switches by preserving terminal moments. We demonstrate terminal accuracy and whole-arc Pontryagin consistency through 55,296 numerical transfers.

items.title: Optimal Coordination of Multiple Ancillary Service Provisions in Active Distribution Networks
items.summary: We propose a multi-rate model predictive control (MPC) framework for coordinating primary frequency control (PFC), automatic generation control (AGC), and voltage control (VC) in active distribution networks. The framework allocates distributed energy resource (DER) flexibility among these three ancillary services while retaining their different update rates. To account for the intertemporal flexibility of electric vehicle aggregations and aggregations of buildings with thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs), we incorporate time-varying power-energy envelopes into our multi-rate MPC formulation. These constraints couple the combined PFC and AGC response to the demand-side flexibility available later in the prediction horizon. Furthermore, the input-multirate structure enables coordinated ancillary service provision by DERs with different response dynamics. The controller optimizes the three services together, allowing fast regulation to be coordinated with the developing slow response within the available DER flexibility. We demonstrate the coordinated provision of the three ancillary services through closed-loop simulations on a modified IEEE 33-bus system using a nonlinear differential-algebraic model.

items.title: Detecting Small Space Objects for Space Situational Awareness with Collaborative Edge AI
items.summary: With the rapid growth of space activities, near-Earth space is becoming increasingly congested, leading to a higher risk of spacecraft collisions and space debris generation. Recent close-proximity encounters and collision incidents necessitate efficient and cost-effective onboard systems for space object detection (SOD) and collision avoidance. While deep learning (DL) enabled Edge AI using low-cost vision sensors on single or multiple satellites has shown promises for SOD, significant challenges remain, including limited datasets, small SOD, and the lack of comprehensive performance assessments. This paper presents a collaborative Edge AI framework for multiview SOD and systematically benchmarks DL models and fusion strategies. Results show that higher image resolution significantly improves small SOD. For multiple views, image-level fusion reduces the combined communication and inference latency by 30.13% and 32.80% on average compared with feature-level and attention-based fusion across the evaluated inter-satellite link (ISL) bandwidth. For larger view sets, feature-level and attention-based fusion achieve better detection accuracy at the cost of analysis in the sensing-communication pipeline, revealing that multiview collaboration introduces minimal latency overhead under ISL constraints when reception capacity is not exceeded. Our work provides valuable design insights for future collaborative satellite network design, supporting the emerging space situational awareness and space traffic management requirements.

items.title: Pixel-KWS: Rendered-Glyph Representations for Orthographically Robust Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting
items.summary: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting (KWS) allows users to enroll arbitrary keywords at inference time. However, character and phoneme-based text encoders rely on fixed symbol vocabularies learned during training, limiting their ability to handle unseen or visually similar symbols such as homoglyphs, l33tspeak substitutions, and accented characters. We propose PIXEL-KWS, an open-vocabulary KWS framework that represents characters through rendered glyphs rather than learned embedding lookups. We render each character as a grayscale image and encode it with a lightweight CNN, enabling the text encoder to generalize from visual form rather than a fixed vocabulary. On LibriPhrase, PIXEL-KWS and its matched character-based counterpart achieve 9.57% and 9.55% EER on LibriPhrase-hard, 0.43% and 0.41% EER on LibriPhrase-easy, outperforming all published baselines without pre-training or synthetic data. PIXEL-KWS provides substantially greater robustness to both homoglyph and l33tspeak symbol-level perturbations. These results highlight glyph-based representations as a simple and effective approach for robust open-vocabulary KWS in practical settings.

items.title: CausalGloss: Multi-Evidence Action Control for a Simultaneous Mandarin Speech-to-ASL Gloss Cascade
items.summary: Simultaneous Mandarin speech-to-American Sign Language (ASL) gloss translation requires deciding when an evolving utterance supports committing each gloss. Fixed Wait-k cannot adapt to source-gloss reordering, while training only on reference histories causes exposure bias. We present CausalGloss, an English-prefix-to-ASL-gloss action policy for a Mandarin-speech cascade. It combines lexical and semantic evidence, bounded delay, negation constraints, burst WRITE actions, and incomplete-history recovery. On a frozen 500-example How2Sign-derived benchmark with weak LLM-generated references, CausalGloss improves the fixed Wait-k frontier and nearly matches a three-seed TransLLaMA-style learned adaptive baseline at k = 5 in Token F1 (0.7047 versus 0.7067), with 54.4% lower LAAL. Against CLERC Epee human-gloss references, it achieves 0.649 Token F1 and Pareto-dominates three-seed TransLLaMA-style k = 5 and fixed k = 5, 7, reducing LAAL by 58.2-69.9%. Ablations separate timing from retention. A synthetic Mandarin-speech cascade preserves a smaller computation-aware latency gain, although outputs remain over-long. We also construct ChineseSpeech-ASLGloss-v1, a 19,924-utterance, 36.54-h controlled evaluation corpus.

items.title: Enforcing Ellipsoidal Constraints in Neural Networks with a Polynomial Safety Layer
items.summary: Often the output of a learned mapping must satisfy prescribed constraints. In the control of autonomous systems, for example, the chosen action must keep the system within a collision-free region. We consider the case in which a proposed output is corrected by projection onto a safety ellipsoid. Computing this projection amounts to solving a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). We construct a neural-network safety layer by unrolling a feasibility-preserving polynomial penalty iteration. The unrolled structure allows the loss gradient to propagate from the feasible output through the safety layer to the network parameters during training. We show how to choose the layer parameters so that every iterate is feasible and give a computable bound on its distance to the exact projection at any prescribed depth. We illustrate the method by training a LiDAR-based policy to control an unmanned aerial vehicle. A privileged model predictive control expert uses the map and the measured vehicle state to generate the training data. In the simulated narrow mazes, the filtered policy avoided wall contact at every tested stage of training, including at initialization, when every unfiltered flight hit a wall. A representative build of the learned policy and its safety layer for an Arm Cortex-M4F microcontroller occupies about 36 KiB of flash, with a RAM budget below 5 KiB.

items.title: XLSAR-Bench: Towards Extremely Large SAR Imagery Understanding of MLLMs
items.summary: The rapid development of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) has highlighted the need for comprehensive benchmarks to assess their capabilities and limitations in remote sensing (RS). However, evaluating MLLMs in large-size synthetic aperture radar (SAR) scenarios remains challenging, as understanding complete scenes requires both global semantic interpretation and fine-grained target perception. Existing SAR benchmarks predominantly rely on small image patches, limiting their ability to assess these capabilities jointly. To address these limitations, we present XLSAR-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating the perception and reasoning capabilities of MLLMs in large-scene SAR imagery. XLSAR-Bench comprises 405 images with an average size of 7153$\times$7153 pixels, ten tasks spanning visual question answering, visual grounding, and detailed image captioning, with all evaluation samples meticulously annotated manually, assisted by a semi-automatic captioner. Experimental results from general-purpose and domain-specific MLLMs reveal persistent challenges in understanding large SAR scenes and accurately perceiving small targets. We have open-sourced XLSAR-Bench to support further research in developing more powerful MLLMs for complete large SAR scenes.

items.title: A Simulation Framework with Guaranteed Error Bounds for Safety and Fuel-Efficiency Analysis of Vehicle Platoons
items.summary: Vehicle platooning is an important technology in modern transportation systems, offering significant improvements in highway traffic efficiency and fuel economy. Achieving coordinated behavior among vehicles in a platoon depends on wireless communication. However, packet losses in wireless communication can create critical safety issues when they occur together with sudden braking. In this paper, we propose a rigorous simulation-based method for studying such safety issues by analyzing the minimum inter-vehicle distance over time across control parameters that guarantee string stability.
